Sparrow is the wine bar and lounge from the Good Salt group, with chef Wendy Lopez cooking southern European small plates: silky mushroom pate, jamon iberico with melon, short rib ragu over rigatoni, and a tomato gimlet that wakes the whole palate up. The wine list leans Old World with New World charm, and Thursday vinyl nights give the room its pulse. It is a grown-up evening in the best sense, intimate, unhurried, and just a little romantic.

places.name: Stasio's Italian Deli
places.address: Stasio's Italian Deli and Market, 210 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803-6024
places.description: On the corner of Bumby and Robinson sits the kind of Italian deli that turns lunch into a small celebration. Stasio's piles its signature sandwich high with prosciutto, hot capicola, soppressata, and fresh mozzarella on house-baked bread, and the chicken parm sub has its own devoted following. Come for a morning sfogliatelle filled with orange-scented ricotta and a proper espresso, then browse the market shelves for imported pastas and pantry goods on the way out. Regulars and first-timers get the same warm bustle. This is the Milk District's little Italy, and it earns every bit of its love.

places.name: Still Lounge by Dre and Snoop
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The second branded lounge from Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg lives inside Live! at the Pointe Orlando, and it carries itself exactly like you would expect: dark wood, leather couches, golden light, and a soundtrack of hip-hop, R&B, and soul from a rotating cast of DJs and live performers. The bar is built around the duo's Still G.I.N., poured into signatures like the Platinum Negroni, the lavender-honey Bee's Knees, and the bourbon-based OG-OF. It is upscale without being uptight, the kind of room where the night feels curated. Sip slow, stay late, and let the beat do the rest.

places.name: Sushi Saint
places.address: 400 Pittman St Ste A, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: From Michelin-starred chef Michael Collantes, the mind behind Soseki, comes the fun sibling: a temaki handroll bar where chefs build cone-shaped handrolls right in front of you. The original Creative Village room earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its obsessive sourcing, tuna with scallion and wasabi, snow crab with truffle and finger lime, A5 wagyu with truffle mushroom jam. There is a lounge for cocktails, a 12-seat omakase for the devoted, and a newer Icon Park outpost for the I-Drive crowd. It is high-end sushi served with lounge energy, and it never takes itself too seriously.

places.name: Taverna Opa
places.address: International Drive
places.description: Dinner here is a party you accidentally joined, and you will not want to leave. Taverna Opa on International Drive starts the night as a classic Greek taverna, whitewashed walls, saganaki flaming tableside, wood-fired lamb chops, fresh Mediterranean seafood, and a mezze spread made for the whole table. Then the belly dancer appears, the Zorba line dance pulls you in, and a confetti of napkins rains over everything. As the night deepens, a live DJ takes over and the room turns into a full celebration. Bring your loudest friends. Or become one.

places.name: Ten Ten Seafood Grill
places.address: Ten Ten Seafood & Grill, 5600 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32808-7614
places.description: On West Colonial, inside a grand dining room with big round tables and lazy Susans, Ten Ten runs one of the city's most serious Cantonese operations. The dim sum carts roll out until mid-afternoon: har gow, siu mai, shrimp and chive dumplings, all made fresh daily. Later in the day the room turns to live seafood, with a daily ginger and scallion lobster special that regulars build their whole week around. It has the banquet-hall joy of a family celebration. Come with a crowd, share everything, and do not skip the carts.

places.name: Thai House
places.address: Thai House, 2117 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4834
places.description: Look for the red building with the green roof on East Colonial: inside is Thai House of Orlando, a Mills 50 fixture that keeps its cooking close to the Thai original. The room is small and cozy, the kind of place where regulars barely glance at the menu. The pad panang is rich and comforting, the duck soup has a loyal following, and the curries carry real depth. Locals have defended this place for years against every newcomer, and the food keeps justifying the loyalty. End with the fried banana and ice cream. You will understand.

places.name: The Beacham & The Social
places.address: The Social, 46 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2419
places.description: A century-old vaudeville theater on Orange Avenue, still doing what it has done since 1921: giving Orlando a place to lose itself in the music. The Beacham went from vaudeville acts to a movie house to the city's defining concert hall and nightclub, and its stage has hosted everyone from Devo and The Police to Soundgarden, Pink, and Lauryn Hill. National tours fill the floor, and late on weekends it turns into a full nightclub. There is history in these walls and bass in the floorboards. Stand up front once in your life. It will spoil other rooms for you.

places.name: The Boathouse & Vintage Amphicars
places.address: Disney Springs
places.description: Every good Disney Springs dinner wants a waterfront, and The Boathouse owns the best one. The raw bar and the steaks both earned their reputations honestly, and the deck at golden hour is the kind of view that slows your table down. But here's the move: book the captain-guided Amphicar tour. It's the only place in the world where a vintage 1960s amphibious car splashes straight off the dock and carries you around the lake.

places.name: The Glass Knife
places.address: The Glass Knife, 276 Orlando Ave S, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Walk in and look at the walls: antique glass cake knives, the unlikely 1920s invention that gave this place its name. The Glass Knife is a French cafe that grew up in Florida, and everything here shows intention. The creme brulee donut, made from 24-hour buttermilk brioche, has a following of its own, and the coffee is Onyx, exclusively, pulled fresh every time. Weekend brunch is full table service; weekdays you order at the counter and linger on the covered patio.

places.name: The Majesty Building ("The I-4 Eyesore")
places.address: 123 E Central Pkwy, Altamonte Springs, FL 32701
places.description: Every Orlando commuter knows it: the half-finished 18-story tower looming over I-4 in Altamonte Springs, construction underway since 2001 and somehow never done. The Majesty Building is the pet project of religious broadcaster Claud Bowers of SuperChannel 55, built donation by donation, debt-free, at a pace that made it a local legend, a Jeopardy clue, and the punchline of a thousand commute jokes. Somehow it turned 25 years in progress. Gawk at it on your drive, ask any local, and watch their face. It is the most beloved eyesore in Florida.

places.name: The Moderne
places.address: Mills 50
places.description: Mills 50's most glamorous room doubles as its most thoughtful kitchen. The Moderne is an Art Deco cocktail lounge with gold accents and sculptural curves, where chef-owner Michael Nguyen builds a bar program around deconstructed classics: smoked old fashioneds poured tableside, theatrical garnishes, drinks with names like Woman in White. The food follows the same logic, tapas-style plates that range from Korean vodka pasta to duck wontons and miso cream noodles, drawing on the whole of Mills 50's heritage. It is the kind of room where a date night feels like an occasion and the cocktails arrive with a ceremony.

places.name: The Monroe
places.address: The Monroe, 448 N Terry Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1894
places.description: The Good Salt group's fourth concept lives on the ground floor of the Julian apartments in Creative Village, and it calls itself a diverse social gathering place with the menu to back it up. The Monroe leans into nostalgic childhood favorites in an airy midcentury room: famous fried chicken, playful bites like pork belly s'mores and jalapeno popper deviled eggs, and a coffee bar by day that turns cocktail bar by night. Next door, the Front Porch overlooks Luminary Green Park. It is the rare room equally good for a working lunch, a long happy hour, or a lingering dinner.

places.name: The Pinery
places.address: The Pinery, 295 NE Ivanhoe Blvd, Orlando, FL 32804-6434
places.description: Right on Lake Ivanhoe, The Pinery is Ivanhoe Village's love letter to its own past, named for the pineapple farms that once grew where the condos stand. Owner Carol Holladay runs a warm, lake-view dining room built on Southern hospitality and chef-driven Florida cooking: smoked peanut soup, a bread board with pimento cheese, broiled blue crab dip, and shrimp and grits that taste like the season they were made in. The patio catches the water breeze, the cocktails lean tropical, and the whole room glows. Dinner with a view, done the Ivanhoe way.

places.name: The Ravenous Pig & Brewing Co.
places.address: 565 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Ask a Winter Park local where to eat and watch their face change when they say this name. Husband-and-wife chefs James and Julie Petrakis turned a warm, butcher-shop-beautiful gastropub into the restaurant that taught Orlando to take its own food seriously. The pig board alone is worth crossing town for, the shrimp 'n grits taste like the Gulf showing off, and the room hums with the particular joy of a place that has never phoned it in.

places.name: The Reverie
places.address: Hannibal Square, Winter Park, FL
places.description: The most anticipated opening of Winter Park's year lives in the space Chez Vincent called home for 28 years. At 533 W New England Ave in Hannibal Square, The Reverie is the new American brasserie from two-time James Beard nominee Brandon McGlamery, the chef behind Luma on Park and Prato. The promise is refined yet approachable cooking with French and European roots: classic technique meeting ingredient-driven dishes that stay grounded and craveable, classic cocktails with seasonal twists, and a thoughtful list spanning New and Old World wines. Winter Park is holding its breath.

places.name: The Social
places.address: 54 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On North Orange Avenue, The Social is the small brick-walled room where indie music in Orlando has been baptized for years. Death Cab for Cutie, FKA Twigs, and Anthony Green all played this stage before the world caught on, and local bands still measure themselves by whether they have earned a set here. It is intimate by design: shoulder-to-shoulder crowds, a busy bar, and that particular electricity of seeing a band up close enough to lock eyes with. Catch an act here first, then tell everyone you were there.

places.name: The Strand
places.address: 807 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The "New Old" is the whole idea here, and The Strand wears it beautifully: classic American cooking rethought with real craft, inside a mid-century dining room on Mills 50 that feels pulled from a warmer decade. Seasonal plates made from scratch, a menu that turns over with the market, and a daily chef's special that rewards regulars. Slide into a long booth, order something you could never make at home, and let the vintage glow do the rest. This is the neighborhood bistro every neighborhood wishes it had.

places.name: The Toothsome Chocolate Emporium & Savory Feast Kitchen
places.address: The Toothsome Chocolate Emporium & Savory Feast Kitchen, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-7611
places.description: You walk in and the factory swallows you whole. Brass, gears, towering chocolate-colored smokestacks, and one wild idea behind everything: chocolate belongs in every course. Start with the warm Chocolate Almond Bread, rich with salted caramel, then the Marshmallow Crisp milkshake, unapologetic and impossible to finish with dignity. Watch for Professor Doctor Penelope Tibeaux-Tinker Toothsome and Jacques, her robot sidekick, wandering the room like they own the place.

places.name: The Vanguard
places.address: The Vanguard, 578 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1341
places.description: Set inside the historic Firestone Tire Building on Orange Avenue, The Vanguard is the biggest independently owned concert room in Central Florida, and it carries itself that way. The sound system hits you in the chest, the lasers paint the ceiling, and the crowd on the floor moves like one body. From heavyweight EDM nights to touring bands and the EDC downtown takeovers, this is where Orlando goes when it wants to feel the music properly. Check the calendar before you plan anything else.

places.name: Tierra
places.address: Baldwin Park, Orlando, FL 32814
places.description: Baldwin Park has quietly become one of Orlando's most serious Japanese corridors, and Tierra adds another reason to make the trip. Expect the clean lines and calm focus of a proper Japanese kitchen: precise knife work, rice that matters, and fish treated with reverence. In a neighborhood built for evening strolls around Lake Baldwin, a focused Japanese room like this is exactly the dinner that makes the whole outing feel complete. Let the omakase instinct take over and trust the chef.

places.name: Tori Tori
places.address: 720 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Low lights, stiff drinks, and charcoal smoke: Tori Tori is Mills 50's love letter to the Japanese izakaya, and chef Sonny Nguyen runs it like Tokyo would want it run. Yakitori skewers come off the binchotan with real fire character, the blue crab and corn croquettes are the plate you will dream about, and the highballs are poured with conviction. Walk-in only, so the crowd is part of the theater. Come hungry, stay late, share everything.

places.name: Turci Pasta
places.address: Turci Pasta, 2120 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Watching fresh pasta get rolled through the pasta window at Turci Pasta is half the magic of dinner here. College Park's little Italian jewel makes everything by hand, every day: purple sweet potato gnocchi, black truffle ravioli, pear ravioli poached in wine, lasagna that tastes like someone's grandmother still runs the kitchen. Cozy, romantic, the kind of room where dates and anniversaries feel inevitable. Order the cannoli at the end and thank me later.

places.name: UniGirl
places.address: Mills 50, Orlando
places.description: Orlando's first dedicated onigiri shop, tucked inside Mills Market, and named for chef William Shen's shiba inu, Uni. These warm rice triangles are the real thing: lightly salted koshihikari rice, crisp nori, fillings like crispy fried chicken thigh, tuna sharpened with mustard, and unagi glazed in sweet sauce. They sell out, so the line moves fast and the menu keeps moving too. A Michelin Bib Gourmand for a food-hall stall tells you everything. Grab a few and a bottled drink, eat them warm.

places.name: Universal Epic Universe
places.address: 1001 Epic Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The first major theme park to open in Orlando in 25 years, and it shows in every square foot. Five worlds wait behind the portals: Celestial Park's celestial gardens, the Ministry of Magic's wizarding streets, Super Nintendo World's playable chaos, the Isle of Berk soaring with dragons, and Dark Universe where the classic monsters live. This is immersion at a scale the industry has never attempted, and a full day barely scratches it. Plan like it's a destination, because now it is one.

faqs.q: How many days do you need for Epic Universe?
faqs.a: Plan at least 2 days. Rope-drop or buy Express Pass. Consensus best rides: Harry Potter and the Battle at the Ministry, and Monsters Unchained. Power-Up Bands for Super Nintendo World run ~$45.

places.name: Universal Helios Grand Hotel
places.address: 8505 S Kirkman Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Dinner inside a theme park rarely feels this grown-up. The Universal Helios Grand Hotel rises right out of Epic Universe's Celestial Park, and its dining program leans full Mediterranean romance. Flora Taverna serves comfort cooking in a light, airy room with an open kitchen and al fresco tables overlooking the park's fountains, while Bar Helios, the rooftop lounge, pours craft cocktails and tapas against a sweeping panorama of the entire universe below. Even if you're not staying over, this is a destination meal in its own right.

places.name: Universal Studios Florida
places.address: Universal
places.description: The original, opened in 1990, and still the park where movie magic feels personal. Slip through the brick wall into Diagon Alley and the wizarding world opens up around you, butterbeer in hand. Revenge of the Mummy throws you backward into ancient curses, E.T. still pedals through the night sky like it's 1982, and Springfield's Krustyland keeps the whole family laughing. Eight lands, endless nostalgia, and a lagoon-side movie-parade finale. This is the park that started Orlando's movie rivalry.

places.name: Universal's Islands of Adventure
places.address: Universal's Islands of Adventure, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: If the Studios is about the movies, Islands of Adventure is about the adventure. Eight themed islands ring a central lagoon, each one a fully realized world: Hogsmeade's snow-dusted rooftops beneath Hogwarts, where Hagrid's motorbike ride has ruined every other coaster for its riders; Marvel Super Hero Island's screaming Hulk launch; the VelociCoaster's raptor hunt through Jurassic jungle. Then you drift into Seuss Landing's whimsy with the kids. This park rewards wanderers: every island has its own weather, its own story.

places.name: Victoria & Albert's
places.address: Victoria & Albert's, Grand Floridian, Orlando, FL 32830
places.description: Inside Disney's Grand Floridian, behind a formal dress code and a hushed dining room, sits the most decorated restaurant in the Southeast. Victoria & Albert's has held AAA's Five Diamond award since 2000 and earned a Michelin star, the first for any Disney-owned restaurant. Course after course of seasonal American cooking arrives with ceremony: personalized menus, tableside flourishes, a coffee service people talk about for years. Book months ahead, dress the part, and give the evening the reverence it deserves.

places.name: Voodoo Doughnut
places.address: Voodoo Doughnut, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Portland's cult doughnut empire landed at CityWalk with all its glorious weirdness intact. The Voodoo Doll, pierced with a pretzel stake and bleeding raspberry jelly, the Bacon Maple Bar that sounds wrong and tastes like genius, fifty-plus varieties sold in those famous pink boxes. Watch the decorators work their magic at the counter, take the obligatory throne photo, and don't sleep on the vegan lineup. Good things come in pink boxes, and they're worth the line.

places.name: WA Sushi
places.address: Wa Sushi, 924 Semoran Blvd, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: Don't let the strip-plaza address fool you: WA Sushi is one of those places Orlando sushi people whisper about. Chef Hong sources fish flown in from Japan, and the Grand Nigiri Moriawase shows it off piece by piece: bluefin toro, yellowback sea bream, heart clam, sweet shrimp, each one pristine. The room is cozy and unpretentious, the presentation is quietly beautiful, and the matcha tiramisu ends things on a fusion note worth saving room for. This is a destination for people who take raw fish seriously.

places.name: Walter's Tavern
places.address: 2105 N Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Game day finally has a proper home in the Packing District. Walter's Tavern, named for citrus heir Walter Simmons Phillips, sits inside the historic Great Southern Box Company food hall with fifteen-plus screens and a massive video wall so every seat is the good seat. The cocktail program is genuinely serious, all fresh-juiced with nothing pre-mixed, plus a house Orange Lager brewed for the room. Best part: order pizza, wings, or a birria crunchwrap from any hall vendor straight to your table without missing a play.

places.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
places.address: 1800 Wekiwa Cir, Apopka, FL 32712
places.description: You think you know Orlando until you slide into water this blue. Wekiwa Springs is Orange County's longest-running tourist attraction, and it earns the title: emerald springs feeding the Wekiva River, a spring vent that has drawn swimmers since the mid-19th century, and tropical hammocks dense enough to lose yourself in. Paddle past pickerelweed blooms, watch the wildlife do its unbothered thing, and stay for the miles of trails. This is the Florida that existed before the theme parks, and it is still showing off.

places.name: White Wolf Cafe
places.address: White Wolf Cafe, 1829 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: This is Ivanhoe Village's morning ritual. White Wolf does Southern comfort the way it should be done: the Crab Cakes Benedict that regulars dream about, French toast worth the trip alone, and a cinnamon bun famous across the neighborhood. Cheese grits, home fries, country fried chicken, the whole honest lineup. The room is art-filled and warm, the staff treats you like a neighbor, and brunch here feels like the day already started right.

places.name: Will's Pub & Lil Indie's
places.address: Mills 50
places.description: If Orlando's underground has an address, it is 1042 North Mills. Will's Pub is the room where punk, metal, post-punk and emo bills pack the floor shoulder to shoulder, and where your new favorite band might be opening. In the second room, Lil Indie's keeps it late and loose: funk DJs, jazz improv, folk strings, often no cover. Two rooms, one block, zero pretension. Come curious, leave converted.

places.name: Wine Bar George
places.address: 1610 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: George Miliotes, one of a few hundred Master Sommeliers on the planet, built his wine bar like a winemaker's own estate in the middle of Disney Springs, and the whole place glows with his obsession. More than 200 wines pour by the glass, the bottle, or the ounce, so you can taste a legendary vintage without committing to the bottle. Small plates, charcuterie, family style feasts: everything on the table feels chosen for what is in your glass. Wine education without the snobbery.

places.name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour
places.address: 312 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: There is no better introduction to Winter Park than a seat on one of these little pontoon boats. Since 1938, the Scenic Boat Tour has been gliding through the chain of lakes and the narrow man-made canals that stitch them together, past Rollins College and waterfront mansions with real stories in their bones. Your skipper narrates the whole hour, and the ride has a way of slowing your breathing down. Bring your out-of-town guests here first. It reframes everything else.

places.name: Woody's Lunch Box
places.address: Woody's Lunch Box, 351 Studio Dr S, Orlando, FL 32830
places.description: Andy's lunch box, flipped on its side and propped open with his thermos, is the best quick bite in Toy Story Land. The menu plays with pure childhood nostalgia done right: Totchos, the legendary tater-tot nachos buried under chili and cheese; a BBQ Brisket Melt on garlic-butter sourdough; and Lunch Box Tarts in rotating seasonal flavors. Green Army Men keep watch while you eat like a toy. Mobile-order ahead, grab a table, and remember that soda floats taste better at toy scale.

places.name: Zaru
places.address: Zaru, 1114 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4636
places.description: A woven bamboo basket gives this place its name, and it tells you everything about the philosophy: simple tools, obsessive craft. The Tung brothers built Zaru around Sanuki-style udon made from flour milled in Kagawa, the birthplace of udon, with equipment shipped from Japan. You fill out your own interactive menu, hot or cold noodles, then watch the kitchen build broths of real smokiness and depth around add-ons like ikura onsen or crispy shrimp tempura. A Michelin Bib Gourmand for a 25-seat noodle room. Slurp loudly, it's appreciated.

places.name: Zeytin Turkish Cuisine
places.address: Zeytin Turkish Cuisine, 4439 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-1229
places.description: A family-run Turkish room on Edgewater Drive where everything, down to the produce, is prepared from scratch and every meat is halal. Start with the pillowy lavash and a tray of dips, move on to Iskender kebab or lamb doner pide, and save room for the knafeh, baked to order with shredded wheat, sweet cheese, and pistachios. Chef Z and his wife Michele run the kind of place that makes regulars out of first-timers. Cozy, lantern-lit, and reservation only, so plan ahead.

places.name: Ômo by Jônt
places.address: Omo by Jont, 115 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4311
places.description: Sixteen seats, three rooms, one Michelin star: Ômo by Jônt is Winter Park's most theatrical fine-dining experience. The evening unfolds as a journey, from the Salon for welcome drinks, to the chef's counter facing the open kitchen, to a pastry parlor for dessert. French technique meets Japanese soul in courses like snow crab chawanmushi crowned with kaluga caviar and uni, and a hazelnut kakigori that tastes like a Ferrero Rocher dreamed in shaved ice. This is the anniversary, the milestone, the night you'll retell.

places.name: June
places.address: 700 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Thornton Park's dreamy modern Mexican room, where the interior feels like golden hour never ended. June cooks wood-fired contemporary Mexican and Yucatecan food with a clean conscience: no seed oils, minimal refined sugars, and a menu built for sharing. Anchor the table with chicken al pastor and esquites, work through tostadas topped with lobster or wagyu, and don't skip the cornbread with agave butter. The cocktails, watermelon tequila and peppery experiments, are as considered as the food. A Michelin Guide nod confirms what the room already told you.

places.name: Mamazzita Gastrobar
places.address: 1949 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Mamazzita calls itself an "exotic Latin soul restaurant lounge," and the soul is the selling point. By day it's a chic Latin-fusion gastrobar on Sand Lake Road: Ceviche Erotismo, pulpo a la brasa, lomo saltado, a wagyu burger, plus a full sushi menu for the adventurous. When the sun drops, the DJs take over and it becomes a full nightlife scene with hookah, dancing, and serious cocktail energy. Two moods, one address: come for dinner, stay because the night decided otherwise.

places.name: Kai Kai BBQ & Dumplings
places.address: Mills Market, 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Dim sum means "touch the heart," and Kai Kai takes that literally. Husband-and-wife team Jerry and Jackie Lau brought 35 years of Cantonese cooking from New York's Chinatown to Mills Market, and the proof hangs in the meat case: glistening roast duck, crackling crispy pork, honey-glazed char siu sold by the pound or piled into rice boxes. The roast duck bao is the move, and the handmade dumplings come off the steamer fresh all day. Michelin Guide recognized, food-hall casual. The line moves fast; your patience won't be tested for long.

places.name: Kappo Sushi
places.address: 11815 Glass House Lane, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Kappo means "cut and cook," and this intimate O-Town West dining room lives up to it: chefs preparing seasonal, ingredient-driven dishes right before your eyes, knife work and fire and plating in real time. The 15-course omakase at the sushi bar runs from delicate raw preparations to warm composed dishes to precision nigiri. The six-seat counter is the full experience, but even à la carte at the bar carries the same calm focus. Now led by Michelin-starred chef Stone Lin as Kappo Sushi, it's one of Orlando's most serene special-occasion rooms.

places.name: Sushi Izuki
places.address: 8685 Fenton St, O-Town West, Orlando, FL
places.description: Eight seats, one chef, eighteen courses: Sushi Izuki is Chef Leo's declaration on omakase. The menu is never printed; it's spoken, decided that morning from whatever arrived fresh, and it never repeats. Whole fish dry-aged in house, cut to order, served with deliberate, restless creativity drawn from Japan and the West. Add a private tatami room for a second, even more intimate way in. Two seatings an evening, reservations on Resy. If you want to taste a chef chasing a Michelin star in real time, this is the room.

places.name: Moon Wok Kitchen & Lounge
places.address: 11701 International Dr Ste 300, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: International Drive has plenty of Chinese food, but nothing quite like Moon Wok's moonlit lounge. The room is extravagant in a warm way, all glowing details and lounge energy, and the kitchen backs it up: handcrafted dim sum, Cantonese-style roast duck and crispy pork, wok-fired beef ho fun, and a General Tso's that balances sweet and heat better than it should. The signature cocktails lean Asian-influenced too. Date night, group dinner, post-SeaWorld splurge: it handles all of them with ease.

places.name: Mochiry
places.address: 20 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: That first bite of a mochi doughnut is the whole argument: chewy, stretchy, nothing like the doughnuts you grew up with. Mochiry's downtown shop on South Orange serves Korean-style mochi doughnuts in the classic bubble-ring shape with glazes and toppings that rotate through the seasons, plus boba teas and specialty coffees to wash them down. Korean corn dogs and ramen round out the savory side. Simple, fast counter service for workers, students, and anyone who believes dessert is a legitimate food group. You will be back for the texture alone.

places.name: Beef Bae
places.address: 10249 S John Young Pkwy Ste 109, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: Beef Bae is where Orlando's halal community goes for real American barbecue. Zabiha halal brisket, fall-off-the-bone ribs, beef short ribs with the smoke dialed in, plus a peri-peri-style Portuguese chicken that regulars swear by. The Inferno Burger brings the heat, the hot chicken brings the crunch, and a mango lassi cools everything down. South Orlando's answer to anyone who thought halal and barbecue couldn't share a smoker: they absolutely can, and this place proves it nightly.

places.name: Pierogi One
places.address: 8865 Commodity Cir, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Poland's national dish finally has a proper Orlando home. Co-owners Iwona Wawer and Pawel Redestowicz opened Pierogi One with one goal: pierogi like grandma made. Fourteen-plus varieties cover the classics, mushroom-sauerkraut and potato, and the surprises, spicy beef, bacon cheddar, Philly cheesesteak, even blueberry and vanilla cheese dessert pierogi served boiled. Pan-fried savories come with bacon and onions. Add kielbasa, red borscht, potato pancakes, and a Polish platter for the table. Comfort food with genuine heritage behind it.

places.name: Taffer's Tavern
places.address: Pointe Orlando, 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Jon Taffer of Bar Rescue put his first Florida tavern inside Pointe Orlando, and the room splits the difference he is known for: old-world tavern warmth up front, a tightly run modern kitchen and bar behind it. The menu is elevated pub food — a Bourbon Burger, slow-braised short rib, French onion soup, pork belly skewers — and the cocktails lean on his browned butter bourbon, including one called the Campfire. On an I-Drive lined with chains, it reads as a tavern that happens to have a television name on the door.

places.name: Great Southern Box Co. Food Hall & Bar
places.address: The Great Southern Box Company, 2105 N Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: A 1930s citrus crate warehouse, restored to celebrate the immigrant cuisine that makes Orlando delicious. The Great Southern Box Company food hall anchors the Packing District with a vendor lineup built on conviction: Antica's Neapolitan pizza, voted best in town; Fui Yo's birria tacos with real consommé; Kayos Jamaican jerk and oxtail; Braza's Brazilian steakhouse; Kabab 2 Go's Lebanese shawarma; Bangkok-style Thai street food; A Lo Cubano's pressed sandwiches. Order at the counters, get a text when it's ready, and drink at the central bar or Walter's Tavern inside. Free garage parking, bring the whole crew.

places.name: Austin's Coffee
places.address: 2240 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL
places.description: Two decades of Orlando's weirdest, warmest creative scene poured into coffee cups. Austin's Coffee is a Winter Park institution: a bohemian café where the beans are roasted in-house, one pound at a time, and every night the room turns into open mics, live music, comedy, and poetry. After 25 years at its original Fairbanks corner, the community rallied, and it reopened at 2240 W Fairbanks with the same soul intact. Artists, night owls, and first-timers all get the same welcome. Coffee strong enough to keep up with the room.

places.name: Eggdose
places.address: 12615 W Colonial Dr, Winter Garden, FL
places.description: Born at the farmers markets, crowned by the breakfast crowds, now a proper brick-and-mortar in Winter Garden. Eggdose keeps one philosophy: breakfast should be simple, fresh, and satisfying. The egg sandwiches are the star, made exactly how you want them on fresh bread with quality eggs. The Maple Dose is the legend: a French toast bun, thick-cut bacon, soft-scrambled eggs, cheddar, powdered sugar, maple syrup on the side. The picanha steak sandwich brings the savory muscle. Show up hungry, leave plotting your next visit.

places.name: CFS Coffee
places.address: CFS Coffee, 430 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4230
places.description: Coffee for the Soul wears its Colombian heart openly. This neighborhood café pours properly crafted espresso drinks, try the dulce de leche latte, alongside a full kitchen doing Colombian breakfast burritos, acai bowls, waffle BLTs, and bakery cases worth lingering over. The Winter Garden room is cozy inside and out, built for regulars: laptop workers, morning regulars, families easing into the day. With breakfast through dinner on the menu, it's less a coffee stop and more a daily ritual waiting to happen.

places.name: SEO Basilico Pizzeria
places.address: Stoneybrook Exchange, Winter Garden, FL
places.description: Seo Basilico brings the true taste of Italy to Winter Garden, and takes the "artigianale" part seriously. This is artisan Neapolitan pizza the way the old country intends: dough fermented with patience, a blistered leopard-spotted crust, fresh basil and proper fior di latte. Dinner-only service keeps it focused and intimate, the kind of neighborhood pizzeria where the oven is the theater. Pair a classic margherita with a glass of wine and a lazy evening, and let Naples come to you.

places.name: Play Street Museum
places.address: Stoneybrook Exchange, Winter Garden, FL
places.description: A tiny town built for kids eight and under, right in Winter Garden. Play Street Museum is an interactive children's museum where little ones run a doctor's office, staff a fire station, rescue pets, make ice cream cones, and learn recycling through pure play. Ninety-minute sessions keep the energy fresh, with daily enrichment themes and add-ons like the slime lab and paint-your-own pottery. First-time local owners run it with obvious love. The birthday-party destination of choice for west Orange County parents.

places.name: Arte Museum
places.address: ICON Park, 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Coming to ICON Park in 2027, and worth marking the calendar for. Arte Museum is the internationally celebrated immersive digital art experience from Korean design powerhouse d'strict, whose locations in Las Vegas, New York, Dubai, and Seoul have drawn over ten million visitors. Thirty thousand square feet of floor-to-ceiling galleries: towering waterfalls, glowing floral fields, tranquil forests, and aurora skies, all brought alive with projection mapping, enveloping soundscapes, and custom scents. Every room invites you to step inside the art, not just look at it. Orlando's version gets all-new works made for Central Florida.

places.name: Category 10
places.address: Universal CityWalk, Orlando, FL
places.description: Luke Combs is bringing a hurricane to CityWalk. Category 10, named for his eight-times-platinum hit "Hurricane," is set to open in late 2027 as a 33,000-square-foot, three-story country music palace at Universal Orlando. Live country music, free line dancing, Carolina-style food honoring Combs' North Carolina roots, and experiential spaces inspired by his songs. It's the third location after Nashville and Las Vegas, and the first built with a theme-park crowd in mind. Break out the boots.

places.name: Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift
places.address: Universal Studios Florida, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: The next great Orlando coaster is already climbing steel. Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift arrives in 2027 at Universal Studios Florida, replacing the retired Rip Ride Rockit with something entirely wilder: outdoor coaster cars that rotate a full 360 degrees to simulate drifting, and a 170-foot vertical spike that launches riders nearly seventeen stories over the edge of CityWalk. The much-criticized Supercharged closed in 2026 to clear the way. Universal is betting the franchise on pure, high-speed, sideways-throwing thrills.

places.name: Tropical Americas
places.address: Disney's Animal Kingdom, 2901 Osceola Pkwy, Orlando, FL
places.description: Animal Kingdom's biggest transformation in decades is rising where DinoLand once stood. Tropical Americas, opening in fall 2027, recreates the lush, biodiverse world of northern South America and Central America in an 11-acre village called Pueblo Esperanza, the Village of Hope. Headliners: Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent, a brand-new expedition into a Mayan temple with groundbreaking animatronics; Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto, the first Encanto ride ever, inside the magical Casita on the day Antonio receives his gift; plus a hand-carved animals carousel and a massive new quick-service hacienda. The wait will be worth it.

places.name: Disney Lakeshore Lodge
places.address: Near Disney's Fort Wilderness Resort, Orlando, FL
places.description: Disney's newest resort opens July 1, 2027, on the shores of Bay Lake between Wilderness Lodge and Fort Wilderness, and it's built around the nature Disney animators have loved for decades. Nine hundred-plus rooms and freestanding Lake Houses draw from Bambi, Pocahontas, Brother Bear, Encanto, and Fantasia. The lobby centers on floor-to-ceiling lake views, a glowing fiber-optic river, and a blown-glass canopy of hundreds of leaves. A lazy river, multiple pools, water-taxi access to Magic Kingdom, and lounges positioned for fireworks views. The tranquil base camp for your park days.

places.name: Diadem Pickleball Complex
places.address: 14748 W Colonial Dr, Winter Garden, FL
places.description: Pickleball's boom gets its Winter Garden cathedral here. Diadem Pickleball Complex is converting a 35,000-plus-square-foot industrial building on West Colonial into a premier indoor pickleball destination: world-class courts, expert coaching, leagues, weekend intro clinics for newcomers, and DUPR-rated tournaments with real prize money. Whether you're learning your first dink or chasing cash in Moneyball divisions, the facility is built for every level. Refuel between matches with food and drinks on site. This is where west Orange County's fastest-growing sport lives.

places.name: Jiang's Kitchen (Mills 50)
places.address: 1111 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Restaurateur Eric Jiang, the chef behind the acclaimed Sushi Izuki omakase, turned his focus to the noodle shop he grew up dreaming about. The Mills 50 Jiang's Kitchen is built around handcrafted noodles and dumplings, with an open kitchen where you watch noodles get stretched and pulled and soup dumplings folded by hand. Expect regional Chinese specialties like biang biang noodles, dan dan noodles, and wontons in chili oil, plus beer, wine, sake, and bubble teas. Across from Mills Market on East Colonial, this is noodle theater at its most delicious.

places.name: Cosa Nostra Italian Deli (Winter Garden)
places.address: Downtown Winter Garden (exact address TBA)
places.description: The family-run Italian deli that built its name in Clermont is crossing into downtown Winter Garden, taking over the beloved former Writer's Block Bookstore space on Plant Street. Cosa Nostra does made-to-order Italian sandwiches the proper way: the Super Tuscany stacks prosciutto di Parma, salami, mortadella, and fresh mozzarella with pesto and roasted peppers; the Muffaletta Nostra is a tower of Italian meats, cheeses, and giardiniera. Fresh pastas, specialty coffees, and imported Italian groceries round it out. Neighborhood-style hospitality, premium ingredients, zero pretension.

places.name: Boca Kitchen Bar Market
places.address: 358 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Local. Simple. Honest. That is the whole philosophy printed on the wall, and Boca actually lives it. This farm-to-table kitchen on Park Avenue builds a hand-crafted menu around what Florida farms deliver that day, with proven favorites holding court alongside daily specials for the adventurous. The sweet potato gnocchi tastes like autumn decided to move to Central Florida, the flatbreads arrive crackling from the oven, and the bar pours cocktails with real care. Tables are arranged to pull people into conversation, so you will linger longer than you planned.

places.name: Bosphorous Turkish Cuisine
places.address: 108 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The hollow lavas bread arrives puffed and blistered straight from the oven, and tearing into it tells you everything about this place. Bosphorous is family owned, and the family cooks like it: smoky lamb adana, tender shanks, meze spreads built for sharing. Some nights there is live Turkish music, guitar and kanoun drifting over the dining room, and it turns dinner into something that feels like travel. Finish with the kunefe, crackling cheese soaked in syrup. Afiyet olsun indeed.

places.name: Pannullo's Italian Restaurant
places.address: 216 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Ask a Park Avenue regular where the neighborhood still eats like family and Pannullo's comes up fast. More than three decades on the same stretch of sidewalk, this Tuscan-styled room overlooks Central Park and wears it proudly, right down to their old motto: the only thing they overlook is the Park. Plates are generous and old-school, from lobster ravioli to chicken marsala, and Chef Pannullo's fresh cheesecake has its own quiet following. Comfortable, unpretentious, and completely sure of itself.

places.name: The Chapman
places.address: 500 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The Chapman feels like Winter Park finally got the restaurant it kept deserving. Warm, artful, and unmistakably local, this Park Avenue dining room runs a scratch kitchen built on Florida ingredients, with a service culture that treats every table like it matters. Start with the pull-apart rolls and whipped seasoned butter, settle into the glow of the room, and let the evening stretch. It has the polish of a special-occasion spot and the soul of a neighborhood favorite, which is a rare combination.

places.name: Atlantic Beer & Oyster
places.address: 358 N Park Ave Ste B, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Winter Park's own oyster bar, tucked into a hidden garden just off Park Avenue. Atlantic Beer & Oyster keeps it gloriously unpretentious: briny Gulf Coast oysters, peel-and-eat shrimp, smoked fish dip that regulars swear by, and a ceviche with real snap. Beer comes in cans and on draft only, because as they like to say, you can't bring bottles on the boat. Grab the pet-friendly patio, crack open something cold, and let the afternoon take its sweet time.

places.name: The Alfond Inn
places.address: 300 E New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: This is the only hotel in America that doubles as an art museum extension, and you feel it the moment you walk in. Owned by Rollins College, The Alfond Inn surrounds you with the Alfond Collection of Contemporary Art, and every stay quietly funds student scholarships, which makes the luxury feel like it stands for something. The new spa wing, the cabana-framed pool terrace, Hamilton's Kitchen downstairs: everything is polished and personal, and it all sits two easy blocks from Park Avenue.

places.name: Casa Feliz Historic Home Museum
places.address: 656 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Casa Feliz is the kind of place that makes preservationists out of ordinary visitors. This Andalusian-style masonry farmhouse, with its original Spanish roof tiles and century-old whitewashed brick, sits under sweeping oaks on Park Avenue and feels like a small piece of Spain dropped into Florida. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, it opens its doors for tours and its Music at the Casa concert series, where live performances fill rooms that were built for gathering. Come for the architecture, stay for the feeling.

places.name: Albin Polasek Museum & Sculpture Gardens
places.address: 633 Osceola Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The story of this place is almost as moving as the sculpture. Czech-born Albin Polasek spent 30 years leading sculpture at the Art Institute of Chicago, then retired to Winter Park at 70, where a stroke took half his body. It did not stop him: he devised a way to keep carving with an assistant holding the chisel. Half of his known works are here, set among lush gardens on the shore of Lake Osceola. The view alone justifies the trip, and the art does the rest.

places.name: Mead Botanical Garden
places.address: 1300 S Denning Dr, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Forty-eight acres of green, and admission does not cost a thing. Mead Botanical Garden is Winter Park's wilder, quieter side: shaded nature trails winding past ponds and streams, butterfly gardens alive with color, and birding walks that reward an early arrival. It feels like the city let this place stay gloriously untamed. Pack a picnic, wear your repellent, and give yourself a couple of unhurried hours. Locals treat it as their reset button, and it works like one.

places.name: Winter Park History Museum
places.address: 200 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: It is only fitting that the museum telling Winter Park's story lives in a former railroad freight depot, because the tracks literally built this town. The Winter Park History Museum packs 5,000 artifacts into a cozy, volunteer-loved space: vintage postcards, area railroads, military and school relics, and exhibits like the celebrated trains-of-Winter-Park show. Best of all, it anchors a free self-guided walking tour of twenty historic sites. Small, passionate, and completely worth your time.

places.name: Oak & Stone
places.address: 310 Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Here is the fun one: a tap wall with dozens of craft beers and wines that you pour yourself, at your own pace, tasting as you go. Oak & Stone pairs that playfulness with stone-fired pizzas built on dough made with triple-filtered water and a 36-hour ferment, so the crust has real character underneath toppings like the buffalo-chicken "winger." It is a classic American tavern sharpened into something sharper: laid-back, buzzing, and great for groups. Pour a little, pour a pint. The wall is calling.

places.name: Nigel's Bananas
places.address: 334 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL
places.description: There is always money in the banana stand, and this one is heading for Park Avenue. Nigel's Bananas began when a chef had a dream about his late father, Nigel, telling him bananas would matter in his life, and turned it into chocolate-dipped frozen bananas cloaked in Belgian chocolate and loaded with toppings. Toasted coconut and caramel, cookies and cream, marshmallow drizzle, the whole joyful menu. A family-owned Florida treat born in Seaside is coming to Winter Park, and the line will be worth standing in.

places.name: Rusteak
places.address: 101 S Eola Dr, Suite 103, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On the corner of Lake Eola, RusTeak is that rare neighborhood spot that cooks like it has something to prove. Executive Chef Maelo Cotto's chef-driven New American menu runs from honey-sage pecan chicken to a pepper-crusted NY strip, with brunch standouts like crab cake benedict that people order on repeat. The patio hums, the cocktails have personality (try the smoked watermelon margarita), and live music turns dinner into a night. Polished but never stiff, it feels like Thornton Park at its best.

places.name: The Guesthouse
places.address: 1321 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The Guesthouse is a Mills 50 bar that feels like someone's very stylish, plant-filled living room. Greenery trails across white walls, sunlight floods through big windows early and candlelight softens it late. The bartenders build classic cocktails with real conviction: a margarita that people call the best in the city, a proper old fashioned, an army navy that regulars swear by. Pair it with a wine list deeper than you would expect from a corner bar. Loud, laughing, and full of locals, this is the neighborhood at its warmest.

places.name: Fixtion Restaurant & Bar
places.address: 15 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Fixtion calls itself Orlando's newest secret, and it lives up to the name by shape-shifting through the day. Come at lunch for comfort food with personality, the Wall Street turkey club, a chimichurri skirt steak, an espresso martini that regulars name as the best downtown. Stay for game day with a 200-inch LED screen and fourteen TVs pulling every eye. Then watch it turn after dark into a full nightclub with bottle service and DJs. One address, three identities, and all of them committed.

places.name: Wall Street Plaza
places.address: 25 Wall St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: This is not one venue. It is eight of them sharing one legendary block, and on a Saturday night the whole street belongs to the party. Wall Street Plaza has been the beating heart of downtown Orlando since 1995: the Cantina pouring the famous house margarita, Rodeo spinning country, intimate corners like the Hen House, concert stages that pull real crowds. Eight venues, one location, and you never have to leave. Come hungry, come ready to move, and let the block decide where your night goes.

places.name: Iron Cow
places.address: 2438 E Robinson St, Suite A, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Only in the Milk District could a sushi spot double as one of the city's serious electronic music rooms. By day, Iron Cow is a hi-fi sushi restaurant with great sound and great rolls. By night, the decks take over: trance nights with international DJs, drum and bass tour stops, house music till late. It is the perfect Milk District contradiction, dinner and dancing under one roof, and the crowd is here for both the food and the frequencies. Check what is on before you go.

places.name: Baires Grill
places.address: 8050 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: This is Argentina, done properly, right off International Drive. Baires Grill builds everything around the parrilla: hand-cut steaks, sizzling provoleta, the mixed Parrilla Criolla loaded with sausage, blood sausage, picanha and asado de tira. Start with fried empanadas and end with flan drowned in dulce de leche, and in between let them pour you a proper Malbec. Passionate about great food and good times is their whole pitch, and you will taste it in every cut.

places.name: Evermore Orlando Resort
places.address: 1590 Evermore Way, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: There is a beach in Orlando, and it has eight acres of crystal-clear water surrounded by twenty acres of white sand. Evermore Bay is the centerpiece of this reimagined Grand Cypress resort, where you can rent houses and flats big enough for the whole family tree, or check into the AAA Five Diamond Conrad Orlando. Golfers get two Jack Nicklaus courses, sunset cruises glide out on classic Chris-Craft boats, and thirteen dining venues keep everyone fed. Landlocked Florida, meeting the Caribbean, right outside Disney's gates.

places.name: Orlando International Premium Outlets
places.address: 4951 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At the north end of International Drive, this open-air outlet village is where designers meet discounts in a big way. Wander shaded walkways past luxury names, athletic giants, and the kind of stores where you walk in for one thing and leave with five. This is the outlet pilgrims plan trips around: arrive early, wear comfortable shoes, and work the Guest Services booths for extra coupons before you start. A full afternoon here feels less like shopping and more like sport.

places.name: Black Hammock Restaurant
places.address: 2316 Black Hammock Fish Camp Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: This is Old Florida, unapologetic and wonderful. The Black Hammock sits on Lake Jesup, home of one of the largest alligator populations in the state, and the restaurant leans all the way in: famous gator bites, gator tacos, fried gator tail, catfish done right. Before you eat, ride an airboat across the lake with an experienced captain, then say hello to Hammy, the 12-foot resident gator at the free wildlife exhibit. Lakeside bar, weekend live music, and a thrilling, only-in-Florida kind of afternoon.

places.name: Poke Hana
places.address: 1225A E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Poke Hana sits at the heart of one of Orlando's greatest foodie neighborhoods, and it knows exactly what it is doing. This Hawaiian spot serves poke bowls with tuna so fresh that regulars call it the best outside a top-tier sushi counter, marinated in house sauces and piled with seaweed salad, pickled cucumber, and edamame. Do not skip the crispy rice tacos, all crunch and flavor, or the Huli chicken plate. Bright, casual, quick, and endlessly customizable. The kind of lunch spot that quietly becomes a habit.

places.name: Rise Southern Biscuits & Righteous Chicken - Winter Park
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave Ste 6, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Rise is a biscuit joint, and it treats the biscuit with the reverence it deserves. They call them the best dang biscuits, and the first bite of a hot honey butter chicken biscuit makes a strong case. The menu is pure Southern joy: juicy fried chicken, a fried green tomato with pimento that people dream about, a glazed blueberry biscuit for the sweet finish. Morning hours, counter energy, and comfort food that punches way above its weight. Winter Park mornings just got better.

places.name: Lazy Moon Pizza
places.address: 11551 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: A slice bigger than your head. That is the Lazy Moon promise, and generations of UCF students have tested it. This divey, sticker-plastered institution has been slinging 30-inch pies and massive by-the-slice wedges near campus since 2004, with flavors you will not find anywhere else: the Cuban, the mustard-based El Fidel, the buffalo-chicken Buff. Craft beer, late nights, and a whole lot of napkins. It is not pretty, and it never needed to be. Eat, drink, and be lazy.

places.name: Dutch Bros Coffee
places.address: 116 S Semoran Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Dutch Bros runs on a simple idea: coffee should come with a shot of pure optimism. The drive-thru on Semoran is all high-fives and speed, with broistas who genuinely seem happy to see you and a menu that rewards the adventurous. The Golden Eagle, caramel and vanilla breve with a caramel drizzle, is the cult favorite, but the real move is inventing your own from dozens of flavors. Blended freezes, Rebel energy drinks, lemonades: this is your morning, your way, with extra pep.

places.name: Hinckley's Fancy Meats
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr #104, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Chef Matt Hinckley cures, smokes, and ages his way into legend at this Audubon Park butcher shop inside East End Market. The charcuterie earned a nod from the New York Times, the bacon was called the best in Florida, and the sandwiches put all of it between bread: a rare Florida porchetta stacked with salsa piccante and broccoli rabe, a proper pastrami on rye, a banh mi with real nerve. Nose-to-tail, transparently sourced, unapologetically meaty. Carnivores, this is your cathedral.

places.name: Agave Azul Winter Springs
places.address: 5248 Red Bug Lake Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: Agave Azul calls itself highly stylized with high energy, and it delivers on both. This family-owned Mexican kitchen in Winter Springs runs hot: birria tacos and birria brisket that people drive across town for, chipotle tequila shrimp, guacamole made fresh and worth every bite. The bar keeps pace with spicy margaritas and a strong pour. It is festive without being cheesy, authentic without being fussy. Bring your appetite and a few friends. This is a celebration spot that earns the noise.

places.name: Fiddler's Green Irish Pub & Eatery
places.address: 544 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: This is the real thing: a dark-wooded, cozy-as-they-come Irish pub on Fairbanks where the Guinness is poured the patient way and the live music fills the room. Fiddler's Green serves the kind of food that makes expats nod approvingly, from beer-battered fish and chips to a shepherd's pie people call the best in Orlando. Trivia nights, Sunday sessions, a patio that welcomes the dog, and bread pudding to finish. One regular said a pint and live music here is the perfect Sunday night, and they are right.

places.name: The Porch Winter Park
places.address: 643 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: True to its name, The Porch starts with an actual front porch you can lounge on while you wait for a table. Inside, this garage-converted sports bar does American comfort with real appetite: buttery peel-and-eat Big Reds, a loaded Big Texas BLT, wings with serious kick. Big screens for game day, live music to keep the night moving, and brunch drink specials that locals plan around. It is loud, easy, and genuinely fun, the kind of place where the whole table ends up staying for one more.

places.name: The Wine Room on Park Avenue
places.address: 270 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Here is wine tasting with the intimidation completely removed. You load a Tasting Card and pour yourself tastes from over 150 hand-selected wines around the world, an ounce to a full glass, exploring at your own pace. The Wine Room has been doing this on Park Avenue since 2006, part bar and part shop, with a former bank vault downstairs that makes a killer backdrop. Add cheese and charcuterie, flatbreads like the pear and brie, and occasional live music. Date night, done perfectly.

places.name: The Imperial on Park
places.address: 136 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The Imperial's pitch is simple: help bring the fun back to Park Avenue. And it is working. This warm, laid-back neighborhood restaurant and bar pours boutique wines, craft beers, and cocktails built on local spirits from Winter Park Distillery, while Executive Chef Drew Weisner's kitchen sends out a blackened grouper sandwich people rave about, smoked salmon crostinis, and truffle fries. Live music plays Thursday through Sunday. Relaxed, full of character, run by people with heart: the low-key Park Avenue spot you wish you had found sooner.

places.name: Park Avenue Pizza
places.address: 119 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Park Avenue has its own pizzeria, and it keeps things beautifully simple. Everything here is made from scratch, the slices are generously sized, and even a plain cheese slice carries that proper New York-style flavor. Buffalo chicken pizza and calzones, cold subs, and the kind of friendly counter service that remembers your face. This is the pie you order when the whole crew is coming over, and nobody will be disappointed. Winter Park's everyday slice, done right.

places.name: Power House Cafe
places.address: 111 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: In the Park Avenue district, surrounded by white-tablecloth competition, this bright little Mediterranean cafe holds its own with pure freshness. Everything is made daily, and you can taste it: a chicken shawarma wrap with real flame flavor, falafel on pita with lemony tahini, silky baba ganoush. The real-fruit smoothies have a devoted following, especially the Good Karma and the mango Margo. Light woods, bustling energy, and food that leaves you feeling genuinely good. The healthy lunch spot Winter Park actually loves.

places.name: Lale Mediterranean Cuisine
places.address: 521 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Taste tradition, taste the Mediterranean: that is Lale's invitation, and the kitchen backs it up. This cozy Park Avenue spot cooks authentic Turkish food from traditional recipes, and regulars keep coming back for the juicy kebabs, the pillowy fresh lavash, the lahmacun and pides straight from the oven. The meze spread is built for grazing, the lamb kofte is a standout, and the kunefe arrives warm with syrup and pistachios. Small, warm, and completely sincere. One of those places you find by accident and guard like a secret.

places.name: Pepe's Cantina
places.address: 433 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Pepe's Cantina was born from a simple desire: great food, specialty cocktails, and a genuinely fun night out. It delivers. This modern cantina serves traditional Mexican food from all regions, presented with a refined touch, and the signature tableside guacamole is worth building a whole evening around. The huge outdoor bar and terrace is one of Winter Park's best-kept secrets, birria tacos anchor the taco menu, and daily fresh handmade corn tortillas keep everything honest. Vibrant, generous, and impossible not to enjoy.

places.name: Sixty Vines
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave Ste 12, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Sixty wines on tap. Let that sink in. Sixty Vines brings wine country to Winter Park with a tap wall of pours you can taste by the glass, the carafe, or the bottle, and a menu that loves a gathering: creamy burrata to start, fig and prosciutto pizza, a double cabernet burger for the hearty among you. The greenhouse patio glows, the room is soft-lit and cozy, and portions are built for sharing. Great food, wine, and company creating unforgettable moments is their whole philosophy, and it works.

places.name: Bulla Gastrobar
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave #7, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Bulla does Spain the shareable way, and the whole room feels like it is in on the celebration. This contemporary gastrobar serves made-to-order sangrias and Spanish and Catalan small plates meant for passing around the table: chorizo-stuffed dates wrapped in bacon that regulars call one of the greatest bites they have ever had, patatas bravas, seafood paella, croquetas. The vibe reads casual but polished, and the weekend brunch runs late into the afternoon. Order a spread, order sangria, and let the table get loud.

places.name: Barnie's Coffee & Tea Co.
places.address: 118 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Barnie's has been doing flavor for more than forty years, and their whole identity is built on it: no one does flavor like Barnie's, and the menu proves it. This European-style courtyard cafe on Park Avenue is a Winter Park institution, where the signature Santa's White Christmas latte tastes like the holidays decided to stay. Beyond the famous flavored coffees, there is a real kitchen doing farm-to-table breakfast and lunch, from shakshuka to avocado toast, all served in a hidden courtyard made for lingering. A local legend, still pouring.

places.name: Tibby's New Orleans Kitchen
places.address: 2203 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Tibby's is a full-tilt French Quarter party dropped onto Aloma Avenue. The room bursts with Mardi Gras color, the food comes straight from the Big Easy, and Sunday brunch on Bourbon adds live jazz to the mix. Gumbo that people cross town for, a shrimp po'boy done right, beignets still warm from the fryer, and bread pudding that regulars call the best they have had in years. Order a Sazerac and settle in. This is the happiest room in Winter Park.

places.name: Alma Argentina
places.address: 3607 Aloma Ave Unit 107, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: This family-run Argentine spot on Aloma Avenue is the kind of place locals whisper about and visitors stumble into, then rave about for weeks. The empanadas are the opening act, fried and stuffed with everything from osobuco to three cheeses, and they have a devoted following all their own. Then comes the real show: a full parrillada of perfectly grilled meats, sizzling provoleta, classic milanesa, and desserts like chocotorta and flan with dulce de leche. Warm service, beautiful plating, and the soul of Buenos Aires in Oviedo.

places.name: AVA Mediterranean
places.address: 290 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: AVA is Riviera Dining Group's modern Greek agora on Park Avenue, and it feels like one: part temple to Mediterranean cooking, part gathering place that refuses to be quiet. The kitchen turns out grilled octopus, lobster pasta, and baklava that guests write home about, while the room shifts moods with the day, airy and relaxed at weekend brunch, dim and intimate at dinner, then electric on Friday and Saturday nights when the DJs take over. Come dressed up. This is Winter Park's glamorous side, fully committed.

places.name: Corona Cigar Company & Diamond Crown Lounge
places.address: 127 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Walk in and the scale hits you first: more than two million cigars in stock, brands from over a dozen countries, and rare vintage pre-embargo Cubans behind the glass. The Diamond Crown Lounge is the ultimate cigar experience, done with real theater: Central American decor, authentic Nicaraguan furniture, Latin music in the air, and a spirit selection worth a pilgrimage, from fine Cognacs to prohibition-era whiskies. Cigar makers like Carlito Fuente and the Padrons have rolled through for events. No cover, no membership, just a good attitude and a fine smoke.

places.name: Elixir Kitchen and Bar
places.address: 9 W Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown Orlando has plenty of places to drink, but few that feel like they belong to the neighborhood the way this one does. Tucked into one of downtown's original buildings, Elixir runs a from-scratch gastropub kitchen where the short-rib grilled cheese and chicken and waffles earned their reputations the honest way, one regular at a time. Grab a seat on the patio they call downtown's best-kept secret, order something honest, and stay past sunset when the energy shifts and the night crowd takes over. This is a local's hideaway in every sense.

places.name: Fogo de Chão, Vineland Pointe
places.address: 11543 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Fogo de Chão doesn't do dinner, it stages it. The gaucho chefs arrive at your table with fire-roasted cuts, Picanha with its ember-kissed crust, Fraldinha dripping juice, Filet Mignon that yields without a fight, carving right there in front of you, one slice at a time. The Market Table is a spread of seasonal salads, exotic fruits, and cheese with honey that regulars plan around. Founded in Southern Brazil and built on the centuries-old art of churrasco, this is the kind of meal that makes an ordinary evening feel like an occasion. The Vineland Pointe patio is your calmest seat.

places.name: Oviedo Downtown Area
places.address: 299 Center Lake Ln, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: Forget the strip malls on Mitchell Hammock for an afternoon and point yourself toward Oviedo's old downtown, where the suburb slows down and shows its original face. Brick-faced blocks, the farmers market rhythm, local kitchens and porches instead of chains: this is the part of Oviedo that regulars defend with quiet pride. Wander it, eat at a counter, and notice how a place this close to the highway learned to keep its small-town heartbeat. Come hungry and unhurried.

places.name: QuesaLoco
places.address: 971 W Fairbanks Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: QuesaLoco started as a food truck with lines that wrapped around the block on Friday nights, and now the brick-and-mortar on Fairbanks Ave carries that same joyful chaos. This is birria country: the quesabirria tacos fold beef and cheese into a crisp tortilla built for dunking in rich consommé, and the birria ramen takes that obsession somewhere brand new. Add loco elote on a stick, birria pizza for the undecided, and a menu that reads like a greatest-hits list of Mexican street food. Go expecting noise, flavor, and no regrets.

places.name: The Robinson Cocktail Room
places.address: 63 E Pine St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Three words tell you everything about this Pine Street hideout: Drinks, Dancing, Disco. By day it's a café pouring real espresso and iced lattes, and by night it turns into downtown's most joyful dance floor, where salsa nights and disco sets keep the room moving until late. The drinks match the energy, from a proper espresso martini to the Dancing Queen, and the chili relleno and tamales give you reason to stay past the first round. You don't have to know how to dance. You'll want to anyway.

places.name: Tom's Watch Bar
places.address: 8050 International Dr, Suite 1000, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Some sports bars hang a TV on the wall and call it a day. Tom's Watch Bar builds a cathedral to the game instead: an oversized stadium screen wrapped in hundreds more, 360-degree viewing so every seat feels like the best in the house, and a rooftop perch on International Drive that puts the whole skyline in the picture. The menu goes past the usual playbook, think Korean BBQ wings and Tom's famous prime rib dip, and the virtual Topgolf swing suites keep things moving at halftime. All the sports, all the time, they promise, and the room delivers.

places.name: Disney Springs
places.address: 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: You don't need a park ticket to feel the Disney magic on an evening here. Disney Springs is the resort's open-air promenade, four waterfront neighborhoods stitched together along the water, and it might be the single best free night out in Orlando. The food runs from Morimoto's ramen to The BOATHOUSE's waterfront tables, the bars keep the live music rolling, and you can finish with Ghirardelli ice cream in hand watching the boats glide by. Locals come for date nights and group nights out, and they never pay for admission. It's the Disney glow without the turnstile.

places.name: Orlando Vineland Premium Outlets
places.address: 8200 Vineland Ave, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: This is the one shoppers plan whole trips around. Minutes from Disney, Orlando Vineland Premium Outlets is the city's only luxury outlet run, with Prada, Bottega Veneta, Burberry, Jimmy Choo, kate spade, Tory Burch, and Ferragamo lining the walkways alongside the big-name sportswear and denim staples. It's a true shopping day, not a quick stop: pace yourself, grab something from the food hall between rounds, and don't be shy about the store staff, they know the inventory like treasure hunters. You came here to find the thing.

places.name: O'Shucks Karaoke Bar
places.address: 7467 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Some bars have a karaoke night. O'Shucks has karaoke every single night, a surround-sound setup, and an Orlando Weekly "Best Karaoke Bar in Central Florida" title to prove it does the job. This is the Irish pub on International Drive where tourists and regulars end up sharing the mic, the kind of unpretentious room where a shy first song turns into a table-wide singalong. No kitchen means you can bring your own food in, and Trivia Tuesdays, poker tournaments, and Nickel Beer nights keep the calendar full even when you're not singing. Grab the mic. You'll be glad you did.

places.name: Overlook Park
places.address: 1988 Spring Ave, Oviedo, FL
places.description: Only three acres, but Overlook Park packs a whole Florida postcard into them. The boardwalk stretches out over the south shore of Lake Jesup, where osprey circle overhead and alligators drift past like they own the place, which they do. Mature oaks shade the pavilion and its barbecue grills, the picnic tables sit in that blissful quiet you don't expect this close to the suburbs, and morning light turns the whole lake into a photographer's daydream. Come to fish, to wander the pier, or just to sit still and watch the water do its thing.

places.name: The Grove Bar + Kitchen
places.address: 480 N Orlando Ave C-134, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The Grove takes its name from the vintage Florida citrus groves that once defined this land, and the room wears that heritage warmly: textured, golden, easy to linger in. The kitchen works a modern New American angle, seasonal ingredients, familiar flavors reimagined, comfort that never turns ordinary. Crafted cocktails, the kind made with care rather than haste, anchor the bar, and the whole place is built for the long, happy evening: lunch, dinner, date night, the spontaneous gathering that becomes a favorite memory. Elevated, never stiff. Made for Winter Park Village regulars.

places.name: Jala Indian Cuisine
places.address: 155 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The name means water in Sanskrit, and the cooking here flows the way water does: pure, adaptable, deeply rooted. Founder Manish Nagar brought the traditions of his childhood in Ahmedabad to Winter Park, and it shows in every slow-simmered curry and every tandoor-fired dish that arrives at the table. Tear into the laccha paratha while it's still warm enough to melt on your tongue, work through the tandoori specialties, and save room for the kesar pista kulfi, pistachio and saffron folded into something unforgettable. This is Indian fine dining done with heart, on Morse Blvd.

places.name: Simply Capri
places.address: 114 Ruby Red Place, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Nick Valenti is the man behind Via Napoli at EPCOT and Space 220, so when he built a trattoria at Flamingo Crossings, Orlando took notice. Simply Capri whisks you to the Isle of Capri on sheer atmosphere: sunny Amalfi yellows, Italian servers, and a pizza oven shipped all the way from Naples turning out blistered Neapolitan pies. The house-made pastas sing with Southern Italian soul, try the Scialatielli dei Faraglioni with shrimp, clams, mussels, and calamari, and the Delizia al Limone is the limoncello-spiked finish you'll dream about. The concept is simple, the cooking is not.

places.name: Salt & Ember
places.address: 322 Alexander St, Mount Dora, FL 32757
places.description: Mount Dora's dining scene keeps punching above its weight, and Salt & Ember is the newest reason why. Chef-owner Fred Bisaillon spent three decades cooking through Southern California, Bermuda, the Bahamas, and Nantucket before bringing his wood-fired touch to Alexander Street, and the result is a room that pairs bold flavor with a relaxed, elevated ease. Start with the raw bar, chilled oysters and caviar, then lean into prime steaks or the lobster carbonara that locals already talk about. The tropical patio makes the evening last. Dress up if you feel like it. Nobody minds either way.

places.name: Pio Pio Latin Cuisine
places.address: 2259 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Born in New York City and raised in Orlando, Pio Pio is a husband-and-wife story told in Colombian and Peruvian flavors. The cooking is generous and unapologetic: bandeja paisa piled high, lomo saltado sizzling, rotisserie chicken that regulars swear by, fried yucca made for dragging through the sauces. Sangria keeps the table lively, the fresh juices are the move if you're pacing yourself, and the whole room hums with the kind of warmth you can't manufacture. Their words, not ours: at Pio Pio, we're all family. Come ready to be adopted.

places.name: Caravan Uzbek & Turkish Cuisine
places.address: 8015 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Few Orlando tables take you further from the ordinary than this one. Caravan is a fully halal celebration of two great cuisines, Uzbek and Turkish, served in a warm, family-owned room on South Orange Ave. The To'y Osh rice pilaf arrives fragrant and hearty, the flaky Samsa pastries come out of the tandoor golden and stuffed, and the hand-pulled laghman noodles are a revelation for anyone who thought they'd tried every noodle. Clay-oven bread, perfectly grilled kebabs, honey cake to close. Green tea on the side, and let the evening unspool slowly. This is discovery you can taste.

places.name: Inchin's Bamboo Garden
places.address: 3900 Town Center Blvd, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: Indo-Chinese is one of those fusion cuisines that shouldn't work and absolutely does, and Inchin's Bamboo Garden in Hunter's Creek is where to fall for it. Think Chinese wok fire meeting Indian spice depth: the Chicken Triple Szechwan arrives layered with crunch and heat, the burnt garlic chili fried rice is the plate everyone reaches for, and the hot pot momos land steaming at the table. The Thai yellow curry and Mongolian beef round out a menu built for sharing, and the handcrafted cocktails keep the night going. Saucy, spicy, totally crave-worthy. Bring friends and order too much.

places.name: Sideward Brewing Co.
places.address: 210 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Their tagline says it best: making great beer and being super humble about it. Sideward is a family-owned brewery set inside a renovated hundred-year-old warehouse in the Milk District, twenty taps pouring fifty feet from where the beer was made. The fruit-forward brews are the calling card, think watermelon and dragonfruit wheat, a smoothie Berliner thick with banana, mango, and pineapple, alongside lagers, IPAs, and a honey wine that surprises everyone. The covered patio, full kitchen, and house-made everything make this the kind of place you meant to stop at for one and stayed for the afternoon.

places.name: F&D Cantina
places.address: 617 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Thornton Park's favorite cantina runs on a simple formula: margaritas worth crossing town for, a patio built for lingering, and a happy hour that shows up seven days a week. The birria tacos are the dish regulars won't stop talking about, the watermelon and strawberry basil margaritas are dangerously balanced, and the bacon-wrapped jalapeños are the appetizer move.
