Sundays bring the bottomless brunch that packs the room, and the big tequila selection keeps the bar interesting long after. Festive, vibrant, dog friendly, and right in the heartbeat of South Eola. Bring your people.

places.name: Ice & Bites Cafe
places.address: 3402 Technological Ave Ste 220, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Near UCF there's a little café that treats dessert like a playground, and the students have clearly noticed. Ice & Bites builds its magic around taiyaki, warm fish-shaped waffle cones cradling ice cream in flavors like taro, lavender, green tea, and coffee, finished with toppings you pick yourself. Then there's the Sno, ribbons of shaved ice dressed with fruit and mochi, and the famous affogato cloud: espresso poured over cotton candy until it melts into the ice cream below. Whimsical, cozy, and made for lingering over board games with friends. Bring your sweet tooth and your camera.

places.name: Crepe Delicious
places.address: 55 W Church St, Orlando, FL
places.description: Downtown's little crêperie on Church Street does exactly what its name promises, and then some. The crepes arrive enormous, folded golden and stuffed with everything from Nutella to savory combinations, all built on ingredients cut fresh daily. Go sweet with the Nutellaccino or a house-made gelato, or go all in on the Godzilla: eight scoops, a pile of toppings, built for the whole table. The staff treats this place like it's their living room and you're a friend who just walked in. From breakfast through dessert, it's downtown comfort at its coziest.

places.name: Rocco's Tacos & Tequila Bar
places.address: 7468 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Guac and margs for life, as the regulars say. Rocco's on Sand Lake Road is the lakeside patio where Orlando goes when it wants the celebration without the fuss. Start with the tableside guacamole, made to order and devoured to the last scoop, then move through the taco lineup: the Hongos for the mushroom lovers, carne asada done right, cochinitas slow with achiote. Taco Tuesday brings the live DJ and an all-you-can-eat spread, weekends bring the bottomless brunch, and the margaritas keep pace all night. Loud, bright, joyful. Exactly what a taco night should be.

places.name: Teak Neighborhood Grill
places.address: Teak Neighborhood Grill, 6400 Time Square Ave, Orlando, FL 32835-6453
places.description: This is a true neighborhood grill in MetroWest, and the burger list is the stuff of local legend: 37 handcrafted creations, plus 19 more hiding on a password-only Underground Menu. The Glazed Donut Burger and the Kobe Burger get the headlines, but insiders know the loaded pierogies are the real dark horse. Craft beers rotate constantly, the covered patio hums with live music and trivia nights, and the vibe is pure having-a-great-time. Their words, not ours. Whether it's game night, birthday night, or just dinner, this is where the neighborhood lands.

places.name: STK Steakhouse
places.address: 1580 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: This is not your father's steakhouse, and that's exactly the point. STK at Disney Springs fuses the modern steakhouse with a chic lounge: the steaks are serious, a 34-ounce Tomahawk with a flawless crust, the Wagyu Lil' BRGs gone in two bites, the lobster mac and cheese that owns the sides, but the DJ, the scene, and the energy make it a night out, not just dinner. The rooftop is the only one in Disney Springs, and the weekend brunch with Lobster and Eggs Benedict is a whole new reason to come. Arrive hungry, dress sharp, settle in.

places.name: Christini's Ristorante Italiano
places.address: 7600 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Some restaurants serve dinner. Christini's, standing on Restaurant Row since 1984, stages an occasion. Chris Christini built this room on old-world Italian hospitality, and four decades later the formula holds: tuxedoed waiters, live accordion music drifting through the candlelight, and Northern Italian cooking with genuine conviction. The veal chop is the dish people plan anniversaries around, the seafood pasta arrives with real mastery, and a rose for the ladies is just how things are done here. Hall of Fame status, a top-100-of-the-century award, and the most romantic dining room in the city. This is where milestones are celebrated.

places.name: El Burro Loco
places.address: 6524 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: What started as a viral food truck during the pandemic grew up into one of I-Drive's loudest, boldest kitchens, and the energy never left. El Burro Loco serves twisted Mexican food made fresh daily, the kind of menu built for the hungry and the curious. The Classic Burro Loco burrito wraps rice, fries, and burro sauce into a fourteen-inch tortilla that takes commitment. The birria tacos drip with au jus, the cheese-shell tacos are pure indulgence, and the whole place runs late for those midnight cravings. Bold, fun, built different. Their words, and they're right.

places.name: MOOYAH Burgers, Fries & Shakes
places.address: 3155 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: The name says it all, and SoDo's MOOYAH backs it up. Certified Angus Beef burgers built to order, hand-cut fries that arrive hot and salty, buns baked fresh daily, and hand-spun shakes made with real ice cream. The Double Diablo brings the heat, the Bacon Hot Jam Burger is the house favorite, and the sweet potato fries have their own following. Voted Best Burger in Orange County, and it shows: fresh, fast, and genuinely family friendly. When the burger craving hits, this is the answer. Don't sleep on the shake.

places.name: Bar Louie (Plaza on University)
places.address: 4100 N Alafaya Trail, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: Eat. Drink. Be Happy. That's the creed at Bar Louie, the Original Gastrobar, and the Plaza on University location lives it next to the UCF crowd. The Bourbon BBQ Burger and the Voodoo Pasta are the dishes people come back for, the Royal Red Sangria has its own little fan club, and the cinnamon donut holes are the move you didn't know you needed. Craft cocktails, bold food, live energy, and a bar that stays open late. Whether it's game night with friends or a date night on the patio, this is the neighborhood hangout done right.

places.name: Goodfella's Pizzeria
places.address: 11873 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: This is the real New York deal, brought to Alafaya by families who ran an Italian deli in Queens for over fifteen years before moving to Florida. Goodfella's is family owned and operated to the bone, with staff who've been there for years and customers who drive across town for a taste of home. The New York-style pies have that proper fold and snap, the Goodfella's Special loads it all on, and the garlic knots are the kind people order by the dozen. Free delivery, big family-friendly room, cannoli and tiramisu to close. Friday night, done right.

places.name: Black Rooster Taqueria
places.address: 1323 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: In a city stacked with tacos, Black Rooster earned its place the hard way: a decade in Mills 50, a Michelin Guide nod, and an Orlando Sentinel Best Tacos title. Chef-owners Juliana and John Calloway press their corn tortillas in house every day, and the difference is in your hands the second the tacos land. The smoked beef brisket taco is the one to beat, the pozole verde with slow-cooked pork shoulder is comfort in a bowl, and the crispy fish taco keeps the daily-catch promise. Finish with tres leches cake. This is craft tacos with a chef's conscience.

places.name: Valhalla Bakery
places.address: 5565 Old Cheney Hwy, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: Here's the secret the plant-based crowd already knows: Valhalla Bakery's doughnuts, cupcakes, and decadent desserts are fully dairy and egg free, and you'd never guess. The sticky buns inspire the kind of devotion people write in all caps, the s'mores brownies are rich enough to stop conversation, and the seasonal specials, like gingerbread cake with vanilla buttercream and cookie butter drizzle, keep the case worth checking on every visit. Fruity pebbles doughnuts, guava and cream cheese cupcakes, triple chocolate everything. Grab lunch next door at Dharma, then bring the dessert. This is indulgence with a conscience.

places.name: Gelato LaCarraia
places.address: 7600 Dr Phillips Blvd Ste 38, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: They came from Florence with a 25-year recipe for happiness, and Orlando is the beneficiary. Gelato LaCarraia at the Market Place at Dr. Phillips serves gelato the Italian way: dense, creamy, natural, with Italian music floating through the air and staff who'll let you taste until you find your flavor. The pistachio is the benchmark, sinfonia has its devotees, and adventurous palates rave about the lavender. Finish it as an affogato, or grab a Nutella crepe on the side. One scoop is never enough. Plan accordingly.

places.name: The Cowfish Sushi Burger Bar
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Can't decide between a burger and sushi? The Cowfish at Universal CityWalk refuses to make you choose. This is the first and only Sushi Burger Bar, and its signature Burgushi fuses the two worlds: sushi rolls built from burger components, pickup sandwiches stuffed with sushi ingredients. The Rise and Swine burger and the fresh tuna rolls are the favorites, and the bento boxes let the indecisive sample both. The bar leans playful, with spiked hand-spun milkshakes and exotic martinis, and kids get bento boxes with candy sushi. Quirky, loud, and a whole lot of fun.

places.name: Paddlefish
places.address: 1670 E Buena Vista Dr, Orlando, FL 32830
places.description: Dinner aboard a steamboat on Lake Buena Vista. That's the promise at Paddlefish, and the reimagined vessel delivers it with three decks of 360-degree waterfront views. Executive Chef Steve Richard runs a seafood menu built for indulgence: the daily catch, whole Maine lobster, king crab, scallops, with filet mignon waiting for anyone who prefers turf with their surf. The rooftop is the move, sunset over the water with a craft cocktail in hand, and the build-your-own boil lets you call the shots. This is Disney Springs' most romantic table. Welcome aboard.

places.name: East End Market
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Forget the food courts you know. East End Market is a culinary hub in Audubon Park where a market hall, incubator kitchens, and an event space all hum under one roof. Line up for the famous Gideon's Bakehouse cookies, tear into a loaf from Olde Hearth Bread, sip Lineage Coffee, and wander past La Femme du Fromage and Domu. Every corner belongs to a local maker with something to prove. Come hungry, leave with a bag full of somebody's craft.

places.name: Wine & Corks
places.address: 420 E Church St Ste 108, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A wine bar that moonlights as a sushi spot, on East Church Street downtown, is exactly the kind of delightful surprise that keeps this city interesting. Wine & Corks is first a boutique wine store, with staff who genuinely love guiding you through a tasting, from crisp whites to full-bodied reds. But the kitchen runs a real sushi program too: the salmon tempura roll and the Miami roll have their loyalists, and blackened fish rounds out the menu. Browse the bottles, grab a pour, order a roll. It's the kind of low-key evening that turns into a tradition.

places.name: Bruster's Real Ice Cream
places.address: 5584 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Every Bruster's makes its ice cream fresh in the store, every single day, and you can taste it. With 150 flavors on rotation and at least 24 handcrafted daily, the case changes constantly, which is why regulars have strong opinions about their favorites. Graham Central Station, the white raspberry truffle, the classic hot fudge brownie sundae, and for the plant-based crowd, the banana peanut butter that rivals any dairy scoop. Fresh waffle cones, thick hand-spun shakes, mini cones for the little ones, and yes, pup cups for the four-legged. Simple, joyful, done right.

places.name: Bonefish Grill
places.address: Bonefish Grill, 5463 Gateway Village Cir, Orlando, FL 32812
places.description: Just across from SeaWorld, Bonefish Grill built its name on a simple idea: market-fresh seafood, cooked over a wood-burning grill, served somewhere you actually want to sit. The Bang Bang Shrimp is the legend, crispy, creamy, with that sweet heat you keep chasing. The Chilean sea bass and the parmesan-crusted rainbow trout show the kitchen's finesse, and the wood-grilled steaks mean nobody's left out. Add a proper martini from the bar, and you've got the kind of dinner that works for date night, family night, or just the craving you came in with.

places.name: Seasons 52
places.address: 7700 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Seasons 52 is for people who want the full experience without the heaviness. The menu turns with the seasons, the cooking happens over an oak fire and in a brick oven, and there's not a fryer in sight, so everything lands fresh, vibrant, lighter. The cedar-plank roasted salmon and wood-grilled filet mignon are the signatures, the coldwater lobster flatbread is the starter that disappears, and the Mini-Indulgence desserts let you finish sweet without regret. Fifty-plus wines by the glass keep the pairings interesting. Waterfront views on Sand Lake, happy vibe throughout. This is date night done easy.

places.name: Keke's Breakfast Cafe
places.address: 4192 Conroy Rd, Orlando, FL
places.description: This is how breakfast is supposed to work. Coffee ground in house, eggs cracked by hand, real butter and real whipped cream, and not a microwave in the building. Keke's near Millenia builds its mornings on abundance: the stuffed French toast, cinnamon apple or turtle, towers over the plate, the Florida pancakes taste like someone's grandmother made them, and the Greek omelet with home fries is the savory move. Lighter options exist if you're pacing yourself, but the portions here are generous in the way that says we love you. Get there early on weekends. Everyone else will.

places.name: Camila's Brazilian Restaurant
places.address: 5458 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Serving Brazilians in Florida since 1989, Camila's is one of the country's largest and most traditional Brazilian restaurants, and the I-Drive location feels like the front door to the whole culture. The buffet runs deep: fourteen salads, a dozen hot dishes, grilled meats, and classics like picanha, feijoada, beef stroganoff the Brazilian way, and a creamy bobó de camarão that will ruin you for shrimp purée elsewhere. Wash it down with ice-cold Guaraná or a Brazilian beer. It's family-friendly, unpretentious, and beloved by the local Brazilian community. Go hungry. Go back for seconds. Nobody here will judge you.

places.name: The Juicy Crab
places.address: 296 E Michigan St, Orlando, FL
places.description: This is a seafood boil the way New Orleans intended it, with a family legend behind it. The Juicy Crab started with the Chen family, inspired by New Orleans and Grandfather Chen's travels: a Cajun boil spot where the crab arrives drenched, seasoned, impossible to eat politely. Build your own combo, shrimp, sausage, corn, potatoes, snow crab, crawfish, whatever you crave, or splurge on Dungeness and king crab. The fried shrimp basket and coco bread cover the non-boil loyalists, and a full bar to wash it down. Grab a bib. Commit. No half measures.

places.name: Portillo's
places.address: 7715 Palm Pkwy, Orlando, FL
places.description: Midwesterners in Orlando, this one's for you. Portillo's has been slinging Chicago street food since 1963, and the Orlando spots go full retro diner: red, chrome, the smell of slow-roasted Italian beef the moment you walk in. The Italian beef sandwich is the legend, dripping with jus, sweet or hot peppers the way Chicagoans argue about. The Chicago-style hot dog is dragged through the garden correctly. The chocolate cake shake sounds wrong until it tastes right. Order at the counter, grab a seat, and watch families, students, homesick transplants reach for the same fries. It's loud, fast, and joyful.

places.name: Bora Bora Smoothie Cafe (UCF)
places.address: 10065 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Step into this spot near campus and the tropics hit you first, in color and in scent. Bora Bora built its name on crepes and towering signature drinks, and both land the way dessert should: the pistachio and Dubai chocolate crepes are the ones people talk about, and the Unicorn strawberry-mango drink is pure theater in a cup. Acai bowls, croffles, and fresh fruit everything fill out a menu that treats sweetness like a craft. It is the kind of place students and sweet-tooths orbit for the sugar rush alone.

places.name: Tasty Takeover
places.address: 2424 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: One night a week, the parking lots behind the Milk District bars turn into the best dinner decision you will make all month. Tasty Takeover has run since 2011, and the formula never changed: a rotating lineup of local food trucks, from poke bowls and Jamaican plates to donuts and vegan spreads, parked where you can carry dinner into the bar next door. Every visit is different because the trucks are different, which is exactly why locals keep coming back.

places.name: Yellow Dog Eats
places.address: 1236 Hempel Ave, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: Inside a century-old general store in Gotha, this place serves Southern comfort with its collar popped and its tongue firmly in cheek. The Florida Cracker is the sandwich that made them famous: house-pulled pork stacked with coleslaw, gouda, bacon, pickles, and crispy onions. The pulled pork nachos have a following of their own. Dogs are welcome, the patio hums, and every sandwich on the menu has a name that makes you grin before the first bite.

places.name: Chef Art Smith's Homecomin'
places.address: 1602 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Celebrity chef Art Smith brought his Florida farmhouse kitchen to Disney Springs, and the result tastes like a homecoming worth having. Art's Famous Fried Chicken is the legend: brined, crackling, unapologetic. Start with Thigh High Chicken Biscuits drizzled in hot honey and Church Lady Deviled Eggs, save room for Momma's Mac & Cheese and a Hallelujah Biscuit if you are brave. This is Southern comfort at its most generous, in a dining room that feels like Sunday afternoon.

places.name: Stadium Club
places.address: 8101 World Center Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: This is not your corner sports bar: it is a two-level temple of game day at the Caribe Royale, built for the moment the whole room erupts. Walls of screens carry every matchup at once, VIP booths come with sports simulators of their own, and the kitchen is run by two Top Chef alums who refuse to serve ordinary bar food. Watch here and you feel the roar move through 360 degrees of fans, drinks in hand, nobody sitting still.

places.name: Duffy's Sports Grill
places.address: Duffy's Sports Grill, Lake Buena Vista, FL
places.description: Duffy's has been the Florida sports bar that takes the game seriously for years, and the Lake Mary location is a big, loud, happy temple to it. Screens everywhere, the game always on, a patio that stays busy through the season. The Major League Burger and jumbo wings are the headliners, and the kitchen clearly believes game-day food deserves real care. Bring the crew, find your screen, settle in.

places.name: Krungthep Tea Time
places.address: 1051 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Krungthep is the Thai name for Bangkok, and this Winter Park tea room carries the city of angels into every cup. The Gra-prow chicken sandwich lands sweet, spicy, and savory all at once, the Thai iced tea is the kind people write love notes about, and the brick toast desserts arrive dressed in condensed milk, coconut ice cream, and matcha. The black-and-white room feels calm and design-forward, a place for long chats and slow afternoons over loose-leaf tea.

places.name: Maitland Chocolate Factory
places.address: 445 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: This is a working chocolate shop, not a gift store that happens to sell candy. Every morning, handmade truffles, dipped strawberries, and fudge get made in the back, and the case up front glows with them. With roughly a thousand themed molds, they can turn chocolate into just about anything you need for a birthday, a wedding, or a Tuesday. The Dubai chocolate bar is the current craze, but the classics are what keep Maitland coming back.

places.name: Metro Diner (Kissimmee)
places.address: 2714 Osceola Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: Born in Jacksonville in 1992 and now a Florida institution, Metro Diner does what great diners do: comfort food without irony, served with genuine warmth. The fried chicken and waffles have won real awards, the cinnamon roll pancakes are the reason weekend lines form, and biscuits with sausage gravy come exactly as they should. All-day breakfast, hearty sandwiches, fried chicken done right. This is the place you bring visitors when you want to show them what a diner is supposed to be.

places.name: Puro Dulzor by Karolene
places.address: 1354 E Vine St, Kissimmee, FL 34744
places.description: Puro Dulzor means pure sweetness, and this Kissimmee kitchen lives up to the name from the coffee cup on. The coffee is the thing people rave about first, but stay for the Puerto Rican breakfast: the towering Tripleta sandwich, crisp empanadillas, crema de maiz like abuela made it, and mayorca stuffed with Nutella for the sweet finish. It feels like a cozy island kitchen where the team treats you like family from the first visit.

places.name: Cocina Maya Mexican Grill & Mezcaleria
places.address: 3590 US-17 Ste 1026, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Lake Mary has a little spot of heaven, and it smells like charred chili and warm corn. Cocina Maya treats Mexican cooking like an art form: the Holy Guacamole is made to be worshipped, the Mayan tortilla soup tastes like a family recipe guarded for generations, and dishes like salmon in mezcal sauce and camarones a la diabla go far beyond taco-shop basics. Order a mezcal cocktail and let the smoke in the glass match the fire on the plate.

places.name: Hooked Fish Camp
places.address: 550 Towne Center Cir, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: The F&D crew brought their fish camp concept to Sanford, and the room does exactly what the name promises: rustic cabin warmth, seafood done the relaxed Florida way. Come for a bowl of clam chowder, a pile of mussels, and hush puppies worth writing home about, and stay for crab legs and a slab of lemon pie that arrives sized for the whole table. It is new, it is friendly, and it knows exactly what it is.

places.name: Green Papaya Thai & Sushi
places.address: 2480 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32779
places.description: One kitchen, two traditions, zero compromise. Green Papaya runs a Thai menu and a full sushi bar side by side, and both sides earn their keep: the Tom Kha soup is the kind you talk about afterward, the pad thai and drunken noodles hit every note, and the duck with yellow curry could carry a restaurant on its own. The sushi rolls are fresh and artful, the room is polished and modern, and it works just as well for a date as for dinner with the whole crew.

places.name: Southern Steer Butcher (Orlando)
places.address: 11024 W Colonial Dr, Ocoee, FL 34761
places.description: This is the butcher shop grocery stores wish they could be. Southern Steer in Ocoee is family-owned, obsessed with guest service, and serious about where its meat comes from: all-natural, humanely processed, and now dry-aged in-house. The staff will walk you through the case, teach you how to cook what you buy, and probably talk you into the armadillo eggs. It is part butcher, part neighborhood food school, and fully worth the drive out Colonial.

places.name: The Twisted Chopstick
places.address: 412 S Woodland Blvd, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: DeLand's sushi scene runs through this family-owned spot on Woodland Boulevard, and it runs on passion. The owner and his crew built a place where the Fire Tonkatsu Ramen steams with real heat, the Black Widow and Samurai rolls are art on a plate, and poke bowls and sushi burritos keep the fun dial up. Set in a historic building with a playful Godzilla spirit, it is approachable, creative, and the kind of local gem you tell friends about.

places.name: Crooked Can Minneola
places.address: 1600 Crooked Can Loop, Minneola, FL 34715
places.description: Winter Garden's beloved brewery went big in Minneola, and the result is a genuine destination. The 42,000-square-foot City Center complex packs a full production brewery and canning line, a sprawling taproom, and a food hall of 11 local vendors chosen to spotlight Lake County flavor. Out back there is a beer garden, a live music stage, and a splash pad for the kids. Core brews, seasonal one-offs, and room to breathe. This is the new Crooked Can headquarters, built to be Minneola's gathering place.

places.name: BTW Burgers Tacos Waffles
places.address: 115 E Main St, Tavares, FL 32778
places.description: Tavares punched way above its weight with this one. BTW does exactly what the name promises, burgers, tacos, waffles, and does each with genuine imagination: the Winner Winner chicken and waffles with crispy, never-over-breaded chicken; the Black N Blue burger that people call unbelievable; tacos with a real kick. Then comes the waffle menu, including a caramel-rum number called the Half Witted Monkey, and deep fried Oreos for the brave. It sits right by Brü Tap House, and your beer and burger can meet in the middle.

places.name: Harrell's Hot Dogs and Cold Cones
places.address: 54 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: On the busiest stretch of Plant Street in Winter Garden, Harrell's keeps the hot dog sacred and the options wide open. The all-beef dogs are grilled, never boiled, so every bite has that char; you can build your own with a wall of toppings or grab a signature like the Chicago Dog or the Mac Monster. The fresh-cut fries come seasoned and crisp, and a cold cone at the end is practically mandatory. Grab a seat outside and watch Plant Street stroll by.

places.name: PokeWorks (Oviedo)
places.address: 45 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: Poke done right is fast, fresh, and exactly the way you want it, and PokeWorks in Oviedo nails the formula. Build your own bowl from sushi-grade ahi tuna, salmon, albacore, shrimp, and scallops over rice or greens, or go straight to the signatures: the Hawaiian Ahi, the yuzu ponzu salmon, the umami ahi. There are poke burritos, bite-size poke bombs, and the garlic spam musubi that regulars order on the side. Healthy never felt this satisfying.

places.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
places.address: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, Kennedy Space Center, FL 32899
places.description: There is nothing on this earth quite like standing beneath a real spaceship. At the Visitor Complex you walk the ground where America went to the Moon, come face to face with the Space Shuttle Atlantis, and ride the bus tour out to the Apollo/Saturn V Center, where a Saturn V hangs overhead like the future it still promises. Meet a veteran astronaut, let the Rocket Garden remind you how small your worries are, and watch your kids decide, right there, to become astronauts.

places.name: Ivanhoe Park Brewing Company
places.address: 1300 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Tucked into the historic Ivanhoe District, this independent brewery pours its heart into every pint. The story runs deep: the name honors Lake Ivanhoe founder George Russell and the old Joyland amusement park that once stood here. The beer follows suit with personality, from the crisp Park Hopp'r pilsner to the bold Tupac ShaPorter. The reclaimed-wood taproom and dog-friendly beer garden hum with neighborhood energy, and the rotating taps keep locals coming back to see what is new.

places.name: La Revancha Cuban Cafe
places.address: 7339 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: This East Colonial institution has been pressing Cubans since 1998 and still calls theirs the best in town, and the pressed bread, the roast pork, and the mustard all back that claim up. Get the ropa vieja platter if you want the full table, or the pan con bistec if you want the sleeper hit. The cortadito hits hard and the guava pastries finish sweet. Unpretentious, fast, and exactly what a Cuban cafe should be.

places.name: Viet-Nomz
places.address: 11798 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Orlando's first fast-casual Vietnamese spot started with three friends who just wanted great pho on the go, and it became a local chain worth every expansion. The King Pho bowl is built for serious appetites, the NOMZ-ster bowl packs grilled meats and garden vegetables, and the street fare, banh mi, bao, Nuoc-Nom wings, Wa-Pho fries, keeps things playful. A fresh herb bar lets you finish your own bowl, and the Vietnamese coffee, including the matcha version, is dangerously good.

places.name: Omelet Bar
places.address: 12250 Strategy Blvd Ste 401, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: The UCF area finally has a brunch spot that treats morning like an event. Omelet Bar lets you build your own omelet from a fresh bar of everything, or go bold with signatures like the Bostonian, stuffed with lobster and finished with lobster bisque, or the carne frittata with smoked brisket under sausage gravy. Bread bowls, benedicts, a chicken and waffle flight, and beignets round out the kind of menu that turns first-timers into regulars.

places.name: Fratelli's Italian Restaurant
places.address: 373 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown Orlando has had its family Italian spot on Orange Avenue for years, and Fratelli's plays the classics with conviction. The Fratelli special pizza and the Fratelli's platter are the house signatures, the pastas land like comfort food should, and the shrimp mediterrano and chicken fettuccine alfredo keep regulars loyal. It is low-key, family-operated, and exactly the reliable red-sauce dinner you want when you are downtown.

places.name: Market On South
places.address: 2603 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Market on South is proof that 100% plant-based food can win over anybody who walks in hungry. The food hall lineup covers all the cravings: Kind Cleaver's sandwiches that taste like the real thing, the OrangeBird sloppy-joe, creamy baked mac n cheese, and BBQ jackfruit with real smoke on it. Save room for the ice cream, the cookie monster cone and the Cuban cafecito scoop are worth the trip alone. Skeptics enter, converts leave.

places.name: At The Diner
places.address: 5072 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At The Diner does breakfast with a wink and a serious streak underneath. The pancakes are the main event: cinnamon roll, Boston cream, Fruity Pebbles, the names keep coming and the stacks keep landing. The Bennyffle, an eggs benedict on a waffle, is the kind of genius only a diner could invent, and the chicken and waffles are done right. The Dr Phillips location is the hidden gem of the group, bright, warm, and beloved by locals who know.

places.name: Insomnia Cookies
places.address: 12101 University Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Warm cookies delivered straight to your door: that is the whole pitch, and near UCF it lands perfectly. The classics arrive gooey straight from the oven, the chocolate chunk, the double chocolate, the salted caramel deluxe, and the Cookiewich, two cookies pressed around ice cream, is the move when you are feeling bold. Vegan options exist too. When the craving hits, this is the answer, and it delivers.

places.name: Shake Shack I-Drive
places.address: 8359 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The I-Drive Shack is Shake Shack at its best: the ShackBurger with that famous sauce, the SmokeShack piled with bacon and cherry peppers, the fried-portobello Shroom burger for the vegetarians, and crinkle-cut fries that stay crisp to the last one. The hand-spun shakes and frozen custard concretes, including the location-only Orlandough, close the deal. Dogs are welcome on the patio with their own biscuits. After a spin on the Orlando Eye, this is the move.

places.name: The Polite Pig
places.address: 1536 E Buena Vista Dr, Orlando, FL 32830
places.description: Disney Springs does quick-service better than anywhere on property, and the Polite Pig is the reason. This family-run modern BBQ outpost smokes it all: the tender pork shoulder, the coffee-rubbed brisket, the St. Louis ribs, plus fried chicken with hot honey and the sweet potato tots everyone steals from your tray. Pair it with something from the deep bourbon list, everything pours from the tap, and finish with the buttermilk chess pie. Polished, smoky, and genuinely fun.

places.name: Kai Asian Street Fare
places.address: 1555 State Rd 436 Ste 1171, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Two brothers from different mothers built this place on a simple idea: the best of Asian street food, all under one roof. The Korean fried wings won back-to-back Orlando Sentinel Best Wings awards, and one bite tells you why: shattering-crisp, glossed in sauces from mango habanero to spicy garlic parmesan. The 24-hour tonkotsu ramen won the 2019 Ramen Rumble, the garlic noodles have their own following, and the sweet potato mochi donut is the sleeper dessert of the year.

places.name: Main Street Pizza
places.address: 16 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34744
places.description: Downtown Kissimmee's answer to New York-style pizza does not hold back. The slices are famously bigger than your face, the handcrafted pies use fresh ingredients and old-school recipes, and the menu has real personality: the Buffalo Chicken with its white base, and the Colorado, which piles pepperoni, bacon, chicken tenders, mozzarella sticks, and fries onto one pie. Do not skip the nitrogen ice cream for dessert. This is the neighborhood pizza joint done right.

places.name: Paloma Parlor
places.address: 625 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: On Main Street in Windermere, Paloma is the kind of coffee shop that turns strangers into regulars. The lattes come strong, smooth, and never bitter, finished with a perfect leaf; the chai and house-baked croissants hold their own beside them. Seasonal specials like the Lucky Latte and the rose latte keep things playful. Black-and-white decor, plants everywhere, soft music, and a sidewalk seat when the weather is kind. Worth the short trip out of Orlando.

places.name: Dough Boyz Pizza
places.address: 201 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Oviedo found its New York slice at Dough Boyz, a family-owned spot with the swagger of a Brooklyn joint. Their line is famous: it is not the water, it is the recipe, and the Grandma Margherita, Brooklyn Sicilian, and vodka margherita pies back it up. The chicken parm stuffed garlic knot is a cult object all its own, and the wings, baked then fried, come out impossibly tender. Big personality, bigger slices, and Central Florida clearly approves.

places.name: Le Macaron Celebration
places.address: 671 Front St #110, Celebration, FL 34747
places.description: A little Paris sits on the lakeside promenade in Celebration. Le Macaron's boutique patisserie lines its case with French macarons in more than twenty flavors, salted caramel, pistachio, rose, Colombian coffee, birthday cake, each one crisp-shelled and chewy at the center the way the real thing should be. Beyond the macarons: buttery croissants, éclairs, beignets, house-made gelato, and a proper espresso menu. It is the sweetest pause you will take all day.

places.name: Kobe Japanese Steakhouse
places.address: 12 Central FL locations incl. 8148 International Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Dinner and a show, Japanese-style. Kobé is family-owned and has been doing teppanyaki with flair across Central Florida for years: onion volcanoes, flying shrimp, chefs who turn a flat-top grill into a stage. The sirloin and seafood trio get the full treatment, the sushi side earns its keep with rolls like the Krabby Shrimp, and the soup dumplings are a sleeper pick. Lively, generous, and perfect for birthdays, date nights, or any night that deserves theater.

places.name: Twistee Treat
places.address: Twistee Treat, 4500 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32812
places.description: You cannot miss it: a 25-foot ice cream cone rising off International Drive, a Florida landmark since 1983. Inside the giant cone, Twistee Treat serves real fresh soft serve the old-school way, creamy twists in cups, cones, shakes, malts, and floats, plus the signature Brownie Boat and banana boat. The waffle taco and cookiewich keep the kids happy. It is cheap, cheerful, and the perfect full stop after a day at the parks.

places.name: Jeremiah's Italian Ice
places.address: 877 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL
places.description: Born in Orlando in 1996, Jeremiah's turned Italian ice into a Florida rite of summer. The genius is the Gelati: vibrant Italian ice layered with creamy soft-serve, in more than forty flavors from mango and cotton candy to sea salted caramel and the famous Scoop Froggy Frog. The shops are bright, the lines move fast, and the J-List rewards the regulars. Live life to the coolest, indeed.

places.name: Lake Nona Deli and Market
places.address: 8510 Insular Ln, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Village Walk's neighborhood heartbeat. Lake Nona Deli and Market is a deli, pizzeria, and market in one, tucked into the heart of Lake Nona, built on Boar's Head meats and cheeses, Olde Hearth bread, and local farm-fresh goods. The Italian Classic sandwich stacks thick, the pizzas draw a loyal crowd, and the market shelves cover your everyday needs. Add gelato, boutique wine events, and real community warmth, and you have a third place Lake Nona can call its own.

places.name: Golden Krust
places.address: 2753 N Hiawassee Rd, Orlando, FL
places.description: The taste of Jamaica, golden-baked and flaky. Golden Krust built its name on family recipes: Jamaican beef patties wrapped in that trademark pastry, tucked into soft coco bread, alongside jerk chicken, braised oxtail, curried goat, and whole snapper. The bakery case keeps going with spice bun, hard dough bread, and sweet plantains. Fast, filling, and deeply rooted in Caribbean kitchens, with several Orlando locations serving the same comforting plates island families grew up on.

places.name: High Tide Harry's
places.address: 4645 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Family-owned and proudly local since 1995, High Tide Harry's is the seafood joint airport-corridor locals swear by. Crab legs, lobster, charbroiled oysters, Dungeness crab, and the famous Captain's Seafood Combo pile high, while the Blue Stew has its own devoted following. Fishbowls come big, the nautical decor is unapologetic, and the room runs on easygoing, everybody-knows-your-name energy. This is Orlando seafood the way the locals eat it: generous, fun, and fresh.

places.name: Margaritaville (CityWalk)
places.address: 6000 Universal Studios Plaza Ste 704, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: It is five o'clock somewhere, and that somewhere is CityWalk. Margaritaville is Jimmy Buffett's tropical escape: the Porch of Indecision for open-air sipping, a giant ship's mast rising from the dining room, a margarita volcano for the centerpiece pour, and live bands every night. The Cheeseburger in Paradise earns its name, the coconut shrimp tastes like the beach, and the whole place runs on escapism. Come for lunch, stay for the sunset, leave wearing a lei.

places.name: Five Guys (CityWalk)
places.address: Five Guys (CityWalk), Orlando, FL
places.description: Your theme park burger stop just got a lot more serious. Five Guys landed on CityWalk's upper level as the chain's 2,000th location worldwide, and this one does something unusual: breakfast, a sandwich built for the morning trek into the parks, before it settles into the classics you came for. Burgers you stack exactly your way, hand-cut fries that arrive in an overflowing cup, milkshakes thick enough to matter. After a full day on your feet, that red and white counter feels like a promise kept.

places.name: El Paraíso Del Marisco
places.address: 8421 S Orange Blossom Trl Ste 156, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: This is the seafood Ecuador and Perú would send to represent them: encebollado the way Manabí cooks it, ceviche mixto with that bright Ecuadorian snap, chaulafán de mariscos built to share, bolón de verde and empanadas de verde for the plantain devotees. Everything arrives cooked to order, so the kitchen takes its time, and the time pays off on the plate. Warm, unfussy, family-run feeling, soccer on the screens, the kind of room where regulars drive an hour and come back weekly anyway.

places.name: Topgolf Orlando
places.address: 9295 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Golf skill is completely optional here, and that is the whole point. Across three floors and 102 climate-controlled bays, micro-chipped balls trace your shots at glowing targets while the kitchen sends out burgers and a full bar backs you up. Rooftop terrace with fire pits for the golden-hour crowd, games that range from precision challenges to Angry Birds target smash, and a room that loves birthdays, conventions, and long friendly rivalries. It is cosmic bowling in golf shoes.

places.name: World Food Trucks
places.address: 5811 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: Think of it as a passport with a parking lot. Over a hundred food trucks from more than twenty countries line this Kissimmee park: Latin American spice next to delicate Asian flavors, Caribbean comfort beside street food you never knew you were craving. The lot hums until the early hours with live entertainment, families and night owls circling the trucks, free parking and an atmosphere that feels like a block party with a map of the world. Come hungry, leave with a list.

places.name: AJ's Press
places.address: 182 W State Rd 434 #1008, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: A family-owned Longwood counter that treats the pressed sandwich like a mission. Every sandwich hits a locally baked bolillo or telera, then the press does its crisping work on combinations with a Latin heartbeat: mojo pork dripping with garlic mojo oil, a Cuban with Cantimpalo chorizo beside the slow-roasted pork, beer-braised brisket with cilantro sour cream. Breakfast is served all day, the lattice chips are house-made, and the owners remember you. Small shop, big devotion.

places.name: Shake Shack Winter Park
places.address: 119 N Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The ShackBurger tastes the same everywhere, but only one Shake Shack serves it with a lake view. This Winter Park spot sits right on Lake Killarney, and the back patio looking out over the water has turned a fast-casual run into a small occasion: crinkle-cut cheese fries, a hand-spun strawberry shake, a burger that arrives pink and honest. Come at golden hour, claim an outside table, and let the lake do the rest of the atmosphere.

places.name: TJ's Seafood Shack
places.address: 12231 E Colonial Dr Ste 230, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: The Oviedo shack that turned a strip plaza into a little piece of the Gulf. Beach signs and bucket lights, a menu that runs on fresh-catch confidence: mahi tacos that regulars swear by, a shrimp po' boy with house-made remoulade, hushpuppies crisp outside and honey-drizzled, and the mahi dip people dream about between visits. Even the Angus burger earns respect here. Beach signs, bucket lights, and a cook who clearly loves the fryer: that is the whole recipe, and it works.

places.name: Ben & Jerry's
places.address: 9101 International Dr #1140, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Right in the middle of Pointe Orlando, steps off the I-Drive strip, sits the little counter with the chunky-fun pints you already know by heart. Cherry Garcia, Phish Food, Half Baked, all scooped the old Vermont way, plus sundaes and shakes when the Florida heat wins. It is the comfort stop after dinner or the reward after a long park day, and there is a particular joy in a cone that needs no introduction.

places.name: Blaze Pizza
places.address: 4100 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: Pizza by the assembly line, but done right. You walk the line pointing at more than thirty toppings, the dough is made from scratch, and a blazing hot oven turns your build into a crisp, leopard-spotted pie in three minutes flat. Gluttons, vegans, keto loyalists, the picky kids: everybody walks out with exactly the pizza they pictured. It is fast food with a pizzaiolo's conscience, and the crust crackle is the proof.

places.name: Rome's Flavours
places.address: Rome's Flavours, 124 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789-3819
places.description: A Roman family kitchen tucked onto Winter Park's Park Avenue, and the authenticity is not marketing: the owners are from Rome, the pasta is handmade, the Roman Holiday poster on the wall is practically a credential. The carbonara steals the show, the fettuccine Alfredo wins converts, meatballs get called the best in town, and pistachio cannolis close the deal. Sidewalk seating, a rotating wine list, and the quiet confidence of people who simply follow the Italian traditions.

places.name: Cuban American Cafe
places.address: 135 W Central Blvd Ste 160, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown's best-kept secret hides inside a credit union, and regulars would keep it quiet if the cortadito weren't that good. Family-operated, bread baked fresh every morning, everything made to order: the pressed Cuban on real Cuban bread, a tripleta with real weight to it, bistec de palomilla for the comfort-seekers. Regulars call the coffee the best in town and mean it. Come for lunch, grab a guava pastry on the way out, thank us later.

places.name: La Palette Artisan Ice Pops
places.address: Relocating — new location TBA (Orlando, FL)
places.description: A little paleta shop doing the Latin American popsicle tradition proud. Over fifty flavors, all made with real fruit you can taste in chunks: passion fruit, mango, guava, strawberry. The creamy ones get serious too, Nutella, coconut, cookie crumble, and the filled paletas hiding a core of condensed milk or dulce de leche. The Oreo one has a whole Oreo inside, which tells you everything about this place's generosity. Pure Florida heat relief.

places.name: LaSpada's Original Cheesesteaks and Hoagies
places.address: 1010 Lee Rd, Orlando, FL 32810
places.description: When the owner grew up in Delco country, the cheesesteak standards arrive pre-installed. LaSpada's runs on family tradition and made-to-order pride: the 12-inch original with steak, sweet onions, and white American cheese; a mushroom cheesesteak people cross counties for; the Famous Italian hoagie for when beef is not the move. Guests talk about the cheese distributed perfectly through every bite, the mountain of meat, the sweetness of those onions. This is Philly in Orlando, no translation needed.

places.name: Lombardi's Seafood
places.address: 1888 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Three generations of the Lombardi family have kept this Fairbanks Avenue market the fish counter Orlando trusts, since the early fifties and counting. The cases run deep: stone crab claws in season, whole snappers glistening on ice, first-of-season Copper River sockeye when the Alaska boats come through, live crawfish when they can get them. The little café cooks what the market sells, and the bisque and fish tacos carry that just-off-the-dock confidence. Chefs shop here. You should too.

places.name: Peterbrooke Chocolatier
places.address: 300 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Park Avenue's chocolate temple has been handcrafting in the European tradition since 1983, and you taste the discipline. Chocolate-covered popcorn, their signature, is the sweet-and-salty miracle that ruins all other snacks. Chocolate-dipped strawberries, truffles, hand-made pretzels, and a case of house gelato for when chocolate alone is not enough. Locally owned, smelling of cocoa from the sidewalk, and running chocolate-making date nights where you build your own edible masterpieces. Dangerous for gift budgets.

places.name: Cold Stone Creamery
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Theme-park dessert theater on a frozen granite slab. The crew folds your mix-ins into fresh-churned ice cream right in front of you, sometimes singing while they do it, and the result is a Creation that is exactly yours: birthday cake pieces, brownie chunks, candy and fruit pressed into every fold. The shop is small and the seating is outside, so grab your cup and stroll CityWalk with it. The Brownie a la Cold Stone, hot brownie under cold scoops, is the move after a long park night.

places.name: Se7en Bites
places.address: 617 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Ask what happened when a spa-industry veteran followed her grandmother's recipes to culinary school and opened a Milk District bake shop, and the answer is Se7en Bites: Guy Fieri on Triple D, a Michelin nod, and a line out the door. The chicken pot pie emerges at 11 and vanishes. The Vanilla Bean Bourbon Bacon Moon Pie is the legend. Their motto says let us fill your pie hole, and the Minnie Pearl chicken and waffles and the Se7enth Heaven smash burger back it up. Come early, they sell out.

places.name: Kelly's Homemade Ice Cream
places.address: 3114 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Orlando-made and proud of it: Florida's Favorite churns small-batch ice cream across a string of scoop shops, with monthly flavors that read like a dessert diary, bear claw, fluffernutter, hummingbird cake, toasted s'mores. Clear labeling for allergies, non-dairy in rotation, and Dog Pops for the four-legged regulars. The Fern Creek shop runs patio karaoke nights, which tells you everything about the vibe. Warm, playful, and impossible to leave with just one scoop.

places.name: The Stubborn Mule
places.address: 100 S Eola Dr #103, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: One block from the swans of Lake Eola, a New American spot built around the Moscow Mule's swagger: hand-crafted mule cocktails, hyper-local drafts, and a kitchen run by Culinary Institute graduates with farm and fisherman relationships to prove it. The Stubborn Mule Burger wears Havarti fondue, the waffle burger sandwiches savory beef between two sweet waffles, and the sticky pork belly and parmesan rosemary fries have their own fan club. Eat too much, then stroll it off around the lake.

places.name: Jesse's Rib Shack
places.address: 2202 W Pine St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: The late Jesse Jackson opened this West Pine shack in 1987, and his grandson Jamaal keeps the smoke and the soul exactly where they belong. The ribs and chicken ride on the homemade Magic Sauce, a household-name recipe locals describe as drinkable, and the creamy mac and cheese has its own following. Smoke in the air, soul in the food, doors open until it sells out, and it sells out. A family recipe still feeding Orlando right.

places.name: Rivals Activity Bar
places.address: 25 Wall St Bldg B, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Wall Street Plaza's arcade-bar rethink, reopened fresh with a split personality that works. Come early with the family for modern arcade games, board game tables, and video game stations, then the room shifts after dark to an adult playground of cocktails, bites, and the best pop hits in downtown Orlando. Winnings trade for food and drinks, Orlando City matches air on the screens, and the whole plaza hums around you. Game night, grown-up style.

places.name: Croissant Gourmet
places.address: 2445 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: A little piece of France from two French brothers, Francois a classically trained pâtissier with Champs-Élysées kitchens on his resume. The almond croissant is the star, flaky layers around sweet almond paste, dusted with confectioners' sugar, but the cases run deep: fruit tarts, éclairs, Napoleons, macarons, the raspberry jalousie. Lunch turns savory with a croque madame whose golden yolk oozes down the sandwich exactly as it should. Baked from scratch every morning, because great bread doesn't sleep in.

places.name: Junior Colombian Burger
places.address: 11875 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: This is what happens when Colombian street food hijacks the American burger. The Explosion Burger stacks plantain, mozzarella, egg, corn, and potato sticks into something glorious and unapologetic. The Triple piles crushed chips and house pineapple sauce. The Burger Dog goes full Bogotá with pineapple and pink sauce. Papas locas, homemade empanadas, and signature garlic and pink sauces on everything. Open late for the night owls, and locals call it the best burger in Orlando. Believe them.

places.name: U & Me Revolving Hot Pot
places.address: 12384 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Hot pot meets conveyor belt, with robot waiters delivering drinks and a sassy one seating you at the table. Pick your broth, bone, beef, mushroom, Sichuan heat, Thai Tom Yum, then pull fresh plates of thin-sliced beef, seafood, and vegetables off the revolving line and drop them in. The sauce bar is yours to customize, the boba tea menu is legitimately good, and the whole thing runs all-you-can-eat. Fun, interactive, and stuffed by the end. Kids lose their minds here.

places.name: Chewy Boba Company
places.address: 1212 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A family business pouring boba since 2002, back when bubble tea was still exotic in Orlando. The Colonial Drive shop keeps it classic, taro milk tea, passionfruit, brown sugar milk, in generous cups at honest prices. The University Boulevard outpost innovates with a tap-served boba system and fresh sugarcane juice that guests call criminally refreshing in the Florida heat. Also on the menu: Vietnamese iced coffee with sea salt cold foam and seasonal specials worth watching for.

places.name: SnowBean
places.address: 5310 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: A Korean-inspired dessert café sitting right on Lake Barton, east of the Milk District, and it might have the prettiest deck in Orlando. The star is bingsu, feather-light Korean shaved ice in Oreo Bomb, green tea, and strawberry renditions, plus the croffle, a croissant-waffle hybrid people call the best they've had. Locally roasted beans, pistachio and misugaru lattes, and a fence full of love locks out front. Planes drift over from the executive airport while you sit. Sunset here is a small event.

places.name: Hard Rock Live
places.address: 6050 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The Coliseum of Rock 'n' Roll holds three thousand people and somehow makes every seat feel close to the stage. Concerts, stand-up, big touring names, all delivered with arena-grade sound and lighting in a room with the intimacy of a club. It sits beside the world's largest Hard Rock Cafe, so the memorabilia is everywhere, Elvis's suit, smashed guitars, a museum of loud. Check the calendar before your CityWalk night. There's usually something worth staying for.

places.name: Inter&Co Stadium
places.address: 655 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Downtown's soccer cathedral, home to Orlando City SC and the Orlando Pride since 2017. On match nights the stands turn purple, the drumline never stops, and twenty-five thousand voices make the downtown air shake. The Orlando Made concessions program stocks the concourses with local favorites, and the building has hosted World Cup qualifiers, an MLS All-Star Game, and the Special Olympics opening ceremony. Even if you're not a football purist, one match night here converts you.

places.name: Orlando Farmers Market
places.address: 20 N Eola Dr, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Every Sunday, the lakefront at Eola transforms into downtown Orlando's weekly ritual, running since 1987. Produce and prepared foods, artisan stalls and handmade goods, a wine and beer garden for the grown-ups, live music drifting over it all. Dogs are welcome, the swan boats glide past, and themed Sundays keep it fresh. This is where the city shops, strolls, and eats on its day of rest. Bring a tote, bring the dog, stay a while.

places.name: Marlow's Tavern
places.address: 6889 Eagle Watch Dr, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: The neighborhood tavern that took itself seriously in the kitchen. Scratch-made American fare with a chef's ambition: firecracker shrimp with cracklin' and sweet chili, J.T.'s kettle chips crowned with gorgonzola and bacon, shrimp and crab nachos that surprise everyone, and shrimp and grits on a white cheddar grit cake. The bar pours craft cocktails alongside the classics. Lively, warm, and the kind of place where the server remembers your order by the second visit.

places.name: Yard House
places.address: 8367 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A wall of a hundred-plus tap handles and a glass-enclosed keg room holding thousands of gallons of fresh beer: this is the gathering place for beer lovers, with classic rock on the speakers and a crowd that came to share. The menu runs globally inspired, poke nachos, a Korean BBQ cheesesteak, a tower of onion rings built for the table. Big portions, big energy, and one of the best late-night scenes on I-Drive when the night needs another chapter.

places.name: Bubba Gump Shrimp Co.
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd Ste 735, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Shrimp every way Bubba named in the movie, served with movie trivia under your plate and staff who keep the show going. Fried shrimp, coconut shrimp, peel-and-eat, shrimp mac and cheese, plus Southern comfort for the nonbelievers: baby back ribs, fried chicken, homemade desserts. Take the photo in the Forrest Gump running shoes out front, find the bus bench, and give in. It's touristy and it knows it, and the shrimp is genuinely good.

places.name: The Cheesecake Factory
places.address: 4200 Conroy Rd Space A-148, Orlando, FL 32839
places.description: The menu is a novel, more than two hundred fifty items made from scratch, and somehow the kitchen pulls it off. Start with the avocado eggrolls or Thai lettuce wraps, move to the orange chicken or the Factory burger, and save room no matter how full you feel, because thirty-plus cheesecakes wait at the end, from the original to toasted marshmallow s'mores. Weekend brunch brings a fried chicken and waffle benedict worth the trip alone. At the Mall at Millenia, the patio catches the Florida sun.

places.name: The Donut King
places.address: 3716 Howell Branch Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A family-run donut shop where the donuts come out soft, pillowy, and bigger than you'd expect. The maple bacon glazed is the cult favorite, the apple fritters sell out if you sleep in, and the cases run from red velvet glazed to blueberry cake to every candy-bar topping imaginable. Fried fresh in-house daily, affordable by the dozen, and the kind of neighborhood morning stop that makes the chains irrelevant. Get there early for the fritters.

places.name: Kilwins Ice Cream - Chocolate - Fudge
places.address: 122 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32889
places.description: Walk onto Park Avenue and the smell of caramel finds you first. This is old-school confectionery theater: fudge paddled on the marble slab in the open kitchen, caramel apples dipped and dressed right in front of you, heritage chocolate going back to 1947. The super-premium ice cream in a hand-crafted waffle cone is the headline, but the turtle fudge and the caramel apples are the reason people leave with a box. Sweet in every sense, as they say.

places.name: Winter Park Farmers Market
places.address: 150 N New York Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Saturday morning belongs to the meadow. The Winter Park Farmers' Market spreads across Central Park West Meadow with Central Florida's best produce, artisan breads, local honey, fresh flowers, seafood, and specialty bites from Jamaican patties to kettle popcorn. It's a genuine community gathering, dog-friendly, strollable, steps from Park Avenue shopping. Locals call it their weekly ritual, and one visit shows you why. Come hungry, arrive early, leave with flowers.

places.name: The Ganachery
places.address: The Ganachery, 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Disney Springs' cure for the common chocolate. Expert chocolatiers work the open show kitchen, cutting ganache squares in sixteen decadent flavors, torched artisan s'mores to order, ganache pops, chocolate piñatas filled with treats. The chocolate program is serious business: single-origin dark chocolate from the Dominican Republic, old-world techniques, fresh cream and real vanilla beans. Mickey and Minnie chocolate bars for the kids, dark chocolate with Egyptian salt for you. Every bite feels crafted, because it is.

places.name: BakeChop
places.address: 110 Artisan Aly, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: A scratch kitchen on Artisan Alley where DeLand does farm-to-table with genuine conviction. The Left Hander burger, the Peach Jam Burger with goat cheese and jalapeños that guests call otherworldly, the Fish Bowl when the day's special hits, collard greens that regulars demand, and a quinoa salad that steals shows it had no business stealing. The family's motto is food, family, friends, service, good times, and every plate tastes like they mean it.

places.name: Donuts To Go
places.address: 502 N Spring Garden Ave, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: Sanford's early-morning sweet spot. The Square Glazed Donut, generously sized and endlessly shareable, leads a lineup of Maple Bacon, French Toast, Almond Joy, and the flaky Cronut, plus chocolate cake donuts fans call heavenly and caramel work no one else touches. It is a breakfast kitchen too: burritos, biscuits and gravy, New York-style bagels with cream cheese. Fresh, homemade, kid-friendly, and beloved in the way only a true local donut shop is.

places.name: The Crooked Spoon
places.address: 200 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711
places.description: A beloved Orlando food truck that grew up into Clermont's hottest gastropub, and it still cooks with a food truck's hunger. Chef Saelg's bold menu runs from the 420 Burger, candied bacon and pineapple relish, to lobster grilled cheese, six-cheese lobster mac, and Polynesian pig wings. The blue cheese chips are legendary among regulars. Full bar, outdoor seating, and a room that feels like the neighborhood's own living room. Foodie ambition, small-town heart.

places.name: Over The Top Pita
places.address: Over the Top Pita, 240 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711-2704
places.description: This is the kind of family-owned pita shop that reminds you fast food doesn't have to taste fast. Warm pita, gyro sliced right off the spit, crisp vegetables and bold sauces stacked until the wrap barely closes, every order made to order with obvious pride. The classic Gyro Pita is the move, the loaded pitas are for the truly hungry, and the whole place runs on the no-corporate-kitchen warmth of people who love what they serve.

places.name: Reunion Resort & Golf Club
places.address: 7593 Gathering Dr, Kissimmee, FL 34747
places.description: Three signature courses drawn by Palmer, Watson and Nicklaus, and each one feels like its own world of fairways. But Reunion is bigger than golf: sprawling villas and vacation homes, a water park with lazy river and slides, tennis and pickleball, and the rooftop restaurant Eleven where you can watch fireworks bloom over the parks. Bring the buddies for the tee times, bring the whole family for everything else, and never once feel like leaving the gates.

places.name: Swine & Sons
places.address: 1280/1282 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Born from the Petrakis family's Ravenous Pig empire and now run by chefs Rhys and Alexia Gawlak, Swine & Sons has settled into Winter Park. This is sandwich craft at its most obsessive: house-cured charcuterie, the Nashville Hot Chicken that regulars plan their week around, a smash burger that stops conversation. Grab a table, order boldly, and save room for the Oatmeal Cream Pie.

places.name: Foxtail Coffee
places.address: 2401 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Orlando's own coffee company grew from one small shop into a hometown institution, and every location keeps the same unhurried, neighborly warmth. The espresso is serious, the cold brew flights are a ritual worth trying, and the seasonal drinks lean playful without ever feeling gimmicky. Bring the dog (pup cups are a thing here), camp with your laptop, and watch a city run on caffeine done right.

places.name: First Watch
places.address: 11951 International Dr S, Orlando, FL
places.description: A Bradenton-born breakfast brand that treats the morning like it matters. Everything is made to order in a kitchen with no heat lamps, no microwaves, no fryers, and the menu reads like a chef's daydream: Floridian French Toast, Million Dollar Bacon, smoked salmon eggs benedict, fresh-pressed juices and their Project Sunrise coffee. Bright rooms, sunlit patios, and the particular pleasure of a brunch place that does exactly one shift and does it beautifully.

places.name: Le Macaron French Pastries Winter Park
places.address: 216 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Tucked off Park Avenue into a courtyard that feels like a secret, this is a little piece of Paris in Winter Park. The macarons are the real thing: crisp shells, soft centers, colors like a jewel box, from classic Belgian chocolate to lavender white chocolate. Beyond them: French gelato, eclairs, Napoleons, beignets, European-style drinks. Walk in for one and walk out with a box, because everyone you know deserves the gesture.

places.name: 1881 Restaurant & Bar
places.address: 1881 Restaurant, 308 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34741-5718
places.description: A rare find in downtown Kissimmee: an Uzbek, Turkish and Mediterranean kitchen inside the historic Makinson's Hardware building on Broadway. Steaming manti dumplings, hand-pulled lagman noodles, fragrant pilaf studded with beef and lamb, a mixed grill built for the table, plus a full bar and welcoming outdoor seating. Come curious, order the dishes you can't pronounce yet, and discover one of Central Florida's most unexpected culinary corners.

places.name: Dang Boba & Musubi House
places.address: Dang Boba & Musubi House, 11772 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4625
places.description: Run by UCF alumni with obvious pride, this is where boba culture meets Hawaiian comfort food. The teas are the draw: lavender milk tea, tiger tea, princess peach fruit tea, all brewed with care by their Bobaristas. Then come the musubi: classic spam, spam and kimchi, garlic soy chicken, stacked like edible architecture. Cheerful, student-friendly, and proof that two great cravings belong under one roof.

places.name: Grape & the Grain
places.address: Grape & the Grain, 1110 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Mills 50's neighborhood wine bar, the kind where the staff remembers your pour. Wines hand-selected from vineyards across the globe, Florida craft beer for the non-wine crowd, and a charcuterie board built for lingering. The real magic is out back: a covered patio with funky art, food trucks, trivia nights and DJs. Zero pretension, all warmth, novices and connoisseurs equally welcome.

places.name: Bento Sushi
places.address: Bento Sushi, 12715 Pegasus Dr, Orlando, FL 32816-8030
places.description: BENTO's pan-Asian kitchens are Orlando's reliable answer to the question "where can we all agree?" Sushi rolls cut fresh, poke bowls built your way, hearty bento boxes with teriyaki and katsu, Thai curries for the spice-seekers, plus boba teas to finish. Fast, friendly, and generous with portions, the kind of spot that works for a quick lunch, a family dinner, or the group chat that could never pick a place.

places.name: Juice Bar
places.address: Juice Bar, 2413 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803-6324
places.description: Don't let the plain name fool you: this East South Street spot is Orlando's longtime temple of fresh juice. Made-to-order and cold-pressed blends pressed on a Norwalk juicer, playful names like Hale to the Kale and Gangsta Green, all-vegan menu, smoothies and acai bowls that regulars swear by. Everything tastes like actual fruit, because it is. Free parking out front, zero pretense inside.

places.name: Matt's Latin BBQ
places.address: Matt's Latin BBQ, 6607 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Campo-style cooking brings the island to the city on South Semoran. Watch your mofongo smashed to order, dig into pernil and ribs over rice and beans, rotisserie chicken dripping with juices, ropa vieja, morcilla, all seasoned from freshly ground ingredients. The decor feels like Puerto Rico, the cooking never stops, and regulars will tell you the mofongo is the best in town. Come hungry, leave family.

places.name: Sly Fox
places.address: Sly Fox, 63 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2425
places.description: Downtown's beloved punk-rock dive bar, where the beer is cold, the nights run late, and the basement stage keeps local music loud. Upstairs there's the surprise hit: legendary vegan hot dogs and burgers from the famous Vegan Hot Dog Cart, plus loaded tater tots and late-night comfort food done right. Gritty, warm, and completely itself, Sly Fox is where Orlando's alternative scene comes to exhale.

places.name: TooJay's
places.address: 2624 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Florida's New York-style deli since 1981, and Orlando's Colonial Drive location brings the whole nostalgic spread: towering pastrami and Reuben sandwiches, matzo ball soup, blintzes, and a bakery case of rugalach, babka and their famous Killer Cake. Big portions, fast friendly service, and that particular deli joy of a menu where you could eat three meals and never repeat yourself. Bring an appetite and a takeout bag.

places.name: Fujiyama Sushi
places.address: Fujiyama Sushi, 10153 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: A UCF-area staple for sushi that respects both your cravings and your wallet. Volcano rolls, Philly rolls, teppan lunches sizzling on the griddle, bento boxes packed with teriyaki and tempura, plus tempura cheesecake for the finish. The room is unfussy and friendly, the fish is fresh, and it's the rare sushi spot that works just as well for a study-break lunch as for a full dinner with friends.

places.name: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen
places.address: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027
places.description: Chef Tuvi brings over 20 years of authentic Thai technique to an unassuming Oviedo plaza, and the neighborhood knows it found gold. Panang duck, lobster phad thai, tamarind shrimp, whole snapper dinners people still talk about months later, plus housemade sauces and durian ice cream for the adventurous. The room is contemporary and calm, the flavors are bright and true, and this is Thai cooking with real soul.

places.name: Stefano's Trattoria
places.address: Stefano's Trattoria, 1425 Tuskawilla Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708-4703
places.description: A family-owned Italian kitchen on Tuskawilla Road, serving Winter Springs for two decades, and it shows in every detail. Gnocchi della nonna in pink sauce, veal piccata, lobster ravioli, and a tiramisu cheesecake worth saving room for, all while live piano drifts across the dining room. The owner still works the room, guests feel like family, and this is what real Italian hospitality tastes like.

places.name: White Rabbit Dessert Experience
places.address: White Rabbit Dessert Experience, 875 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828-7049
places.description: Follow the white rabbit to Waterford Lakes for dessert as a full evening out. Over 100 made-to-order creations in a modern open kitchen: waffles, crepes, towering sundaes, cakes and brownies, all crowned with homemade ice cream made fresh daily. The space is designed like an indulgence, the espresso bar keeps the adults happy, and one visit proves dessert was never meant to be an afterthought.

places.name: Broken Strings Taproom
places.address: Broken Strings Brewery, 1012 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805-2216
places.description: Two breweries under one roof on West Church Street, and live music in its DNA. The taproom walls are covered in murals of music legends, the stage hosts reggae nights, local bands, open mics and DJ sets, and the beer lineup leans playful: Penny Layne strawberry blonde, Purple Mane pale ale, Liquid Vinyl. Pet-friendly, game-day ready, and reopened under local ownership with the community spirit fully intact.

places.name: Clean Eatz
places.address: Clean Eatz, 2205 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32806-3038
places.description: Your first step to a healthy lifestyle, according to the sign, and it's the rare health-food spot where flavor didn't get the memo to stay home. Build-your-own bowls, a Bang Bang Shrimp Wrap, Monterey Chicken, buffalo chicken wraps in tomato-basil tortillas, plus weekly meal plans and grab-and-go cases for the week's worth of dinners. Every menu item lists its calories, so you eat informed, not guilty.

places.name: Gentry's BBQ
places.address: 1241 Miller Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Award-winning pitmaster Chris Gentry built this institution on championship craft barbecue, fusing Central Texas brisket technique with Eastern North Carolina pulled pork and flavors gathered from travels across the South. His world-championship mustard sauce leads a whole line of rubs and sauces, and the Friday spreads with ribs, sweet heat chicken, smoked potato salad and honey cornbread have a devoted following. This is barbecue as a life's work.

places.name: Maple Street Biscuit Company
places.address: Maple Street Biscuit Company, 11810 Glass House Ln, Orlando, FL 32836-3794
places.description: Southern comfort on a biscuit throne. Every biscuit is baked from scratch daily, the chicken is always hand-breaded, and the signatures have earned their cult followings: the Squawking Goat (fried goat cheese meets fried chicken, pure genius), the Five and Dime, smashbrowns with sausage gravy, fried green tomatoes. Order the maple vanilla latte, settle onto the patio, and understand why this Florida-born chain keeps growing.

places.name: Sushi Yama
places.address: Sushi Yama, 6748 Grand National Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-8526
places.description: All-you-can-eat sushi on International Drive, served all day at one set price. The lineup is deep: dragon rolls, rainbow rolls, crazy yellowtail, thick-cut sashimi, hibachi steak and fried rice, yellowtail jalapeno, even fried tempura cheesecake at the end. Lines form for a reason. Bring an empty stomach, order in waves, and pace yourself like the pros at the next table.

places.name: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen
places.address: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen, 6125 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822-1500
places.description: Fresh plates of ono grindz near the airport, and devotees will tell you it's the best Hawaiian food on the mainland. The Aloha Special stacks crispy pork belly, ono shrimp and mochiko chicken over rice; the kalbi, huli huli chicken and loco moco all arrive in generous portions with that perfect mac salad. Save room for Alohasadas, doughnuts filled with ube, haupia and pandan. Friendly, clean, island-vibe warm.

places.name: Black Magic Pizza
places.address: Black Magic Pizza, 121 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The self-proclaimed punk rock pizza wizards of the Milk District, born as a pandemic pop-up and now one of Orlando's most talked-about slices. Their hand-tossed pies are neither New York nor Neapolitan but somewhere deliciously in between: the Dr. Pepperoni, the Hornets Nest with hot honey and soppressata, the Tuscan Leather. Dough made in small batches, flavors that take risks, vegan options that don't feel like an afterthought.

places.name: City Food Hall
places.address: City Food Hall, 1412 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803-1862
places.description: The Hall on the Yard is Orlando's flavor hub for the indecisive: a curated mix of local concepts under one big roof by Lake Formosa. Smash burgers, street tacos on hand-pressed tortillas, New Orleans po'boys and shrimp and grits, fresh sushi, New York-style bagels, all circling a central bar with seasonal cocktails and local taps. Add Topgolf Swing Suites upstairs and live events in the outdoor plaza, and dinner becomes a whole evening.

places.name: Crocante Restaurant
places.address: Crocante Restaurant, 4311 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5217
places.description: A full-service restaurant and cocktail bar elevating traditional Puerto Rican cuisine on East Colonial. Executive chef Yamuel Bigio's signature porchetta is slow-roasted until it earns the name, and the menu rewards the curious: bacalaitos tacos, bistec encebollado eggrolls, chicharron with guacamole, shrimp mofongo, tembleque for dessert. Elevated, soulful, and full of crunch, this is Boricua cooking dressed for a night out.

places.name: Chicken Fire
places.address: Chicken Fire, 2425 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5018
places.description: Nashville-style hot chicken with soul, served out of a no-frills joint on East Colonial. Never-frozen tenderloins, brined for up to 24 hours, hand-breaded and fried to order, then tossed in your chosen heat level, from gentle Soulful to straight fire. The Hot Box piles on crinkle-cut fries, coleslaw and their signature Soul Sauce; the mega sliders are a two-fisted commitment. Crispy, fiery, and made with love.

places.name: Empanada & Co.
places.address: Empanada & Co., 15 E 5th St, Apopka, FL 32703-5244
places.description: Baked empanadas that fuel your soul, made from scratch with ingredients sourced from local small businesses. The lineup runs deep: chicken and cheese, Cuban, picadillo, smoked gouda and mushroom, plus dessert empanadas like guava and queso and banana Nutella. Don't skip the housemade sauces, green chile tomatillo, Ecuadorian hot, cilantro garlic mayo. Quick, flaky, golden, and made with obvious love.

places.name: Joes Holy Smoke BBQ
places.address: Joes Holy Smoke BBQ, 1515 Lee Rd, Orlando, FL 32810 (name variant of JK Holy Smoke?)
places.description: Don't judge a barbecue joint by its gas station, because this one inside the Shell on 17/92 has been smoking up some of the area's best 'cue since its food truck days. Fall-off-the-bone ribs, pulled pork and the kind of friendly service that remembers your name, all from a family operation with real name recognition among Orlando barbecue loyalists. A genuine hidden gem on Lee Road.

places.name: Kavas Tacos & Tequila
places.address: Kavas Tacos & Tequila, 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Bienvenidos to Pointe Orlando's loudest, most colorful taco bar.
