Quesabirria tacos dripping with consomme, a three-foot taco board built for the whole table, carnitas flautas, and a margarita list that includes the watermelon and the Kadillac. Nightly live entertainment, DJs, fire shows, brunch on weekends, and a tequila selection that means business. This is I-Drive energy at its most delicious.

places.name: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf
places.address: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf, 3402 Technological Ave, Orlando, FL 32817-1402
places.description: Ramen with a side of theater near UCF. The bowls are the main act: Tokyo tonkotsu shoyu, Kyushu spicy tonkotsu, the yin-yang bowl with two broths in one, plus fluffy tonkotsu omurice and pork belly bao. The room is pure Instagram: treehouse-like seating, private honeycomb booths, curtain-drawn date tables. Finish with TBaar bubble tea or matcha pudding, and this is the most photogenic ramen night in town.

places.name: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant
places.address: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant, 933 Orlando Ave S, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Lim Ros means "to taste" in Thai, and this modern Maitland dining room makes sure you do plenty of it. Crying tiger steak that earns its name, kanom jeen namya pu, a house curry brimming with real crabmeat, tom kha gai hot pot, and one of the best panang curries in town. Upscale but unpretentious, with a full gluten-free and vegan menu, butterfly pea tea cocktails, and flavors that taste like someone's grandmother is in the kitchen.

places.name: Melt N Dip
places.address: Melt N Dip, 7341 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-5263
places.description: A Dubai-born dessert house built around one glorious idea: Belgian chocolate, warm and gooey, coating everything. Stuffed crepes dripping with sauce, fresh-baked brownies, crispy waffle sticks, thick milkshakes, gelato and fresh fruit platters with chocolate dips. The menu is enormous, the chocolate is rich, and one visit will cure whatever sweet tooth brought you in. A family-friendly treat destination in every sense.

places.name: Oza Izakaya
places.address: Oza Izakaya, 5310 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-8772
places.description: A modern Japanese izakaya with sleek garden vibes and a chef, Tim Liu, cooking like every plate is a first date. Yuzu hamachi, buttery uni toast, wagyu gyoza with truffle, grilled octopus with yuzu foam, miso yaki cod, an excellent sake list, nightly happy-hour cocktails. It's a stay-drink-place built for lingering: order small, share everything, and let the night stretch out under the garden lights.

places.name: Smokey Jay's BBQ
places.address: Smokey Jay's BBQ, 9318 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4100
places.description: True Southern barbecue cannot be rushed, and the pitmasters at Smokey Jay's start before dawn, smoking over real wood until the bark and smoke ring are just right. Fall-off-the-bone ribs, tender pulled pork, brisket loaded fries, collard greens, candied yams, homemade mac and cheese, red velvet cake at the end. A family-run operation with a devoted following, open until sold out, because the best barbecue never lasts the day.

places.name: Sushi Pop
places.address: Sushi Pop, 310 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765-4921
places.description: Oviedo's monotony breaker, in their own perfect words. Chef Chau runs the sushi bar like an artist's studio: seasonal crudo, nikkei maki, ceviche rolls, buffalo rock shrimp, and an omakase worth trusting him with. The room feels like a Vegas tourist district in the best way, bold, loud, unapologetic, and the seafood is some of the freshest in Orlando. Book ahead, this one gets packed.

places.name: Ten10 Brewing
places.address: Ten10 Brewing, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2532
places.description: A local brewery, a tasting room, a meeting place for friends and strangers: that's how Ten10 describes itself, and the Mills 50 taproom lives it. A self-styled DIY punk rock brew crew with character-drenched beers, Grandmas Purse butterscotch ale, Big Green Egg smoked wings, a kitchen that punches above its weight. Dog-friendly patio, Tuesday run club, Thursday trivia, live music. This is neighborhood brewing at its happiest.

places.name: The Escobar Kitchen
places.address: The Escobar Kitchen, 420 E Church St, Orlando, FL 32801-2775
places.description: Latin Asian fusion done with swagger. The Escobar Roll fuses shrimp tempura, churrasco and sweet plantains; the Mar Y Tierra tops it with chimichurri; the Paisa Roll and Gentleman's Roll keep regulars loyal. Then there's the famous Arroz Enchurrascado, paella-style rice with skirt steak, plantains and chimichurri. Family-owned, made with love, and proof that Latin flavors taste even better in sushi form.

places.name: TT Crepes
places.address: TT Crepes, 10681 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4470
places.description: A great little surprise tucked inside Mei Supermarket in Union Park. TT Crepes keeps the menu small and the flavors dialed in: jianbing, the beloved Chinese street crepe with its crisp, egg-laced crunch, plus scallion pancakes done right. The kind of unassuming counter where regulars know exactly what they're getting, and what they're getting is very good. Hidden gem energy, zero pretension.

places.name: Vinia Wine & Kitchen
places.address: Vinia Wine & Kitchen, 444 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4224
places.description: Husband and wife Fabio Perricelli and Paula Gamba run this Hannibal Square wine bar the way you'd welcome guests into your own home. Shared plates with an Italian-Brazilian soul, braised oxtail gnocchi, Romeu & Julieta cheese bread with guava sauce, vegan escargot and beet wellington, all poured alongside a curated boutique wine list. Low light, live music, warm hospitality. Named Critic's Choice for Best Vegan/Vegetarian in the 2025 Orlando Sentinel Foodie Awards, but carnivores will never feel neglected.

places.name: AJ Chocolate House
places.address: AJ Chocolate House, 552 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4322, United States
places.description: A European-rooted chocolate emporium on Park Avenue that blends luxury with edible art. Belgian truffles, molten fondues, a charcuterie tower built for sharing, waffles you dip in chocolate, fig and salmon crostinis, and wine and coffee to round out the evening. The owner is famously warm and attentive, and guests feel genuinely welcomed. Executive chef Edwin Jablonskas runs the kitchen. A second location just opened in New Smyrna Beach: proof this flagship hit on something special.

places.name: Boku Sushi
places.address: Boku Sushi, 140 Independence Ln, Maitland, FL 32751-5603, United States
places.description: Tucked into the corner of its Maitland complex behind the Starbucks, Boku is the kind of neighborhood sushi spot that makes regulars out of first-timers. The room glows with warm wood, tile and stone, and the rolls have cult followings: the Drama Queen, the Foxy Lady, the Out of Control, and a jalapeño hamachi one reviewer swore was the best version he had ever tasted. Sit out on the pet-friendly patio when the evening cools, and ask about the Sea Bass.

places.name: Schakolad Chocolate Factory
places.address: Schakolad Chocolate Factory, 9901 Hawaiian Ct, Orlando, FL 32819-8102, United States
places.description: Pronounce it shaq-oh-LAD and prepare to fall. This is a family affair, born when Edgar Schaked walked away from an engineering career to keep his father Baruch's chocolatier legacy alive, and the Orlando factory makes its European-style chocolates fresh on the premises every day. More than seventy varieties of truffles, molded novelties, wedding favors, and edible gift creations line the cases, and their Sweet Night Out events let you go behind the counter to make and decorate your own, with generous taste testing along the way.

places.name: Half Barrel Beer Project
places.address: Half Barrel Beer Project, 9650 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-8766, United States
places.description: Do not let the size fool you. Half Barrel squeezes a brewer's obsession into a twelve-tap room on Universal Boulevard: two of its own house brews pouring beside a ruthlessly curated selection of Florida craft, with coolers stacked deep in bottles and cans to take home. The room is industrial and unpretentious, the staff talks beer the way regulars do, and the fall-off-the-bone wings have their own following. A craft-beer hideout hiding in plain sight.

places.name: Mario's Pizza
places.address: Mario's Pizza, 7213 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32822-5805, United States
places.description: This Curry Ford corner spot does New York style the honest way: dough made fresh daily, cheese cut fresh daily, produce from a local distributor, and a menu that stretches from calzones and strombolis to baked pasta and ziti. The owner is known to sit down and talk with guests, and the vegan side of the menu punches far above its weight, from the Girlfriend pie to the Crown Jewel. A neighborhood family joint that treats a slice like it matters.

places.name: Pienezza Pizza
places.address: Pienezza Pizza, 3236 N John Young Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741-7549, United States
places.description: Generations of Brooklyn tradition set the table at this family-owned Kissimmee pizzeria, and you can taste the borough in every fold of the crust. Beyond the classic round pies, the signatures tell the story: the Hey Brooklyn, the Crazy Margherita, a Sicilian Flag layered with red and white sauces, and a Grandma's pie that regulars swear transports them straight to The City. With a second spot in Downtown Orlando's Creative Village, the Pienezza family is spreading the gospel far beyond The Loop.

places.name: San Julian's Coffee
places.address: San Julian's Coffee, 110 Orlando Ave S, Winter Park, FL 32789-3656, United States
places.description: Winter Park has no shortage of coffee shops, but none pour quite like San Julián's. This cozy Colombian coffee bar on Orlando Avenue brews the way the Andes intended: rich, smooth, unapologetically strong, with standouts like the pistachio latte and the viral tiramisu latte. The food menu reads like a love letter to Colombia and Venezuela, with arepas, empanadas, crispy tequeños, and flaky guava-and-cheese quesitos. Mornings simply taste better here, and the regulars will tell you so.

places.name: Sushi Lola's
places.address: Sushi Lola's, 2902 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803, United States
places.description: Sushi Lola's runs on a delicious split personality. Owner Aaron Pak has kept two kitchens humming on Corrine Drive in Audubon Park for over a decade: one for sushi, one for Korean, so your table can hold a Playboy roll and a sizzling dolsot bibimbap at once. The Lava Dips are a cult appetizer, the Volcano roll lives up to its name, and dessert arrives as a warm browned butter cookie, on the house. It is the rare fusion spot where both halves of the hyphen earn their keep.

places.name: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry
places.address: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry, 1436 State Road 436, Casselberry, FL 32707-6506, United States
places.description: Founder Freddy Zubieta started cooking at fifteen and brought that lifelong obsession to Orlando in a food truck back in 2015; the Casselberry outpost is part of a fleet that now stretches to Tampa and Sarasota. Come for the ceviche in all its forms, from the classic to the Carretilla, and do not skip the leche de tigre, the fiery citrus marinade that regulars drink straight. Lomo Saltado, crispy jalea, and a proper pisco sour complete the trip to the Peruvian coast.

places.name: Hinode Sushi
places.address: Hinode Sushi, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027, United States
places.description: Chef George Tan plates sushi like art in this Oviedo neighborhood spot, and locals treat it as their own delicious secret. The Trio Tower stacks tuna, salmon, yellowtail, mango and avocado into something striking, the Black Widow roll wears a spiderweb of sauce, and even the avocado fries arrive as beautiful little sculptures. Everything tastes as vivid as it looks, from the Roll On Fire to the Oviedo Sunrise. A warm, family-run room where the fish is always fresh and the plates always turn heads.

places.name: Ollie's Public House
places.address: Ollie's Public House, 3400 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-3602, United States
places.description: Ask College Park where the neighborhood goes when it wants everything at once, and they will point you to Ollie's. This Edgewater Drive public house pairs a rotating craft beer list with more than thirty TVs, live music, and a big covered patio where dogs get water and cold cuts by name. The Legend sandwich and the Wall Street Reuben are the plates regulars swear by, the bar food runs deep and satisfying, and a rotating Good Bite menu item gives back to a local cause. It is the room where weeknights are never boring.

places.name: Tropico Mofongo
places.address: Tropico Mofongo, 3160 Vineland Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34746-4657, United States
places.description: The name tells you everything: this Kissimmee kitchen worships the mofongo. Plantains pounded with chicharrón and garlic arrive under pernil, shrimp, or all three in the Mofongo Trio, and locals call it the best in town. The room is bright and cheerful, the music stays upbeat, the pernil sandwich with pickled onions is a sleeper hit, and regulars insist the mojitos and margaritas are the area's finest. Generous portions, proud Puerto Rican soul, zero pretension.

places.name: Bad AS's Sandwich
places.address: Bad AS's Sandwich, 207 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5819, United States
places.description: Chef John Collazo does not make sandwiches so much as compose them. The Milk District counter that grew out of a 2015 food truck dream serves the Ninja, an Asian-glazed pork belly bomb with spicy miso aioli that put the place on Orlando's food map, alongside a roster of house-built beasts on French rolls baked in-house. Every sandwich lands with crunchy house-made kettle chips, and the weekly specials have a habit of selling out before noon. The room shares its address with a bike shop and feels like a regular's club.

places.name: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe
places.address: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe, 1181 Rinehart Rd, Sanford, FL 32771-7390, United States
places.description: Dali's runs on mom's recipes, and you can taste the family in every bite. This small Sanford spot serves Lao and Thai cooking built on fresh ingredients and generous portions, from the homemade sausage with sticky rice and the fiery jaew bong pepper paste to the red curry chicken noodle soup regulars order on repeat. The pad thai and papaya salad get raved about, the curry beef empanadas sell themselves, and takeout orders arrive with sweet handwritten notes. Come for flavor, not frills; you will not miss them.

places.name: Taqueria las Cazuelas
places.address: Taqueria las Cazuelas, 10360 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4364, United States
places.description: A beloved Eastside story: when the original Las Cazuelas built a devoted following on authentic home-style Mexican, the family opened this taco-centric outpost on East Colonial, and the magic carried over. Tacos come double-wrapped in soft corn tortillas with onion and cilantro: birria, carne asada, al pastor, carnitas, with a house red sauce that regulars warn is potent. Weekend menudo keeps the loyalists coming back, and every plate tastes like a kitchen that genuinely loves feeding you.

places.name: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana
places.address: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana, 5475 Gateway Village Cir, Orlando, FL 32812-4002, United States
places.description: Family owned and operated since 1998, Agave Azul brings a high-energy, highly stylized take on the Mexican kitchen. Tortillas are hand-pressed fresh, the churrasco comes off the fire smoky, and the margarita program is the real show: the Clase Aparte and the Night in Tulum are the kind of pours people write home about. Birria tacos, queso fundido with chorizo, and jalapeños rellenos round out a menu that never phones in flavor. Vibrant, loud in the best way, and built for a night out.

places.name: Delaney's Tavern
places.address: Delaney's Tavern, 1315 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: On the ground floor of the boutique Delaney Hotel, this SoDo tavern has been the neighborhood's special-occasion answer since 2019, and it earned the reputation honestly. Chef Anthony Albino runs a farm-to-fork New American menu anchored by the blue crab beignets, the almond-crusted salmon, and a Wagyu burger worth writing home about, while the bar pours house craft cocktails with real conviction. The weekend bottomless brunch is a local legend, and the patio firepits keep evenings glowing long after dinner.

places.name: Knife Burger
places.address: Knife Burger, 4040 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32837-7662, United States
places.description: When the chef behind a Michelin-starred steakhouse decides to do burgers poolside, you pay attention. Chef John Tesar's Knife Burger sits at the edge of the JW Marriott Grande Lakes pool, slinging 44 Farms sirloin patties with the same seriousness he brings to Knife & Spoon next door. The Ozersky keeps it classic and perfect, The Magic swaps the bun for an English muffin and adds bacon, and the pimento burger and mahi sandwich have their own devotees. Serious beef, resort pool, zero stuffiness.

places.name: Uncle Tony's Backyard BBQ Orlando
places.address: Uncle Tony's Backyard BBQ Orlando, 6807 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32809-6025, United States
places.description: Down in Pinecastle, Uncle Tony's cooks the way a backyard legend would: brisket, ribs that fall apart, and sides that hold their own, from collard greens and baked beans to fried okra and mac and cheese. The Brisket Birria Tacos and the Mac Daddy Burger prove the kitchen likes to play, but the smoke is the star, and the staff treats you like a neighbor. It has the small-town feel of a place that never expected to blow up, and the food of one that was always going to.

places.name: Beirut Grill and Deli
places.address: Beirut Grill and Deli, 3100 Alafaya Trl, Oviedo, FL 32765-9466, United States
places.description: When a place earns Best Middle Eastern in the Orlando Sentinel Foodie Awards, you listen, and this family-owned halal Lebanese kitchen near UCF makes believers fast. The chicken shawarma and falafel win converts, the grape leaves are made from scratch, the manakish bakes up fresh, and regulars beg newcomers to save room for the kenefeh. A guest who once lived in Lebanon called it the real thing, and the owner greets you with the warmth of someone cooking for family. Generous, authentic, and deeply loved in Oviedo.

places.name: Domu Chibi Ramen
places.address: Domu Chibi Ramen, 869 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828-7049, United States
places.description: DOMU's fast-casual little sibling brings the house-made noodles and broths east to Waterford Lakes, and the quality carries the family name proudly. Six varieties run from classic tonkotsu to butter miso and a solid vegan option, and the Japanese Curry Ramen with tonkatsu is the move for the indecisive. The boneless wing bites have their own fan club, the pork katsu sando is no joke, and the modern room with self-order kiosks keeps everything easy. Real ramen craft, minus the waitlist.

places.name: Thrive
places.address: Thrive, 15 E 5th St, Apopka, FL 32703-5244, United States
places.description: Apopka's food hall scene leveled up when the crew behind the downtown Thrive Cocktail Lounge planted an eatery inside Halls On 5th. The drinks are the draw: the Best Beehavior pours cranberry-infused gin with rosemary honey, the Nuttin' Serious washes bourbon in brown butter, and seasonal releases keep the menu turning. With brunch, lunch and dinner all covered, it is proof that serious cocktail craft does not need a downtown address, just a talented bar and a room that knows how to celebrate.

places.name: The Goblin Market Restaurant
places.address: The Goblin Market Restaurant, 330 Dora Drawdy Ln, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5593, United States
places.description: Charming locals and tourists since 1996, the Goblin Market is Mount Dora's storybook gastropub, and the name fits. Inside, book-lined rooms glow like a library that learned to cook; outside, a secret-garden courtyard beneath a big camphor tree turns spectacular after dark. The Irish Whiskey Onion Soup is non-negotiable, locals will tell you, followed by the crab and lobster bisque and the Irish Cheddar Burger. It is the kind of place where dinner stretches long because nobody wants to leave.

places.name: Henry's Depot
places.address: Henry's Depot, 212 W 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771-1204, United States
places.description: Sanford's old train station, the site of Florida's first railroad system built by Henry B. Plant, now hums as an open-air food hall, and the history tastes great with lunch. Vendors run the full delicious spectrum: wood-fired pizza, ramen, seafood, sandwiches, ice cream from the Greenery Creamery, and craft coffee from Mahogany. The old-Florida-themed Basin anchors it all with craft cocktails and live music, and Sunday brunch is the local ritual. Come hungry, stay for the entertainment, bring the whole family.

places.name: Hollerbach's German Market
places.address: 117 Magnolia Ave, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: Right around the corner from the famous beer hall, the Hollerbach family's German Market is the deli of dreams for anyone who loves Deutschland. A full-service bakery turns out Black Forest cake and apple strudel, the delikatessen lunch counter builds sandwiches like the Reubenstein, and the shelves stock imported German everything: beer and wine from over fifty breweries and wineries, Milka chocolate, Gummi bears, Haribo, Knorr, Löwensenf. Pair a pretzel with a Riesling, grab provisions for your own German dinner at home, and take home a little Gemütlichkeit.

places.name: Indian Pavilion
places.address: Indian Pavilion, 13770 W Colonial Dr, Winter Garden, FL 34787-4202, United States
places.description: The only place in Winter Garden where a sports-themed dining room meets modern Indian cooking, and it works. Indian Pavilion promises a century in every dish, then delivers: Old Delhi butter chicken, chicken tikka masala, lamb korma and saag paneer anchor the classics, while playful standouts like tandoori pineapple burrata and the Tik Tok Chaat keep things interesting. The garlic naan never survives long enough for seconds to arrive. Bold spices, modern presentation, and a room with real energy.

places.name: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams
places.address: 510 N Orlando Ave #102, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Jeni's is not ice cream, it is ice cream with ambition, and the Winter Park scoop shop is where Orlando got the message. Every flavor is scratch-made and unapologetically original: Brambleberry Crisp, Brown Butter Almond Brittle, Darkest Chocolate, and the seasonal Wildberry Lavender that tastes like a spring patio. Stack them in a Buttercrisp waffle cone for a bonus pie-crust crunch, or order the flight and taste ten half-scoops at once. Once this spoils you, the grocery aisle never stands a chance.

places.name: Lazy Dog
places.address: Lazy Dog, Kissimmee, FL 34747, United States
places.description: The name is a promise Lazy Dog keeps. This warm, lodge-style spot on Irlo Bronson is the rare restaurant that treats your dog like a guest, with a dog meal on the menu and a patio firepit to lounge around. The humans get comfort food done right: Mom's Chicken Pot Pie is the signature everyone raves about, the bison burger brings a lean richness, and the bacon old fashioned brings the party. Family nights, weekend brunch, and a whole lot of welcome.

places.name: Linda's La Cantina Steakhouse
places.address: Linda's la Cantina, 4721 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4305, United States
places.description: Before Disney came to town, Linda's was already serving steaks on East Colonial, and the family still runs it like the treasure it is. The black-and-white dining room with checkered tablecloths feels like a time capsule in the best way, and the kitchen keeps the classics coming: a bacon-wrapped filet, a serious ribeye, bourbon shrimp, and a coconut custard pie to finish. Regulars swear the value beats steakhouses charging far more. Reserve ahead, dress easy, and taste seven decades of Orlando.

places.name: Maitland Social
places.address: Maitland Social, 360 E Horatio Ave, Maitland, FL 32751-4517, United States
places.description: Part food hall, part neighborhood living room, Maitland Social is where Maitland connects. The vendor lineup reads like a local all-star team: Pizza Bruno's wood-fired pies from Bruno Zacchini, Wave Sushi's viral Asian fusion creations like the sushi crunch wrap supreme, Foxtail Coffee, a Thrive cocktail lounge, and a fitness center tucked in for balance. The indoor-outdoor spaces fill with families, friends and regulars all day long. Come for one stall, stay because the whole corridor pulls you in.

places.name: Mikado
places.address: Mikado, 6417 Raleigh St, Orlando, FL 32835-5739, United States
places.description: The original Mikado in Metro West has been Orlando's sushi benchmark for over a decade, and the standard is set at the source: seafood air-shipped from Tokyo's Tsukiji market. Order the omakase and let the chefs work, or go for the signature Mikado Roll, the buttery uni toast, and a seasonal sashimi moriawase that shows off the market's freshness. Meals are prepared with visible skill right in front of you, and the fish simply tastes like it traveled well. This is where the locals go when only real sushi will do.

places.name: Paik's Noodles
places.address: Paik's Noodles, 7501 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32818-6665, United States
places.description: Tucked inside the H Mart food court on West Colonial, Paik's Noodle is the spot Korean food lovers cross town for. The handmade noodles carry the holy trinity of Korean-Chinese comfort: jjajangmyeon in rich black bean sauce, fiery jjamppong loaded with pork and seafood, and tangsuyuk, the crispy sweet-and-sour pork that never survives the ride home. The creamy shrimp and crispy steamed buns with condensed milk are the sleeper hits. Fast, authentic, and deeply satisfying.

places.name: Sea Thai Restaurant
places.address: Sea Thai Restaurant, 3812 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5208, United States
places.description: Do not let the strip-mall address fool you. Sea Thai on East Colonial is the kind of neighborhood favorite where the room glows cozy and romantic and the food keeps getting better. One dish has held a regular's heart for over a decade: the Prik King soft shell crabs with Thai fried rice. The basil fried rice with crispy duck, pineapple duck curry and shrimp toast are all worthy companions. Friendly staff, a vegan-friendly menu, and years of loyal regulars cannot be wrong.

places.name: Soulicious Vegan Kitchen
places.address: Soulicious Vegan Kitchen, 15 E 5th St, Apopka, FL 32703-5244, United States
places.description: The name is a promise and the kitchen delivers. Inside Apopka's Halls On 5th food hall, this women-owned spot serves vegan soul food with zero compromise: golden crispy fried oyster mushroom chick'n, wings tossed in hot honey or lemon pepper, jackfruit soul brisket sliders, and island jerk tacos with pineapple pico and plantains. The creamy mac and cheese and collard greens hold their own against any grandma's recipe. Comfort food that happens to be plants, and it will convert the skeptics at your table.

places.name: Sunshine Soulfood Cafe
places.address: Sunshine Soulfood Cafe, 2528 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-8009, United States
places.description: On West Colonial, Sunshine Soulfood lives up to its name, with a Caribbean twist that sets it apart. This is soul food kissed by the islands: fall-off-the-bone oxtails, jerk chicken, rasta pasta, buttery mac and cheese, collard greens and sweet plantains, all in generous portions that taste like home whether you grew up on it or not. Their own motto says every meal hits the soul, and a guest from North Carolina swore it tasted like hers. Good food, good vibes, real warmth.

places.name: Tactical Brewing Company
places.address: Tactical Brewing Company, 4882 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6628, United States
places.description: Founded by veterans in Baldwin Park, Tactical Brewing runs on what they call Strategically Chaotic Beer, and the taps prove it. Experimental sours are the house specialty: the pho-inspired Gose PhoSho, the watermelon sour, the caramel-apple Night Post, with names like Keanu Tumblereeves keeping things fun. The taproom wears Star Wars murals, keeps Super Nintendos on hand, and runs trivia nights and a run club. Serious about quality, playful about everything else, and a community hangout in the truest sense.

places.name: The Jersey Spot Pizza and Pasta
places.address: The Jersey Spot Pizza and Pasta, 1137 W Columbia Ave, Kissimmee, FL 34741-3202, United States
places.description: Kissimmee's answer to the great pizza debate wears a Garden State badge. The Jersey Spot is a small family-run joint slinging thin-crust, New Jersey-style pies with a proper fold, plus a pasta lineup that regulars rate just as highly: penne alla vodka, spaghetti and meatballs that get raved about, and garlic knots people call to die for. The wings are a sleeper hit too. Friendly staff, a clean family room, and pizza that reminds transplants of home.

places.name: The Salty Donut
places.address: The Salty Donut, 11585 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821, United States
places.description: Miami's cult donut import landed in Audubon Park and Orlando has never quite recovered. The Salty Donut treats the humble donut like fine pastry: brown butter and salt, guava and cheese, butterbeer, cherry pie, even a vegan PB and J. The coffee program is just as serious, with a cinnamon cereal milk latte that has its own candle. The Corrine Drive shop is all cute curves, dog-friendly patio, and cases that make decision-making genuinely painful.

places.name: Tikka Shack Indian Grub
places.address: Tikka Shack Indian Grub, 1500 Alafaya Trl, Oviedo, FL 32765-4517, United States
places.description: Scratch-made Indian food, minus the formality. Tikka Shack is a fast-casual kitchen on a mission to make Indian flavors approachable for everyone, and it works: tikka fries that regulars call a must-try, a tandoori chicken pizza on naan crust, chicken tikka kabob bowls, and paneer tikka biryani, all with naan that is fluffy, soft and chewy. Halal, vegan and gluten-free options cover every eater, and you set the spice level. Quick, generous, and genuinely fun.

places.name: Toll Road Brewing Company
places.address: Toll Road Brewing Company, 101 W McKey St, Ocoee, FL 34761-2616, United States
places.description: Ocoee's little taproom packs a big welcome. Toll Road Brewing keeps around twenty house beers on tap, pairing them with a steady rotation of food trucks and a calendar that never sits still: live music, music bingo, Sunday brunch with bottomless mimosas and build-your-own bloody marys, and football on the screens. The staff treats newcomers like locals even on a first visit. Small craft brewery, big-hearted hangout, and a westside evening done right.

places.name: Twenty Pho Hour
places.address: 11951 International Dr Ste B-2, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: America's first 2D noodle bar, and yes, it looks like you walked into a comic book. Twenty Pho Hour covers everything in black-and-white ink lines on International Drive, and the fun does not stop at the photos: the pho broths run rich and clean, short rib pho and crispy pork belly pho among the standouts, plus kimchi fries, Korean fire noodles and taro churro bites. Michelin Guide selected, and every corner begs for a picture.

places.name: Vivoli Il Gelato
places.address: Vivoli Il Gelato, 1780 N Buena Vista Dr, Orlando, FL 32830, United States
places.description: A piece of Florence in the middle of Disney Springs. Vivoli il Gelato is the Orlando outpost of one of the most famous gelaterias in Italy, and it tastes like it: dense, creamy, unhurried scoops made the old way, with cannoli and espresso on the menu for good measure. Between park commando runs, this is the civilized pause, a shaded seat and a cup of something perfect. One of the sweetest stops in the district, literally.

places.name: Brooklyn Water Bagel
places.address: Brooklyn Water Bagel, 9368 Narcoossee Rd, Orlando, FL 32827-5701, United States
places.description: New Yorkers in Orlando can be merciless about bagels, and Brooklyn Water Bagel answers with chemistry. The chain's whole pitch is its Brooklyn Water Works system, which Brooklynizes the local water to mimic the real thing, boiled and baked into authentic NY-style bagels. Flavors run from asiago to Black Russian, and the signature sandwiches, the Greenpoint, the Brooklyn, a proper corned beef reuben, stack deli-style. Bonus: a DIY coffee bar where you play barista. Morning crowds come early for a reason.

places.name: The Wilson
places.address: The Wilson, 225 Celebration Pl, Kissimmee, FL 34747-4601, United States
places.description: Tucked inside the Meliá Orlando Celebration, The Wilson feels like a coastal bistro that traded the ocean for a palm-framed pool. The room runs on seasonal cocktails and stone-oven pizzas, but the burgers are the quiet headline: double-patty, bacon-jam-laced, the kind you think about the next day. Ask for a table in the Backyard, where umbrellas float over the patio and the whole afternoon softens. It is the rare hotel restaurant locals claim as their own.

places.name: Island Thyme
places.address: Island Thyme, 457 Avalon Park South Blvd, Orlando, FL 32828-6700, United States
places.description: This is not a coffee shop, it is a Virgin Islands kitchen with conviction. Chef Vern Thomas, a St. Thomas native, cooks the way he grew up: jerk chicken with real fire, braised oxtail that gives up at the touch of a fork, coconut shrimp that taste like the trade winds. The dining room is fast-casual but the flavors are anything but rushed. One plate here and you will start planning your next trip to Avalon Park before you have even finished the rice.

places.name: Premium Matcha Cafe Maiko
places.address: Premium Matcha Cafe Maiko, 639 Mills Ave N, Orlando, FL 32803-4640, United States
places.description: In the middle of Mills 50, this little counter is a temple to real matcha. Not the dusty, bitter-afterthought kind: whisked-to-order lattes, silky soft serve, shaved ice stacked like fresh snow, and taiyaki fish waffles stuffed warm from the griddle. The banana pudding matcha latte sounds like a dare and drinks like a decision you will make again. Sit a minute, watch the whisk work, and let the caffeine arrive the graceful Japanese way.

places.name: Schweini's Delicatessen
places.address: Schweini's Delicatessen, 108 S Main St, Winter Garden, FL 34787-3556, United States
places.description: On Main Street in Winter Garden, owner Chris Frommeyer built the German deli of his heart: schnitzel pounded thin and breaded, stacked on pretzel rolls, layered with lingonberry compote, pickled red cabbage, and horseradish that wakes you up kindly. The Die Behrens is the order, a pork schnitzel sandwich with real swagger. German beers pour cheap and cold, soccer plays on the screens, and your dog is welcome on the patio. Come hungry, leave grinning.

places.name: Take A Sushi
places.address: 4725 W Sand Lake Rd #101, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: This one started as a small food truck with a big idea: what happens when Japan takes a date night with Latin America. The answer is the Mayorquina, a roll crowned with bright ceviche, and the Godzilla, a tempura-fried beast of a roll that refuses to be delicate. Sushi burritos roll out of the same kitchen, built fat and shareable. The vibe is sunny and unpretentious, the patio invites lingering, and every plate tastes like two dreamers proving the sky really is the limit.

places.name: Imperial Wine Bar
places.address: Imperial, 1800 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804-6415, United States
places.description: A wine bar on North Orange Avenue in Ivanhoe Village, and one of the first names locals give when the question is happy hour. The room works the way a good wine bar should — bottles open, small bites built for the table to share, and a pace that lets one drink become two. It is a top city-wide pick for happy hour and small bites, the kind of place Ivanhoe regulars treat as their default answer and visitors only find when a local points them up Orange Avenue.

places.name: Sus Hi Eatstation
places.address: Sus Hi Eatstation, 9680 Narcoossee Rd, Orlando, FL 32827-7311, United States
places.description: A ninja-themed fast-casual joint where you build your own sushi adventure, and yes, it is as fun as it sounds. Pick a roll, a bowl, or a burrito, then load it with proteins, veggies, and sauces until it is unmistakably yours. The legend here is the Fry Me A River burrito, a tempura-deep-fried sushi burrito that is crispy, juicy, and gloriously over the top. It stays open late, which makes it a lifesaver after a long night out. Feed your inner ninja.

places.name: Volcano Hot Pot & BBQ
places.address: Volcano Hot Pot & BBQ, 3279 Daniels Rd, Winter Garden, FL 34787, United States
places.description: Why choose between hot pot and Korean BBQ when one table can hold both. Volcano runs on a simple, glorious engine: an all-you-can-eat buffet of meats, seafood, and vegetables, a bubbling pot of rich broth at the center, and a grill right beside it for searing. Pick your broth, slide noodles into the depths, and cook exactly how you like it. The room hums with groups feeding off each other's joy. Come hungry, leave happy, plan two and a half hours you will not regret.

places.name: Buster's Sanford
places.address: 300 S Sanford Ave, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: Sanford's little corner of Belgium. Buster's Bistro is a Belgian beer hall at heart, with rows of Trappist ales and lambics poured in their proper glassware by people who know the difference. The food follows suit: a croque monsieur with smoked ham and gouda, curried chicken on warm baguette, frites cut thick and fried to a proper crunch. Live music spills out onto Sanford Avenue on the weekends. Settle in, order the frites, and let Belgium do the rest.

places.name: Deeply Coffee
places.address: Deeply Coffee, 111 N Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2304, United States
places.description: Downtown mornings start at Deeply, a few steps off Magnolia where the espresso runs bright and fruity. This is third-wave coffee done with real conviction: careful pour-overs, silky lattes, seasonal signatures, all pulled on serious equipment in a bright, minimalist room. The twist is the bottle shop wall of natural wines, so the same counter that wakes you up can wind you down. Dog-friendly, laptop-friendly, and quietly one of the best cups in the core.

places.name: King O Falafel
places.address: King O Falafel, 5045 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746-5345, United States
places.description: Since January 2009, this Kissimmee kitchen has been frying falafel to a deep golden crunch and grilling shawarma over real fire, and the neighborhood never left. The combination platter is the move: kifta, chicken, and lamb shawarma over saffron-kissed yellow rice with sumac and parsley. Start with the red lentil soup, end with pistachio baklava and Middle Eastern coffee. The storefront is unassuming; the flavors are not. This is the non-chain gem the attractions corridor needed.

places.name: The Current Seafood Counter-Sanford
places.address: 116 E 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: A little piece of the Northeast landed on 1st Street in Sanford, and it tastes like home for anyone who grew up near cold water. The Current runs a counter-service kitchen of responsibly sourced seafood: blackened mahi sandwiches with real char, New England lobster rolls that a transplant called the closest thing to home, clam chowder made the honest way. Relaxed, neighborhood, unfussy. Order at the counter and taste the Atlantic in Central Florida.

places.name: Bakery 1908
places.address: Bakery 1908, 12399 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32836, United States
places.description: East Colonial Drive hides one of Florida's finest Asian bakeries, and walking in feels like finding the good room. Trays of pineapple buns, pork floss buns, and the celebrated Golden Onion Roll gleam behind the glass, while the dim sum side serves dumplings and shumai worth lingering over. The boba is fresh, the space is bright and modern, and everything comes out made that day. One visit and you will understand why this place has become a small empire across Florida.

places.name: Cavo's Bar & Kitchen
places.address: Cavo's Bar & Kitchen, 900 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801-2906, United States
places.description: Thornton Park's loudest little piece of Philadelphia. Cavo's is a sports bar where Eagles fans gather and the Philly cheesesteak earns its reputation: shaved steak, molten cheese, a roll with real character. The kitchen does not stop at game-day fare though, with French onion soup, arancini, and steak tostadas sharing the menu. Wednesdays mean trivia, weekends mean crowds. Come for the game, stay because the food refuses to be ordinary.

places.name: KURA SUSHI
places.address: KURA SUSHI, 11579 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821, United States
places.description: Sushi dinner, but make it a theme park. At Kura's revolving sushi bar, plates of golden crunchy roll, sockeye salmon, and seared eel glide past on a two-level conveyor while a robot rolls your drinks to the table. Stack fifteen plates through the slot and the Bikkura Pon game dispenses a prize. The philosophy is "muten," nothing added: fresh, clean fish with no shortcuts. Dinner and a show, and the show is delicious.

places.name: Rockpit Brewing
places.address: Rockpit Brewing, 10 W Illiana St, Orlando, FL 32806-4408, United States
places.description: Orlando's neighborhood brewery wears its coal-mining theme like a favorite work jacket, and the taps rotate with small-batch brews brewed right behind the bar. The SoDo Blondin goes down easy, the red ales bring the malt, and the sours keep the adventurous happy. Live music fills the room most nights, smoked BBQ lands at your table, and the vibe is all warm wood and easy conversation. This is a taproom that feels like a second living room.

places.name: YH Seafood Clubhouse
places.address: YH Seafood Clubhouse, 8081 Turkey Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-7321, United States
places.description: The flagship of the Yummy House family does Cantonese seafood the way it deserves to be done. Dim sum carts of delicate dumplings arrive at midday, and dinner brings whole fish steamed to perfection, Peking duck carved tableside, and clay-pot dishes built for sharing. The room is elegant without being stiff, the kind of place where three generations share one round table. If you only eat one Cantonese meal in Orlando, eat it here.

places.name: Barkhaven
places.address: Barkhaven, 724 Brookhaven Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2505, United States
places.description: The one rule at BarkHaven is that your dog has as much fun as you do. This is Orlando's dog bar: a supervised off-leash park, a splash zone, on-site grooming, and a full restaurant and bar so humans can eat properly while the pups play. The kitchen goes beyond pub fare with burgers, guava wings, and a brisket bratwurst that will ruin lesser bratwursts for you. Fire pits, live DJs, and a whole community of regulars on four legs.

places.name: Beth's Burger Bar
places.address: Beth's Burger Bar, 9938 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-8702, United States
places.description: Beth Steele built the burger joint of her dreams, and it feels exactly like that: a late-night big kid's diner where you build your burger your way, from patty to the last pickle. The signature stack gets wild, with a peanut butter burger, a mac n cheese burger, and a pizza burger for the brave. Board games on the shelves, bingo nights on the calendar, fridges stocked with beer. It is playful, it is loud, and the burgers deliver.

places.name: Blue Amphora
places.address: Blue Amphora, 1461 N Goldenrod Rd, Orlando, FL 32807-8301, United States
places.description: No official site or reputable profile could be found for this one, so walk in with an open mind and an appetite for discovery. The name promises something Vietnamese, and if the kitchen delivers the fundamentals, look for the things that make this cuisine sing: broths simmered to depth, herbs that hit like a bright green chord, grilled pork with proper char. When a place flies under the radar, the regulars usually know something you do not, and finding it is half the fun.

places.name: Burger Vault
places.address: Burger Vault, 520 W State Road 436, Altamonte Springs, FL 32714-4000, United States
places.description: A halal burger spot on 436 that treats the burger like a craft. Everything starts with handcrafted halal beef, cooked exactly how you want it, and builds from there. The Volcano Burger brings the heat with chili volcano sauce and jalapenos, the Mozza Melt stacks fried mozzarella with mushrooms and house sauce, and the shakes, including a pistachio one, cool everything down. Open late, served fresh, and built for anyone who believes a burger should never be an afterthought.

places.name: Corner Chophouse
places.address: Corner Chophouse, 558 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4125, United States
places.description: Just off Park Avenue, the Corner Chophouse does steaks the old way and everything else the fun way. Dry-aged cuts land with fluffy milk bread and salted European butter, cocktails pour strong, and the dessert trolley rolls through like a promise. The room is warm and lively, the kind of place where a night stretches longer than planned. Classic in all the right ways, never afraid to bend the rules. This is Winter Park coming to cut loose.

places.name: The Current Seafood Counter
places.address: The Current Seafood Counter, 2425 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-5303, United States
places.description: A Northeast-style seafood counter in the heart of historic downtown Sanford, The Current keeps it simple: fresh, responsibly sourced seafood, counter-service ease, and the kind of honest cooking that made New England transplants homesick. The blackened mahi sandwich is a Sanford legend in the making, the clam chowder tastes like a weekend up north, and the lobster roll needs no translation. Go hungry, leave converted.

places.name: 480N Wine Bar
places.address: 480 N Orlando Ave Ste 133, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Reborn from Flutes Champagne Bar, 480N is Winter Park Village's modern wine bar: a darker, lounge-style room pouring wines, wine cocktails and beer, with music in the mix. It leans later and looser than its champagne-bar past — a nightcap spot as much as a celebration spot.

places.name: Hot Asian Buns
places.address: 204 S Sanford Ave, Sanford, FL
places.description: Central Florida's favorite food truck finally got a roof, and Sanford is better for it. Every bao here is handmade from scratch, steamed to pillowy perfection, and filled with flavors that cross borders: Korean fried chicken with gochujang and sesame slaw, beef bulgogi with kimchi, lacquered pork belly with hoisin and peanut powder. Add an order of loaded kimchi fries. The buns are the kind you think about for days, and now you know exactly where to find them.

places.name: Jerkman BBQ
places.address: Jerkman BBQ, 6408 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32818, United States
places.description: Jamaican fire meets smokehouse soul. Jerkman has spent a decade perfecting the marriage of jerk seasoning and slow BBQ, and the results speak for themselves: fall-off-the-bone ribs with real char, jerk chicken that drips with flavor, and jerk fries that people come back for on their own. The honey garlic wings and creamy mac and cheese round out a plate built for serious appetites. This is comfort food with island swagger, served hot and fast.

places.name: Lake Meadow Naturals
places.address: Lake Meadow Naturals, 10000 Mark Adam Rd, Ocoee, FL 34761-3246, United States
places.description: Ten miles outside Orlando, this family farm has been raising chickens, ducks, goats, and grass-fed cattle since 2004, and the farm store sells everything straight from the source. Come for the cage-free eggs you can pick yourself on Saturdays, stay for the heritage pork, grass-fed beef, raw milk, honey, and artisan cheeses. Everything here tastes like the real thing because it is the real thing. A working farm, not a petting zoo, and all the better for it.

places.name: Lineage Coffee Roasting
places.address: Lineage Coffee Roasting, 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2224, United States
places.description: In 2012, husband-and-wife team Jarrett and Justine started roasting in Orlando with a retrofitted grill and an ice cream motor, and the coffee was, by their own admission, terrible. Look at them now. Lineage roasts small, hand-picked lots, cups and dials in every coffee, and teaches you the craft while you drink it through the Lineage Academy. Three locations across the city, from East End Market to Mills/50, and every cup tastes like the work of people who never stopped learning.

places.name: Nuri's
places.address: Nuri's, 63 E Pine St, Orlando, FL 32801-2617, United States
places.description: Downtown Orlando finally got a proper tavern-style pizza joint, and Nuri's does it the right way: cracker-crisp, paper-thin crust, party-cut into squares you cannot stop grabbing. The pepperoni and jalapeno pie with chili crisp and homemade ranch drizzle is a certified banger, and the vodka pizza converts skeptics. Pinball machines, sports on the projectors, pistachio soft serve for the finish. Come with friends, order too much, leave happy.

places.name: Qreate Coffee
places.address: 1212 Woodward St #1, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Tucked off Mills on Woodward Street, Qreate is half coffee lab, half creative studio, and fully one of the district's best kept secrets. The menu is a playground: Crème Brûlée Lattes, Purple Pearl ube creations, Tiger Lattes with house brown sugar, and seasonal specials that rotate like a gallery show. The Korean cream cheese garlic bread is dangerously good. Quiet corners, plenty of outlets, a photo studio in back. Come to create, stay for the second cup.

places.name: Sourdough Bread House
places.address: Sourdough Bread House, 5761 US-17-92, Casselberry, FL 32707-3819, United States
places.description: In a Casselberry strip mall sits a Turkish love story told in sourdough. Husband-and-wife team Euhan and Hulya built this café around slow-fermented loaves so good that people drive hours for a fresh round. Stay for the Turkish breakfast: menemen with soudjouk sausage, olives, cheeses, and proper Turkish coffee served with delight. Every plate comes with thick slices of that legendary bread. It is a hidden gem, a neighborhood treasure, and one of the best breakfasts in Central Florida.

places.name: Sullivans Public House
places.address: Sullivans Public House, 116 E 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771-1325, United States
places.description: Sanford's slice of Dublin sits on 1st Street with hand-carved woodwork, dim light, and a Guinness pour people cross town for. Live Irish and Scottish music fills the room on weekends, and the kitchen backs it up with proper pub classics: shepherd's pie, fish and chips, a meatloaf sandwich on soda bread, scotch eggs, and a whiskey list worth lingering over. Whether you came for the music, the pints, or both, you will be glad you came.

places.name: Walala Hand-Pulled Noodle House
places.address: 5062 W Colonial Dr #120, Orlando, FL 32808
places.description: In the heart of the Chinatown plaza, a father-daughter team pulls Lanzhou noodles by hand behind a glass wall, and dinner becomes a show. The clear beef broth simmers with patience, the noodles land with perfect chew, and the braised beef short rib version is the bowl people dream about. Pan-fried dumplings and buns fill out the table, and yes, noodle refills are free. Michelin noticed this one. So will you.

places.name: Wunderbar
places.address: Wunderbar, 4200 Conroy Rd, Orlando, FL 32839-2400, United States
places.description: Do not come looking for cocktails, the name is a beautiful lie. WunderBAR is a family-owned superfood cafe in the Mall of Millenia food court, and it pours pure sunshine: cold-pressed juices, protein-packed smoothies, acai bowls, pitaya bowls, and coconut bowls built fresh to order. The tropical bowls with mango, pineapple, and chia pudding taste like a beach day. It is the healthiest pit stop in the whole mall, and the service is as bright as the menu.

places.name: Bagel King Bakery
places.address: Bagel King Bakery, 668 Kennedy Blvd W, Orlando, FL 32810-6255, United States
places.description: Behind many of Central Florida's best breakfast sandwiches is this bakery. Bagel King bakes more than twenty types of bagels every day from its Orlando plant, plus homemade danish, muffins, croissants, and specialty breads that supply delis and cafes across the region. It is a wholesale operation with family roots, and the bagels carry the kind of chew and shine that says they were made by people who care. If you have had a great bagel in town lately, there is a good chance it started here.

places.name: Cafe 34 Istanbul
places.address: Cafe 34 Istanbul, 8255 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-9326, United States
places.description: Named for Istanbul's area code, this International Drive cafe brings Turkey to Orlando with real heart. The grill runs hot with lamb adana kebabs, chicken shish, and lamb chops people rave about, while the baklava and rice pudding handle the sweet side. Ornately authentic hookahs shipped straight from Turkey fill the lounge with fragrance and calm. Finish with Turkish tea or coffee served the traditional way. Late-night, lively, and full of life.

places.name: Parva
places.address: Parva, 220 W Lake Mary Blvd, Sanford, FL 32773-5925, United States
places.description: Colombia has a word for this kind of place: a parva is a bakery, and this one does the homeland proud. The Sanford shop bakes pan de bono, buñuelos, and pan con queso fresh through the day, cheesy and golden and impossible to eat just one of. The café con leche is done the proper Colombian way, and the kitchen keeps going with calentados, churrasco, and cachapa pabellon for lunch. It smells like nostalgia and tastes like family.

places.name: Red Eye Sports Tavern
places.address: 855 E State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: This is Orlando's only moonshine-themed sports tavern, and it commits to the bit beautifully. Premium flavored moonshine from the folks on the Moonshiners TV show anchors the bar, alongside craft cocktails, cold beer, and a serious BBQ menu. The rustic industrial room runs on big screen TVs, pool tables, darts, ping pong, and weekly live music. Part sports bar, part music venue, part neighborhood party, all good energy.

places.name: Shaka Donuts
places.address: 2641 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: In the Hourglass District, Shaka makes donuts to order, and the difference is not subtle. These are fluffy, oversized rings of joy: maple bacon for the sweet-savory believers, banana pudding for the dreamers, Boston cream for the traditionalists. The breakfast sandwich served inside a glazed donut is a power move. Coffee is good, the shop is sunny, and locals will tell you these are some of the best donuts in town. Believe them.

places.name: Charlie's Bakery
places.address: Charlie's Bakery, 3213 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: Charlie's has been feeding Orlando since 1971, and half a century of mornings has made it an institution on Curry Ford. The bakery case does legendary cakes, éclairs, cupcakes, and those famous Parker House rolls, but the plot twist is the super-premium ice cream churned in-house: dense, rich, and award-winning, with rotating flavors like the Sunshine State lemon strawberry swirl that won the Orlando Sentinel's 150th Scoop contest. A true neighborhood treasure.

places.name: Ispirazione
places.address: Ispirazione, 1711 Amazing Way, Ocoee, FL 34761-3279, United States
places.description: Tucked away on Amazing Way in Ocoee, Ispirazione is one of those hidden gems you have to know about. The specialty is tigelle: small round Italian breads baked fresh to order, crunchy outside and soft inside, loaded with creamy burrata, prosciutto, mortadella, and imported Italian ingredients. The Deliziosa and Bella Vita are local favorites, and the pistachio tiramisu makes a worthy finish. Genuine Italian soul, hiding in plain sight.

places.name: Marketplace at Avalon Park
places.address: Marketplace at Avalon Park, 3801 Avalon Park East Blvd, Orlando, FL 32828, United States
places.description: Downtown Avalon Park has its own food hall, and it functions as the neighborhood's living room. Over 8,000 square feet hold nine eatery bays, a general store, a brewery taproom, and a sit-down restaurant and bar, all built around local chefs, artisans, and makers. Regular events and live entertainment keep the energy high. Bring the whole crew and let everyone eat what they actually want.

places.name: Shakers American Cafe
places.address: Shakers American Cafe, 1308 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-6351, United States
places.description: There is no such thing as a quiet breakfast at Shakers. The cozy College Park cottage hums around walls crowded with thousands of salt-and-pepper shakers donated by regulars since 1993, and the room feels like a neighborhood clubhouse that happens to serve the cinnamon roll pancakes Orlando dreams about. Order them, fluffy and glazed with that familiar cinnamon swirl, or go savory with an omelet and the potato pancake regulars swear by. Friendly, old-school, and gone by midafternoon. That is the deal, and it is a good one.

places.name: Theo's Kitchen
places.address: Theo's Kitchen, 2952 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: Theo's Kitchen pulls off the rare double act. A family-owned Mediterranean spot on Curry Ford for more than 25 years, where the gyro platter comes stacked and the tzatziki tastes genuinely homemade, and it also serves the fried chicken people call the best in Orlando. Crispy, golden, the kind of bird that reminds you what fried chicken is supposed to be. One visit and you understand the line. Greeks eat here. Southerners eat here. Everybody leaves planning their return.

places.name: Winter Park Biscuit Company
places.address: Winter Park Biscuit Company, 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2224, United States
places.description: Tucked inside East End Market, Winter Park Biscuit Company runs on a simple dare: everything is vegan, and nobody will believe it. The oat-buttermilk biscuits are flaky, golden, and gone in minutes, and the crispy chick sandwich has converted more skeptics than any sermon. Even the biscuits and gravy lands, rich and peppery, and the hibiscus lemonade cuts through it all like sunshine. This is comfort food that never announces its virtue, it just tastes like the South at its best.

places.name: Happy Snapper Seafood Restaurant
places.address: Happy Snapper Seafood Restaurant, 6327 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32809-5109, United States
places.description: Drive past the strip mall on South Orange and you would never know. Inside, Happy Snapper is the kind of tiny, family-run seafood joint locals quietly defend like a secret: the deep fried whole snapper arrives crackling and golden, the blue crab bisque is the color of a Florida sunset, and the dilled yuca and potatoes have a small cult following of their own. No white tablecloths, no view, just seafood cooked by people who care. Scott Joseph himself swung by and walked away impressed. That tells you plenty.

places.name: The Spice Indian Grill
places.address: The Spice Indian Grill, 4498 Alafaya Trl N, Orlando, FL 32817, United States
places.description: Near UCF, Spice Indian Grill has quietly become the neighborhood's Indian go-to. The lunch buffet lets you graze through the classics, chicken tikka masala, saag, crispy gobi manchurian, and that garlic naan that keeps coming until you say stop. The food is not Americanized, regulars note the heat is honest, so ask questions and trust the staff. Cool off with a mango lassi and finish with the sugar-dusted dough balls. Comforting, generous, and priced for a student crowd.

places.name: TORCHY'S TACOS
places.address: TORCHY'S TACOS, 11757 Daryl Carter Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-4002, United States
places.description: Born in an Austin food trailer and now a Texas-sized chain, Torchy's lands in Orlando with its swagger fully intact. The tacos are the event: the Trailer Park, a hillbilly-fried-chicken affair, Mr. Orange with salmon, Hellfire with jerk pork and a dipping sauce that means business. Start with the Threesome, green chile queso plus guac and salsa, because skipping the queso is a rookie mistake. Garage-vibe room, full bar with real margaritas, counter ordering that keeps things moving. Loud, fun, unapologetic.

places.name: Fun-Ko's Poke Bowls and Asian Snacks
places.address: Fun-Ko's Poke Bowls and Asian Snacks, 334 N Donnelly St, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5525, United States
places.description: In a region of drive-thrus, Fun-Ko's is a small joy: a tucked-away poke counter inside Mount Dora Marketplace where the fish is fresh, the bowls are generous, and the owner treats first-timers like regulars. Build your own from tuna, salmon, shrimp or tofu, or go signature with the Classic Hawaiian or the spicy Funko Fire. Adventurous? Try the jellyfish salad or grab onigiri for the road. Quiet courtyard seating, zero fuss, and the kind of wholesome freshness that makes you a monthly visitor without noticing.

places.name: The Smoothie Room
places.address: The Smoothie Room, 25 W Crystal Lake St, Orlando, FL 32806-4403, United States
places.description: SoDo's answer to the sugar-bomb smoothie chain is this bright little room where nothing comes from a powder, a concentrate, or a pump. The Bahama Mama and Berry Dose are made fresh on the spot, thick with real fruit, and the PB Falcon acai bowl is the move when you want something with substance. Wheatgrass shots, ginger shots, cold-pressed juices, all of it in a space that feels calm on purpose. Locals swear this is the best smoothie in Orlando. One sip and the argument is over.

places.name: Zorba's Kitchen
places.address: Zorba's Kitchen, 7325 Lake Underhill Rd, Orlando, FL 32822-6061, United States
places.description: The name Zorba means live each day with passion, and the little Greek kitchen on Lake Underhill takes it literally. Walk in and it feels like a corner of Greece, warm, family-run, everything from scratch. The lamb gyro is the order that converts people, tender meat on soft doughy pita, but regulars know the skepasti: lamb, peppers, fries and feta piled on crispy pita. Finish with baklava cheesecake. Scott Joseph found the owner greeting guests between stints at the stove. That is the whole place in one gesture.

places.name: Bruno's Oysters
places.address: Bruno's Oysters, 426 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787, United States
places.description: Tucked into the Barrel Room at Plant St Market, Bruno's is a small seafood temple with big convictions. The oyster selection turns over daily, East and West coast varieties shucked to order, served with a watermelon-serrano mignonette that should probably be bottled. Beyond the shell: Oysters Rockefeller with Pernod and gruyere, a duck confit grilled cheese, roasted bone marrow, a lobster roll worth crossing town for. Grab a Crooked Can pint next door and settle in. Cozy, moody, and made for lingering.

places.name: Cress Restaurant
places.address: Cress Restaurant, 103 W Indiana Ave, DeLand, FL 32720-4209, United States
places.description: Worth the drive to historic downtown DeLand: Cress is a farm-to-table restaurant built on the radical idea that a chef should know the farmer, the dairyman, and the fisherman by name. The globally inspired menu follows Florida's seasons, so the kitchen works with whatever the land is offering right now, and the staff talk about the food like they grew up with it. Zagat named it a top Orlando restaurant, and it earned it. Refined without stiffness, serious without a lecture. DeLand's quiet fine-dining crown jewel.

places.name: Death in the Afternoon
places.address: Death in the Afternoon, 930 Mills Ave N, Orlando, FL 32803-3230, United States
places.description: Named for Hemingway's famous absinthe-and-champagne toast, Death in the Afternoon is Mills 50's moody shrine to the green fairy. From the crew behind Sanford's Suffering Bastard, this dim little room pours absinthes from around the world and builds cocktails with the confidence of people who take the spirit seriously. The Sauterelle tastes like mint chocolate chip ice cream with a swagger. Not feeling absinthe? The Spanish-leaning kitchen has you with patatas brava, grilled octopus, and a chorizo burger. Date-night dark in the best way.

places.name: Donutste Family Bakery
places.address: 605 Crescent Executive Ct Ste 120, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Donutste is proof that the best donuts in Central Florida contain no butter, milk, or eggs. Chefs Shalom and Victoria run this family-owned, plant-based Lake Mary shop like a labor of love, and the donuts show it: bouncy, not-too-sweet yeast rings in flavors like ube cinnamon roll, red velvet, and strawberry shortcake. FOX News called them the best around, and regulars preorder because quantities are small and sellouts are real. Bright, welcoming, and quietly miraculous. You will not believe they are vegan until you finish the box.

places.name: El Coqui Ninja Restaurant
places.address: El Coqui Ninja Restaurant, 3097 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-3301, United States
places.description: Only in Orlando: a restaurant where mofongo meets lo mein and it works. El Coqui Ninja fuses Puerto Rican soul with Asian comfort on Curry Ford Road, and the menu reads like a dare, cuerno beef eggrolls, crab rangoon, pepper steak beside roast pork mofongo with shrimp. Sip a sake margarita or fresh passion fruit juice while you decide. The room is quirky and cozy, flowered couches, projector boxes at the tables, spotless and welcoming. Come hungry, come curious, and let the island-ninja mashup do its thing.

places.name: GG Korean BBQ
places.address: GG Korean BBQ, 5319 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32808-7607, United States
places.description: Pine Hills hides one of the great KBBQ nights in Orlando. GG runs on real charcoal and open flame, and the all-you-can-eat format means you grill your way through LA galbi, marinated short ribs, pork belly, and beef tongue at your own pace while the banchan keeps coming. Do not skip the corn cheese or the steaming bowl of gyeran-jjim egg. The room is big, the staff attentive, and the whole thing has the festive energy of a cookout where nobody is in a rush. Charcoal makes the difference. You will taste it.

places.name: Hourglass Brewing
places.address: Hourglass Brewing, 2500 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-2506, United States
places.description: Hourglass started in 2012 as two friends brewing on a back patio, and the spirit never left. The Curry Ford District taproom pours in a former church building with more than 40 rotating house beers, everything all-natural, the beer names gloriously unhinged. This is a nerdy brewery in the best way: video game vibes, an NES corner, trivia nights, a crowd that genuinely loves craft beer. Formerly Florida Brewery of the Year. Order a flight, settle into the long bar, and let the room's good humor do the rest. Independent to the bone.

places.name: J'Adore the French Bakery
places.address: J'Adore the French Bakery, 910 Sand Lake Rd, Altamonte Springs, FL 32714-7053, United States
places.description: Behind an unassuming Altamonte Springs storefront, Sophia and Teddy Dumoulin are baking some of the most serious French pastry in Central Florida. The flour comes from France. The croissants crackle, flaky on the outside, honeycombed inside, the way laminated dough is supposed to behave. The bacon twist is a braided marvel, the baguettes toothsome, the canele and almond chocolate croissants worth a special trip. Even the Orlando Sentinel took notice. Small room, a few tables, and pastries made with patience and love. This is the real thing, not a theme.

places.name: Jinya Ramen Bar
places.address: Jinya Ramen Bar, 8 N Summerlin Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2930, United States
places.description: JINYA's whole philosophy fits in a pot: broths simmered for 20 hours, in-house, the slow way. The Thornton Park room is sleek and lively, the kind of place built for a noisy table of friends, and the bowls earn their reputation. The Tonkotsu Black with garlic chips and garlic oil is the purist's pick, the Spicy Creamy Vegan Ramen converts skeptics, and the JINYA Bun, slow-braised pork chashu in a steamed bun with kewpie mayo, is one of the better buns in Orlando. Ramen done with patience. You can taste the hours.

places.name: Kamayan Grill
places.address: Kamayan Grill, 7868 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34747-1738, United States
places.description: Filipino food is made for sharing, and Kamayan Grill in Kissimmee treats that as a promise. This family-run spot serves the traditional favorites with real conviction: crispy pata, sizzling sisig, adobo, kare-kare with thick peanut sauce, and halo-halo to finish. Order a bilao and the whole table eats like royalty. The room is cozy and welcoming, with live music and karaoke some nights plus an in-house bakery turning out Filipino breads and desserts. Filipino hospitality is not a slogan here. It is the whole experience.

places.name: Lighthouse Seafood
places.address: Lighthouse Seafood, 101 N Country Club Rd, Lake Mary, FL 32746, United States
places.description: Lighthouse is two experiences in one building: a proper seafood market stacked with the day's catch and a cafe that cooks it how you like. Steamed crab legs, grilled swordfish, stone crab, royal reds, the kind of spread that makes deciding the hardest part. Regulars rave about the clam chowder and will fight you over the key lime pie, whole pie to go is the pro move. Friendly staff, honest food, and the freshest seafood many diners say they have ever had. Part market, part restaurant, all worth it.

places.name: Moa Kai Hawaiian Diner
places.address: Moa Kai Hawaiian Diner, 2217 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4911, United States
places.description: Hawaiian diner food is rare in Orlando, which is exactly why Moa Kai on Colonial Drive has a line. The room fuses retro diner comfort with island soul: loco moco, shoyu chicken plate lunches, garlic shrimp, and a garlic shrimp po boy people cross town for. The deep-fried Spam musubi is the conversion experience. Save room for malasadas and the ube haupia pie, and wash it down with POG juice. Owner Hoi Nguyen named it for the moa, Hawaii's beloved feral chickens. Bold, balanced, unfussy. Pure aloha, no plane ticket required.

places.name: Nan and Pop's Ice Cream Shop
places.address: Nan and Pop's Ice Cream Shop, 351 N Ronald Reagan Blvd, Longwood, FL 32750-4159, United States
places.description: Nan and Pop's feels like the neighborhood parlor every town wishes it had. The Longwood shop serves the classics done right, sundaes, banana splits, thick milkshakes, but the signatures are the bubble waffle cones, warm, crisp-edged, and made for Instagram before they disappear, and flavors like red velvet and the Butterscotch Bomb. Monthly special sundaes keep the regulars curious, and the staff treats every kid like the most important person in the room. Friendly, old-fashioned, and sweet in every sense.

places.name: Papi Smash'd Burger
places.address: Papi Smash'd Burger, 66 E Pine St, Orlando, FL 32801-2616, United States
places.description: On East Pine, Papi Smash'd does one thing with total conviction: smash burgers with a Latin soul. The patties hit the griddle hard, lacy crispy edges, juicy centers, and the Papi's OG double beef is the downtown benchmark. The menu winks at home with Papi Chulo and Papi's Big Mak, and the yuca fries are the side you did not know you needed. Passion fruit lemonade, cookies and cream shakes, and a full vegetarian lineup so nobody sits out. Loud, proud, and exactly what a downtown burger joint should be.

places.name: Quigley Coffee
places.address: Quigley Coffee, 1730 Rinehart Rd, Sanford, FL 32771-6590, United States
places.description: Quigley started as a mobile coffee cart and grew into one of Sanford's most beloved coffee shops, and the personality came with it. The room is playful and bright, full of plants, with a skate shop tucked in the back. The drink menu rewards curiosity: seasonal creations like the Smokey Bokey, the Florida Boi, and the Bear Hug, an all-time favorite. Grab the Jammy Sammy with its habanero bacon jam if you want breakfast done right. Service is warm, wifi is free, and the vibe says stay awhile. Support local, sip something fun.

places.name: Red Panda Noodle
places.address: Red Panda Noodle, Orlando, FL 32801, United States
places.description: Parked at the downtown food hall, Red Panda Noodle is a food truck with fine-dining DNA. The founders earned a Michelin nod at Orlando Meats before deciding to pull noodles instead, and it shows: hand-pulled biang biang noodles with chewy swagger, a spicy chicken katsu that shatters, bourbon-spiked chicken in a velvety sauce, and the Goomba for vegans, mushrooms and mustard greens kicked up with black vinegar. Orlando Weekly readers named it Best Food Truck. The portions are generous, the sauces are house-made, and every bowl eats like a dare. Slurp loudly.

places.name: Sal's Pizza Bar
places.address: Sal's Pizza Bar, 11020 Daryl Carter Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32836, United States
places.description: Real New York pizza in Florida is a debate that never ends, but Sal's has strong opinions on the matter. Sal came to Orlando via Italy and the Bronx, and his family-owned bar turns out proper Brooklyn-style pies: the vodka burrata with creamy fresh burrata melting over hot crust, a beloved grandpa slice, and garlic knots glistening with fresh garlic, parsley, and pecorino. The crust is chewy with bite, the sauce is on point, and Sal himself is often behind the counter. That personal touch is what elevates a slice joint to a neighborhood institution.

places.name: Wine 4 Oysters
places.address: Wine 4 Oysters, 1957 Alafaya Trl S, Orlando, FL 32828-8732, United States
places.description: The name tells you the pairing strategy: wine, oysters, and the happy marriage between them. Wine 4 Oysters is a neighborhood gem out in East Orlando run by two people who have spent over a decade traveling the world in search of oyster preparations. The menu reads like a passport: Brest oysters from France, steamed oysters from Japan, spicy Hong Kong style, Oysters Rockefeller, caviar-topped, each with a suggested wine. Raw, baked, or broiled, the oysters are fresh and the room is romantic. A date-night find worth the drive.

places.name: Ziggie's Pizza
places.address: Ziggie's Pizza, 603 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-1844, United States
places.description: Ziggie's is the kind of pizza place built for people who get excited about menus. In Ivanhoe Village, attached to the Thirsty Topher craft beer bar, this tiny shop turns out thin-crust 12-inch personal pies with joyful, offbeat toppings. The Killa Beez, fig jam, prosciutto, pepperoni, goat cheese, and house-made hot honey, is the cult favorite. Ziggie's Stardust piles on pistachio pesto and truffle oil. Order at the counter, then settle at the bar with a Florida-brewed pint while it bakes. Small, playful, and fiercely loved.

places.name: Dezerland Park Orlando
places.address: 5250 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Rain or shine, Dezerland delivers the most fun per square foot on I-Drive. This 850,000-square-foot indoor wonderland packs in over 20 attractions: Florida's longest indoor go-kart track, glow-in-the-dark mini golf, bowling, laser tag, axe throwing, a massive trampoline park, and the state's biggest arcade and pinball palace. The crown jewel is the Orlando Auto Museum, over 2,000 vehicles including Batmobiles, the Ecto-1, and the world's largest James Bond collection. Entry is free, you only pay to play. A full day, air-conditioned, no reservations needed.

places.name: Fun Spot America
places.address: 5700 Fun Spot Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The anti-theme-park theme park, and locals love it for exactly that. Fun Spot is family-owned since 1997, and it delivers big thrills without the big gates: White Lightning, Orlando's first wooden roller coaster, Freedom Flyer, the suspended coaster, four go-kart tracks, and the SkyCoaster slingshot. No admission gate games, no two-hour waits, just pay, ride, repeat. It is the place Orlando families actually go when they want a coaster day, and it feels like the classic American midway the mega-parks left behind.

places.name: Orlando Watersports Complex
places.address: 8615 Florida Rock Rd, Orlando, FL 32824
places.description: Orlando is the wakeboarding capital of the world, and this is its proving ground. The Orlando Watersports Complex runs two full-size cableways, the only facility in the country with that setup, plus traditional boat pulls behind Nautique boats. Pros train here year-round, and so can you: the staff teaches complete beginners all the way to competition riders. Never ridden? The beginner cable is made for first-timers, and the staff is genuinely motivated to get you up. The feeling of your first clean lap is one you will chase forever.

places.name: Crayola Experience
places.address: 8001 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Inside The Florida Mall hides 70,000 square feet of pure color. The Crayola Experience is a hands-on wonderland for kids, over 25 stations where children name and wrap their own crayon with the resident Crayonologist, watch crayons being made in a live show, melt wax into shapes, sculpt with Model Magic, and climb a two-story color playground. The world's largest Crayola crayon, 15 feet long, is the obligatory photo stop. Air-conditioned, self-paced, and built for ages three to ten. The perfect rainy-day rescue from the theme park grind.

places.name: Andretti Indoor Karting and Games
places.address: 9299 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A 150,000-square-foot indoor racing and games hall on Universal Boulevard, named for Mario Andretti and built around electric go-karts that run 35 mph on multiple indoor tracks. Around the racing: two-level laser tag, 120 arcade games, boutique bowling, VR bays, F1 simulators, and a ropes course with curved ziplines. A restaurant and full bar sit inside, and the walls carry racing memorabilia. It is I-Drive's default answer for a rainy afternoon, a birthday party, or a group that wants competition with air conditioning.

places.name: Nona Adventure Park
places.address: 14086 Centerline Drive, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: This is where Lake Nona goes to play hooky.
