Nona Adventure Park turns a lake into a full-contact playground: a sprawling inflatable aqua park you bounce, climb, and wipe out across, a cable park for wakeboarders of every level, and a sixty-foot climbing tower with ropes courses and rock walls for the vertically ambitious. Refuel at Splashes Bar & Grill, catch the sunset over the water, and come back for karaoke nights and live music. Few places in Orlando wear you out this happily.

places.name: WonderWorks Orlando
places.address: 9067 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: You cannot miss it: the upside-down house on I-Drive, a top-secret laboratory supposedly flung out of the Bermuda Triangle by a tornado experiment gone awry. Since 1998, WonderWorks has been Orlando's best rainy-day rescue, an amusement park for the mind with over 100 hands-on exhibits. Feel 74-mph winds in the hurricane shack, ride out an earthquake, climb the glow-in-the-dark ropes course, battle in laser tag, and cross the inversion tunnel that flips your world right-side up. Science you can touch, and kids absolutely eat it up.

places.name: Peppa Pig Theme Park Florida
places.address: 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: Small riders grip the bar on Daddy Pig's Roller Coaster, splash through muddy puddles, then run straight back for another short line. Peppa Pig Theme Park in Winter Haven, next to LEGOLAND, is built for ages 2 to 6 with gentle rides, live shows, and Certified Autism Center support. This is a first-park day done right — go early, move at toddler pace, and leave before the meltdown hour. Tourist Trail: Worth it for preschoolers — skip it if your youngest is past Peppa.

places.name: Legoland Florida
places.address: 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: Winter Haven's LEGOLAND is the theme park for kids who build. Opened in 2011 on the historic Cypress Gardens grounds, the resort packs over 50 rides, shows, and attractions aimed squarely at ages two to twelve: The Dragon coaster in LEGO Kingdoms, Ninjago rides, the LEGO Movie World, and Miniland USA, where millions of bricks recreate American landmarks. Add the water park and SEA LIFE aquarium for a full multi-day trip. Shorter lines, gentler thrills, and imagination everywhere. The perfect first big theme park.

places.name: Dinosaur World
places.address: 5145 Harvey Tew Rd, Plant City, FL 33565
places.description: Out in Plant City, Dinosaur World is the kind of roadside classic Florida does best. Over 200 life-size dinosaurs spread across 20 shaded acres, arranged in species groups so real some visitors swear they see movement in the trees. Kids dig for fossils, pan for gems, crack geodes, and excavate a life-size Stegosaurus at the Boneyard. A giant T-Rex greets you at the gate, and yes, the whole place is dog-friendly. Unpretentious, educational, and a slow wander through prehistory. A genuinely good half-day for dino-obsessed kids.

places.name: Wild Florida
places.address: 3301 Lake Cypress Rd, Kenansville, FL 34739
places.description: Forty-five minutes from the theme parks, Central Florida turns genuinely wild. Wild Florida sits at the Headwaters of the Everglades, where airboats skim 4,200 acres of protected marshes and the captain points out gators sunning on logs and hawks circling overhead. Back on land, the 15-acre gator park holds over 200 native and exotic animals with feeding demos, and the drive-thru safari lets you feed zebras and bison from your own car. Equal parts wildlife encounter and old-Florida adventure. This is the side of the state the coasters never show you.

places.name: Knight Library
places.address: 11448 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: UCF's legendary college bar sits on University Boulevard directly across from campus, and it runs on a simple formula: cheap drinks, a big patio, and DJ nights that pull the whole student crowd across the street. This is not a craft-cocktail room and does not pretend to be — it is the loud, easy, everybody-you-know-is-here kind of bar that defines a college town's nightlife, priced for a student budget and built for groups spilling out onto the patio.

places.name: On Tap
places.address: 10028 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: A casual bar on University Boulevard in the heart of UCF country, built for the student playbook: games on, prices low, and a crowd that builds as the night goes on. On Tap is the no-decisions stop on the boulevard — walk in with a group, order drinks that do not dent a student budget, and let the games and the late-night crowd carry the evening. It knows exactly what it is, and on this stretch of east Orlando, that is the job.

places.name: Aero Rooftop Bar & Lounge
places.address: 60 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A rooftop nightclub above North Orange Avenue, where the dance floor comes with the downtown skyline as its backdrop. Aero runs on house and EDM DJs and laser shows — the full open-air club package stacked on top of the city's bar district. The elevation changes the energy: the same downtown crowd, but dancing over the rooftops instead of inside them, and on a clear night the view does half the decorating before the lasers even warm up.

places.name: Tier Nightclub
places.address: 20 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown's big-room statement: a high-energy, multi-level nightclub on East Central Boulevard built around scale — skyboxes looking down on the floor, bottle service for groups that want a base camp, and EDM and dance music driving the main room. Tier is where the night goes when a bar stops being enough. Dress for a club, expect a club, and let the skyline outside the windows remind you this is still Orlando underneath the bass.

places.name: Euphoria Downtown
places.address: 110 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A downtown nightclub on South Orange Avenue with a split personality: brunch spot by day, techno room by night. Euphoria hosts the Techno Euphoria nights on a big sound system, which tells you where its heart is — this end of Orange Avenue is mostly bars and bottle-service clubs, and this is the address for people who came for the music itself. Come for the DJs over the bottle sparklers, and know the room takes its sound seriously.

places.name: Aura Night Club
places.address: 49 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: An LED-lit dance floor on North Orange Avenue, right in the spine of downtown's club row. Aura splits its programming between EDM and hip-hop, with local and touring DJs trading nights, so the room's personality shifts with the booking — check who is playing and you will know what kind of night it is. What does not change: the lights, the volume, and a floor that fills with the downtown crowd that came to dance rather than be seen.

places.name: Yaz Orlando
places.address: 114 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A restaurant, lounge, and nightlife spot sharing one address on North Orange Avenue — three gears in a single downtown room. Yaz runs dinner first, then shifts: the lights drop, the sound comes up, and the lounge becomes the night. Its own description promises shadows, sound, and eclectic flavor, which is a fair summary of the appeal — one stop on the Orange Avenue strip that can take a group from a meal to a night out without anyone moving the car.

places.name: The Burrow Cafe and Play
places.address: 618 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A parent-friendly cafe and bar where kids get a supervised indoor playground and adults get serious coffee, wine, beer, and cocktails. Order the signature Honey Badger latte, settle in for remote work during the day, come back for Monday trivia, or book a birthday party.

places.name: SeaWorld Orlando
places.address: 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Your stomach lifts on Mako's airtime hills while below you orcas cut through blue water and sharks drift overhead in the tunnel. SeaWorld Orlando on I-Drive pairs a working marine park with some of Florida's most serious coasters, including Pipeline the surf coaster and family coaster Penguin Trek. Come for both sides of it — ride in the morning, slow down for the presentations after. Tourist Trail: Worth it — ride early, then watch the shows when the coaster lines peak.

places.name: Aquatica Orlando
places.address: 5800 Water Play Way, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: You shoot through a clear tube and Commerson's dolphins streak past beside you, then the current in Roa's Rapids pulls you faster than a lazy river should. Aquatica on I-Drive is SeaWorld's water park, built around slides through animal habitats, wave pools, and a wide sand beach. It works best as a hot-day reset — arrive with suits on, ride the big slides first, and claim shade early. Tourist Trail: Worth it — especially as the slower, cheaper break between theme park days.

places.name: Discovery Cove
places.address: 6000 Discovery Cove Way, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Warm sand stays between your toes while stingrays glide past in the Grand Reef and a dolphin pulls you through clear water. Discovery Cove on I-Drive is a reservation-only, capped-attendance day resort where the dolphin swim, lazy river, meals and drinks are all included. This is the calm splurge day in the middle of a trip — pick one date, book it early, and let everything else wait. Tourist Trail: Worth it — if you want one all-in day instead of another park line.

places.name: Gatorland
places.address: 14501 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: A gator launches out of the water for chicken at the Gator Jumparoo while handlers wrestle in the sand and white leucistic gators watch from the shade. Gatorland on Orange Blossom Trail has done this since 1949 — thousands of gators, a breeding marsh, and the Screamin' Gator Zip Line overhead. This is old Florida without polish — go early, wear shoes you can hose off, and give it a half day. Tourist Trail: Worth it — the one locals defend, zip line and all.

places.name: Medieval Times Dinner & Tournament
places.address: 4510 W Vine St, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: No forks, no problem — you tear into roasted chicken and tomato bisque with your hands while knights charge on horseback below your cheering section. Medieval Times in Kissimmee serves a four-course feast inside a castle arena where jousting decides the night. It lands best with kids and groups who will actually shout — pick your section, lean into the cheering, and eat as it comes. Tourist Trail: Worth it — the bisque and the jousting carry it, even if you have seen it once.

places.name: Pirates Dinner Adventure
places.address: 6400 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A full-size Spanish galleon rocks in an indoor lagoon while acrobats swing overhead, swords clash, and cannons flash around the tables. Pirates Dinner Adventure on Carrier Drive off I-Drive pairs a multi-course dinner with aerial stunts and a story aimed squarely at younger kids. Go in expecting loud and silly in the best way — sit close, cheer for your pirate, and let bedtime slide a little. Tourist Trail: Worth it for under-10s — older teens will feel they have outgrown it.

places.name: The Outta Control Magic Dinner Show
places.address: 9067 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Pizza keeps coming, the magician pulls a volunteer into the bit, and the room is laughing before the trick even lands. The Outta Control Magic Dinner Show inside WonderWorks on I-Drive includes unlimited pizza, salad, and dessert with high-energy magic and comedy built on audience participation. It is the low-effort night out — show up hungry, sit near the front if you want in, and pick the late show for the liveliest crowd. Tourist Trail: Worth it — the best value dinner show on I-Drive.

places.name: Boggy Creek Airboat Adventures
places.address: 2001 E Southport Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: Boggy Creek runs airboats out onto East Lake Tohopekaliga, and the ride is pure Florida: the boat skims across open water at speed, then slows into the marsh grass where the captain spots gators, turtles, and wading birds most visitors would never notice. The 30-minute and hour-long tours are the core, but the night tours, when the guides sweep spotlights across the water and the gator eyes light up red, are the ones people talk about for years. Arrive early for the Native American village and the gem-mining sluice if you have kids in tow.

places.name: Museum of Illusions Orlando
places.address: 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The Museum of Illusions at ICON Park is built for the camera roll: room after room of optical illusions, from the Ames room that shrinks your friends to the vortex tunnel that scrambles your balance. Staff are stationed at the big set pieces to take the exact photo that makes the illusion work, which saves every group from the usual awkward guessing. Plan about an hour, pair it with the Orlando Eye next door, and go on a weekday morning to dodge the school-group rush.

places.name: SEA LIFE Orlando Aquarium
places.address: 8449 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: SEA LIFE Orlando sits at ICON Park and does the aquarium greatest-hits in a compact, well-paced walkthrough: a 360-degree ocean tunnel with sharks and rays overhead, touch pools with starfish and anemones, and themed zones from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean. It is smaller than the big-city aquariums, which is exactly why it works as a 90-minute I-Drive stop rather than a full-day commitment. Combine it with Madame Tussauds next door for the bundle ticket.

places.name: The Escape Game Orlando
places.address: 8145 International Dr Ste 511, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The Escape Game on I-Drive runs the polished, big-budget end of escape rooms: cinematic sets, genuinely clever puzzles, and game guides who nudge without spoiling. The Heist and Prison Break rooms are the classics, and the multi-room layouts mean even groups of eight stay busy instead of standing around. Book the evening slots for date night or a group outing, and arrive a few minutes early for the briefing.

places.name: Merritt Island Bioluminescence Kayak Tours
places.address: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge, Merritt Island, FL
places.description: On summer nights, the lagoons around Merritt Island glow. Dinoflagellates in the water light up electric blue with every paddle stroke, and mullet darting under the kayak leave comet trails behind them. Local outfitters run guided clear-kayak tours after dark from roughly June through October, timed around the new moon for maximum glow. It is one of the most surreal things you can do within an hour of Orlando, and it books out fast in peak season.

places.name: Blue Spring Manatee Kayak Tours
places.address: Blue Spring State Park, 2100 W French Ave, Orange City, FL 32763
places.description: In winter, hundreds of manatees pile into the 72-degree spring run at Blue Spring State Park, and the guided kayak tours from Orange City put you right alongside them. The water is so clear you can watch the manatees roll and graze beneath the boat, and the guides know exactly where the herds gather on any given morning. Go November through March for the manatee season, book the earliest tour of the day, and remember the rule: look, do not touch.

places.name: Orlando Helicopter Tours
places.address: 8990 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The helicopter pads along I-Drive sell the one view you cannot get any other way: the theme parks, the Orlando Eye, and the whole tourist corridor laid out beneath you at sunset. Tours run from quick daytime loops over the parks to longer after-dark flights when the coasters are lit up. It is unapologetically a splurge, but for an anniversary or a first visit, the ten-minute version delivers the postcard.

places.name: Revolution Adventures
places.address: 4000 FL-33, Clermont, FL 34714
places.description: Revolution Adventures sits on 230 acres of purpose-built terrain in Clermont, about 30 minutes west of the parks, and it is the answer when the family needs a break from queues. The guided ATV and Mucky Duck amphibious-vehicle tours run through mud pits, wooded trails, and open fields, and you will get dirty no matter which vehicle you pick. Book the morning slot before the Florida heat settles in, and bring a change of clothes.

places.name: Polynesian Fire Luau
places.address: 4740 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: Drums roll as fire-knife performers spin light in the dark and dancers move from hula to fast Tahitian beats. The Polynesian Fire Luau in Kissimmee on the 192 corridor starts with a tropical buffet, then builds into a show with audience participation woven in. It is an easy evening for families who want dinner handled — eat first, settle in, and let the kids get pulled into the fun. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — book the show night, not another I-Drive dinner.

places.name: St. Augustine Day Trip
places.address: St. Augustine, FL 32084
places.description: St. Augustine, about two hours northeast, is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the continental US, and it wears the history well. The Castillo de San Marcos still guards the bay, St. George Street strings together colonial architecture with ice cream shops and pubs, and the beaches are a short drive over the Bridge of Lions. Go on a weekday to dodge the weekend crowds, and do the fort first before the afternoon heat.

places.name: Clearwater Beach Day Trip
places.address: Clearwater Beach, FL 33767
places.description: Clearwater Beach is the Gulf-coast answer to Orlando's theme-park days: powder-white sand, calm shallow water, and sunsets that draw a nightly crowd to Pier 60. The drive is about two hours each way, which makes it a legitimate day trip if you leave by eight. Pack the cooler, claim sand early near the pier for the facilities, and stay for the sunset celebration if you can stand the drive home after dark.

places.name: Universal Stella Nova Resort
places.address: Near Epic Universe, Orlando, FL
places.description: Stella Nova opened in January 2025 as one of the two new value-tier resorts serving Epic Universe, and it is the budget play for the new park. The space-themed design runs through the lobby and the 750 rooms, the pool deck is built for recovery days, and shuttle service runs to all the Universal parks. Rates stay well under the in-park Helios Grand, which makes it the practical base camp for a multi-day Epic Universe trip.

places.name: Universal Terra Luna Resort
places.address: Near Epic Universe, Orlando, FL
places.description: Terra Luna is Stella Nova's sister resort, opened March 2025 with the same value-tier brief: clean, modern rooms themed around exploration, a big resort pool, and quick shuttles to Epic Universe and the rest of Universal Orlando. The two resorts share the same DNA, so pick whichever has the better rate on your dates. Both beat the I-Drive chain hotels on location if Epic Universe is the reason for the trip.

places.name: B&B HOTEL Orlando International Drive
places.address: International Drive, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The B&B HOTEL on I-Drive, opened March 2026, is the European budget brand's second US property and its first fully renovated on-brand hotel stateside. Expect the formula that made the chain huge in Europe: compact, well-designed rooms, solid breakfast, honest pricing, and no resort-fee games. It is a smart pick for I-Drive visitors who plan to spend their days out, not in the room.

places.name: Villatel Orlando Resort
places.address: International Drive, Orlando, FL
places.description: Villatel, opened in 2026 on I-Drive, is built for the big-group trip: 270 themed villas sleeping four to nine bedrooms each, plus the Aqua Bay water park and the first US Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy. If you are traveling with extended family or two families splitting costs, the per-bedroom math beats booking a block of hotel rooms, and everyone still gets the resort pool scene. Book the villas, not the apartments, for the full themed experience.

places.name: Nikitta
places.address: 8255 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Nikitta, opened June 2025 on I-Drive, is Orlando's first serious Nikkei restaurant, fusing Peruvian ingredients with Japanese technique. The tiraditos and acevichados are the move, and the lomo saltado reimagined through a Tokyo lens shows what the kitchen is really after. It is already a date-night flagship for the corridor, so reserve on OpenTable and do not walk in on a Friday expecting a table.

places.name: Zama
places.address: 1120 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Zama opened in late 2025 in Mills 50 from Agave Azul's Juan Rios, and it cooks Mexican food over live fire with a seafood lean. The menu moves between wood-fired fish, ember-roasted vegetables, and the kind of tacos that remind you how good a tortilla can be, backed by a serious tequila and mezcal program. It slots right into the Mills 50 restaurant row as the special-occasion Mexican spot.

places.name: Zukku-San Sushi Bar & Grill
places.address: Pointe Orlando, 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Zukku-San, the Tampa-born sushi bar that opened at Pointe Orlando in April 2026, brings the Majestic Restaurant Group's polished take on sushi and robata grill to I-Drive. The sushi program is the draw, but the grilled skewers and small plates make it work for a mixed group where not everyone wants raw fish. It is a strong pre-show dinner option given the Pointe's theaters and the I-Drive nightlife a short walk away.

places.name: Zaza Cuban Comfort Food
places.address: 1621 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Zaza Cuban Comfort Food's Hospital Row location, opened mid-2026, extends the local chainlet's formula: cafecito that actually wakes you up, medianoche sandwiches pressed to order, and daily specials like ropa vieja over rice that taste like someone's grandmother is still running the kitchen. It is a counter-service diner, not a white-tablecloth spot, and the prices reflect that. The morning crowd is hospital staff and regulars, which tells you everything.

places.name: Reeves Sports Bar
places.address: 50 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Reeves Sports Bar opened in September 2026 on Central Boulevard from the Thriving Hospitality group, and it aims higher than the typical sports bar menu. The kitchen runs a chef-driven take on bar food, the screens are everywhere without overwhelming the room, and the downtown location makes it the natural pre-game for events at the Kia Center. Come for a Magic or Orlando City watch party, stay because the wings are better than they needed to be.

places.name: Pig Floyd's x Pigzza
places.address: 1050 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Two Mills 50 institutions merged in September 2026: Pig Floyd's urban BBQ and Pigzza's pizza and pasta now share one roof at 1050 N Mills. The menu lets you order brisket and a wood-fired pizza at the same table, which solves the group-dinner argument before it starts. It is loud, casual, and unapologetically indulgent, exactly what the neighborhood wanted from the pairing.

places.name: Mills Market
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Mills Market is the food hall that turned the old Colonial Plaza stretch into Mills 50's culinary anchor, with stalls like Banh Mi Boy, Kai Kai BBQ and Dumplings, and UniGirl drawing lines that spill onto the patio. The vendor mix leans Asian and chef-driven, and the shared seating makes it the easiest group dinner in the district when nobody can agree. Go hungry, order across three stalls, and thank the food-hall format for making it possible.

places.name: O-Town West
places.address: Near Epic Universe, Orlando, FL
places.description: O-Town West is the emerging mixed-use district rising around Epic Universe, and it is where the area's next wave of restaurants is landing. With 2025-26 openings like Kappo Tsan setting the tone, the district is positioning itself as the food-and-stay corridor for Epic Universe visitors who want something beyond the parks. Still early, but the trajectory is clear: watch this grid.

places.name: Disney Starlight: Dream the Night Away
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Disney Starlight, which debuted in July 2025, is Magic Kingdom's first new daily nighttime parade since 2016, and it was built for the drone-and-projection era. The floats blend classic characters with newer favorites, the soundtrack is engineered to stick in your head for days, and the route down Main Street USA still delivers the moment the castle lights up behind the final float. Stake out a spot on Main Street at least 45 minutes early, because everyone else has the same idea.

places.name: Test Track 3.0
places.address: EPCOT, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Test Track reopened in July 2025 as version 3.0, a retro-futuristic overhaul that trades the old crash-test theme for a sleek celebration of automotive design through the decades. The ride system is the same beloved high-speed loop, including the 65-mph outdoor sprint, but the show scenes and queue now tell a much richer story. It remains EPCOT's headliner thrill ride, so use the morning or the single-rider line.

places.name: GEO-82
places.address: EPCOT, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: GEO-82, opened June 2025 inside Spaceship Earth, is EPCOT's first adults-only lounge, and the setting is the draw: cocktails served inside the park's icon with a mid-century space-age design. The drinks program leans classic with a few geodesic-themed signatures, and the 21-and-over policy keeps it calm even on the busiest festival days. Reservations open ahead of time and go fast; this is the EPCOT date-night move.

places.name: The Beak and Barrel
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: The Beak and Barrel, opened August 2025 in Adventureland, is the standalone Pirates of the Caribbean tavern Magic Kingdom fans waited decades for. The interior is dense with pirate lore and Audio-Animatronic touches, the menu runs to themed cocktails and shareable bites, and the whole thing feels like stepping into the ride's world with a drink in hand. Walk-up waits get long by midday, so try it early or during the fireworks when the land empties.

places.name: Zootopia: Better Zoogether!
places.address: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Zootopia: Better Zoogether!, which opened in November 2025 inside the Tree of Life, replaces the long-running It's Tough to Be a Bug with a 4D Zootopia show. Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde host a celebration of the animal kingdom's biomes, with the in-theater effects doing the heavy lifting. It is the rare Animal Kingdom addition that plays to all ages, and the Tree of Life theater means you are getting the show plus the park's most photographed icon in one stop.

places.name: Disney Villains: Unfairly Ever After
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Unfairly Ever After, which debuted in May 2025 at Hollywood Studios, finally gives the villains their own stage show, and it commits to the bit. The production leans into the villains' grievances with Broadway-scale staging, and the audience is encouraged to pick sides. It is the strongest new stage show at the Studios in years, and the indoor theater makes it a strategic midday break from the Florida sun.

places.name: The Little Mermaid: A Musical Adventure
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: The Little Mermaid: A Musical Adventure opened in May 2025 at Hollywood Studios, replacing the Voyage of the Little Mermaid show that ran for decades. The new production retells Ariel's story with updated puppetry, projection work, and the songs everyone already knows by heart. It is built for families with young kids, runs multiple times daily, and the theater's air conditioning is a feature, not a footnote.

places.name: Soarin' Across America
places.address: EPCOT, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Soarin' Across America, which debuted in May 2026, swaps the ride's usual world tour for a 250th-anniversary flight over the United States. The hang-glider simulator still delivers the signature sensations, the scents and wind doing half the storytelling, but the new film is the reason to ride it again. Expect it to draw the longest EPCOT lines through the anniversary year.

places.name: Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring the Muppets
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: In May 2026 the Rock 'n' Roller Coaster got its biggest change since opening: the Electric Mayhem band took over the storyline, turning the super-stretch limo ride into a Muppets-helmed dash across Hollywood. The coaster itself is unchanged, still launching 0 to 57 in under three seconds, with inversions in the dark, but the new pre-show and soundtrack give longtime riders a reason to queue again. Single rider remains the fastest way on.

places.name: Big Thunder Mountain Railroad
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Big Thunder Mountain reopened in May 2026 after a full refurbishment, and the wildest ride in the wilderness is running better than it has in years. The project replaced the track, added a new Rainbow Caverns scene, and refreshed the animatronics throughout the mining town. It is still the perfect first big coaster for kids graduating from the Barnstormer, and the refurbished version rewards a re-ride even if you have done it a hundred times.

places.name: Expedition Odyssey: Fire & Ice
places.address: SeaWorld Orlando, 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: SeaWorld's Arctic flying theater, opened in 2025: a Soarin-style ride that lifts you over polar landscapes filmed with the real animals — belugas, orcas, and walruses moving through ice water below the screen. The flight footage is the draw, and the conservation thread running through it is the park's signature move. For families it works best early, as the anchor ride of the morning before the coaster lines build and the Florida heat settles over the park.

places.name: SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep
places.address: SeaWorld Orlando, 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: SEAQuest: Legends of the Deep opens spring 2026 at SeaWorld as the park's first suspended dark ride, carrying riders through an underwater legend in a new expanded area of the park. As a weatherproof, family-friendly ride, it fills the biggest gap in SeaWorld's lineup: something everyone can do together when the afternoon storms roll in. Check the park's site for the exact opening date before planning around it.

places.name: LEGO Galaxy + Galacticoaster
places.address: LEGOLAND Florida Resort, 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: LEGO Galaxy, which opened in February 2026 at LEGOLAND Florida, is the park's new space-themed land anchored by the Galacticoaster, its first indoor launch coaster. The 36-inch height requirement makes it a genuine first-coaster milestone for young kids, and the indoor queue is merciful in the summer heat. It gives families with small children one more reason to make the Winter Haven day trip.

places.name: SEA LIFE Florida
places.address: LEGOLAND Florida Resort, 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: SEA LIFE Florida opened in June 2025 inside LEGOLAND Florida Resort, and it is now included with park admission, which changes the value math of a LEGOLAND day. The aquarium holds more than 3,000 creatures across 150 species, with a 180-degree ocean tunnel and a 'Theme Park Under the Sea' concept built for kids. Plan it as the midday air-conditioned break between the outdoor rides.

places.address: 201 E Pine St #101, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: This family-run downtown cafe does the morning routine properly: crackly tartines, buttery biscuits, and chocolate cookies that locals order by the box for catering. The drinks carry the same care, from the sea salt caramel latte to the white chocolate lavender number. Note the hours before you go: weekdays 8 to 3 only, right inside the PNC building on Pine.

The patio is pet-friendly and the bar pours frozen sangria alongside a solid craft cocktail list. It doubles as a game-day hang, with cornhole and trivia leagues running through the week.

Go sweet gochujang or spicy honey on the wings, and do not skip the kimchi fries, which stay crunchy all the way to the last bite. It is a laid-back little counter on Mills with bulgogi bowls and loaded waffle fries too, and the staff moves fast even at the lunch rush.

places.address: 1412 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Chef Brandi's all-day Creole stall in City Food Hall is Black, women, and LGBTQ owned, and it cooks like it has something to prove. The chicken and croffles (yes, a croissant crossed with a waffle, dripping hot honey) are the move, but the gumbo ramen and the loaded Bourbon Street po'boy deserve your attention too. Rich, soulful, and seasoned with confidence: this is NOLA comfort that actually tastes like the Crescent City. The vibe is warm and the music never misses.

Save room for the churros stuffed with dulce de leche, and a mangonada smoothie if you want the full experience. Fast, friendly, and priced like a taco shop should be.

places.description: Egg Dose calls itself Orlando's best breakfast spot and honestly the line at its City Food Hall stall (number 9) suggests they might be right. The Maple Dose is the legend: brioche French toast as the bun, thick-cut bacon, soft-scrambled eggs, cheddar, and a side of real maple syrup for dunking. The picanha steak sandwich is the sleeper pick, and every sandwich is built fresh that morning. Catch them here daily from 8 to 3, or at the Lake Eola and Winter Garden farmers markets on weekends.

The bagels come with house-made schmears that range from classic to playful (lucky charms cream cheese exists, and it works), plus deli-inspired breakfast sandwiches for a bigger bite. This is the spot when you want a bagel that actually tastes like a bagel: crisp crust, dense crumb, no shortcuts.

The patties get a proper crust from the flat-top, the dunk sauce is dangerously good on everything, and the picanha steak fries nod to the owners' Brazilian roots. This City Food Hall stall is the newest outpost of the brand that started at 2207 E Michigan St, so the playbook is already proven. Get the onion hoops if you know what is good for you.

places.description: Yakuza is a Japanese-Mexican fusion sushi counter with a food-truck past, and it plays with flavors most Orlando sushi spots will not touch. The Black Panther roll and the dragon tempura rolls get the love, but the playful side is the real draw: sushi push pops, sushi burritos, and buildable poke bowls alongside shrimp ceviche and tostones yaku. Big rolls, bold sauces, zero pretension. It is the fun order when the group cannot agree on dinner.

places.description: This little Mills 50 coffee house runs on pay-what-you-can generosity and genuinely excellent espresso. The Sunflower and Spice Mocha and the vegan lemon rosemary bread have a small but devoted following, and the matcha latte is the real kind, forward and unsweetened, like the ones you get in Japan. It started as the mobile Vita Luna cart and grew into a true community hub with free Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, and dogs welcome, which is exactly the kind of place Orlando's local scene is built on.

places.description: The line moves, a wand chooses someone up front, and butterbeer foam ends up on a kid who swore he was too old for this. These are Universal Orlando Resort tickets from $143, covering the original parks plus Epic Universe, the new park that opened in 2025. For a family, the real choice is park-to-park or one park per day. Decide that before you buy, not at the gate. Tourist Trail: Worth it — especially if Epic Universe is the reason you came.

places.name: Universal 2-Park 1-Day VIP Experience
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: You walk past a posted wait, follow your guide through a staff door, and are seated before most guests have found the queue entrance. This is the Universal 2-Park 1-Day VIP Experience, $319, a guided group day across both original parks with rides prioritized for you. For a splurge, it buys back hours, not just comfort. If you only have one day, check this date first. Tourist Trail: Worth it for a one-day trip when time matters more than budget.

places.name: SeaWorld Howl-O-Scream
places.address: 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Fog sits low over the midway, a scare actor drags something metal in the dark, and a coaster leaves the station half-screaming already. Howl-O-Scream is SeaWorld's separate-ticket nighttime Halloween event, with scare zones, haunted houses, and coasters running after dark, priced by date. For teens and adults, it is a different park than the daytime one. Pick a night and leave the daytime ticket separate. Tourist Trail: Worth it in October — skip it if jump scares are not your thing.

places.name: CoCo Key Water Park
places.address: 7400 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A toddler goes down the same small slide nine times, an older brother disappears into the arcade, and nobody asks about the beach again. CoCo Key is a hotel water park on International Drive with slides and an arcade, and day passes start at $33 with no resort stay needed. For families with younger kids, it fills a half day easily. Buy it for your low-energy day. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — use it as a reset day between theme parks.

places.name: Hilton Orlando Pool Pass
places.address: 6001 Destination Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: You drift the lazy river under a palm, hear a waterslide splash behind you, and for once there is no park crowd to get back to. This is a day pass to the Hilton Orlando pool on Destination Parkway, with a lazy river and waterslide, without booking a room. For a visitor, it is a resort day kept simple. Reserve it for a non-park day. Tourist Trail: Worth it if a quiet pool day is the point of the day.

places.name: Omni Orlando Resort Pool Pass
places.address: 1500 Masters Blvd, ChampionsGate, FL 33896
places.description: Two friends float the lazy river while the kids race the slides and the adults-only pool stays calm around the corner. This is a pool day pass at the Omni Orlando Resort at ChampionsGate, with a lazy river, slides, and an adults-only pool, no overnight stay required. For a group split between relaxing and playing, everyone gets their version of the day. Book it for a full, rested day. Tourist Trail: Worth it — ChampionsGate is a drive, so stay the whole day.

places.name: The Grove Resort Water Park Day Pass
places.address: 14501 Grove Resort Ave, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: A surf simulator throws up a sheet of white water, the lazy river loops past, and lunch arrives without anyone changing out of swim clothes. The Grove Resort in Winter Garden opens its Surfari water park to day guests, with passes from $82 including the lazy river. For families in a rental nearby, it is a water park day without a theme park ticket. Choose your date early on weekends. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — Winter Garden families use this over I-Drive.

places.name: Go City Explorer Pass
places.address: Multiple attractions across Orlando
places.description: One family picks a science center and a boat tour, another picks mini golf and a museum, and both used the same pass. The Go City Explorer Pass lets you choose two to five Orlando attractions from a set list and visit them at your own pace. For flexible planners, it beats buying each ticket alone. List your must-dos first, then pick the pass size that covers them. Tourist Trail: Worth it only if at least three picks are already on your list.

places.name: Orlando Essentials Pass
places.address: Multiple attractions across Orlando
places.description: You scan once, ride something tall in the morning, and by the second stop the math on the bundle starts to make sense. The Orlando Essentials Pass bundles three top attractions for $139, sold as one pass instead of three separate tickets. For a first-time visitor with limited days, it narrows choices to the headline stops. Line up your three before you travel. Tourist Trail: Worth it for a short first trip — locals and repeat visitors can skip it.

places.name: All-Inclusive Pass with Kennedy Space Center
places.address: Multiple attractions across Orlando + Kennedy Space Center
places.description: A Saturn V rocket fills the hall above you, and later that week the same pass gets you through a gate back in Orlando. This all-inclusive pass, $239, is anchored by Kennedy Space Center and includes other attractions you can work in around it. For space fans, KSC is the day you plan around. Put Kennedy on your calendar first, then fill the other days from the pass. Tourist Trail: Worth it — treat Kennedy Space Center as a full day, not a half-day stop.

places.name: Drawn to Life — Cirque du Soleil
places.address: 1478 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: An animator's pencil sketch lifts off the page, an acrobat turns it into a leap, and the whole theater goes quiet before the landing. Drawn to Life at Disney Springs is the Cirque du Soleil show built around Disney animation drawings, with tickets from $90. For couples and older kids, it is a date night that needs no park ticket. Choose an evening you are already at Disney Springs. Tourist Trail: Worth it — make dinner at Disney Springs part of the night.

places.name: Speakeasy Murder Mystery Dinner Show
places.address: 6400 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A singer in fringe takes your drink order, a guest at the next table is accused, and your table starts comparing notes over dessert. This speakeasy murder mystery dinner show near International Drive, $94, sets a 1920s crime for the audience to solve with dinner included. For adults, it is a night out with a game built in. Book it instead of another park dinner. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — go with a group that will play along.

places.name: Downtown Food Tour
places.address: Downtown Orlando (meeting point confirmed at booking)
places.description: You start with a plate you would never have ordered, cross a street you have driven past for years, and end up with three new regular spots. This downtown Orlando food tour serves five local dishes in the part of downtown locals actually eat in, for $94. For food people, it replaces a week of guessing with one afternoon of tasting. Wear walking shoes and come hungry on the day you book.

places.name: Milk District Eats Food Tour
places.address: E Robinson St, Milk District, Orlando, FL (meets in front of the Milkhouse)
places.description: A dairy sign still marks the corner, someone is carrying a bakery box, and every stop is a small room with a regulars' table. Milk District Eats is a five-stop walking food tour through the dairy-named district east of downtown, built around independent spots. For visitors who want Orlando beyond the attractions, this is the neighborhood version. Book it for a late morning and leave room between stops.

places.name: Ivanhoe Village Food Tour
places.address: 1211 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Vintage shop windows, a lake at the end of the street, and a tasting waiting two doors down is the rhythm of the walk here. This Ivanhoe Village food tour, $90, pairs tastings with a lakefront vintage district of small shops and cafes. For a couple or a small group, it is an easy half day that mixes eating with browsing. Reserve your date and wander the shops a little longer afterward.

places.name: Brews and Bites Walking Tour
places.address: Ten10 Brewing Company, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The brewer pulls a small pour, explains what changed in this batch, and a plate arrives that was clearly chosen to go with it. Brews and Bites is a walking tour of breweries and bars with food paired along the way, around $94, in small groups. For craft beer people, it is a guided first round through a scene that takes time to map alone. Pick an evening and plan a ride home.

places.name: Fettuccine Pasta-Making Class
places.address: Goblin Studios, 805 W Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Flour on your hands, a sheet of dough thinning under the rolling pin, and your own uneven ribbons laid out in a small, proud pile. In this fettuccine-making class with a local chef, $75, you make the pasta by hand and then sit down to eat what you made. For a home cook, it is a skill you will reuse, not just a meal. Book a session and bring an appetite for your own work.

places.name: Ramen-Making Class
places.address: Orlando, FL (address confirmed at booking)
places.description: Steam clouds the pot, noodles go in for less time than you expected, and the broth you seasoned yourself finally tastes like a bowl, not an attempt. This ramen-making class from scratch with a local chef, $68, covers broth and noodles and ends with the bowl you built. For anyone who orders ramen often, it changes how you taste the next one. Choose a class date and arrive ready to work standing up.

places.name: Beginner Sushi-Making Class
places.address: Ten10 Brewing Company, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Your first roll leans, the second holds, and someone at your table trades a piece for a sip of the pint in front of you. This beginner sushi-making class at a local brewery, $75, teaches rolls step by step in a relaxed brewery setting made for first-timers. For a date or friends' night, the low stakes are the point. Reserve your spots together so you share a table.

places.name: Moonshine Mixology Class
places.address: 8200 Vineland Ave, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Ice cracks in a shaker, a tasting flight lines the bar in small glasses, and the instructor tells you to taste before you mix anything. This moonshine mixology class at Caribbean Moonshine on Vineland Avenue, $40, has you craft two cocktails alongside a tasting flight of island rums, for guests 21 and over. For cocktail people, it is a working lesson, not a lecture. Book it for early evening. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — small class, so reserve ahead.

places.name: Caribbean Moonshine Distillery Tour
places.address: 8200 Vineland Ave, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Copper catches the light, a mash scent hangs sweet in the room, and the pour at the end tastes different once you have seen where it rested. This distillery tour and tasting at Caribbean Moonshine, 8200 Vineland Avenue, $40, walks through a small-batch, island-style distillery and finishes at the tasting bar. For rum drinkers, it is a short stop near the outlets. Add it to a Vineland afternoon. Tourist Trail: Worth it paired with Vineland shopping — too short to anchor a day.

places.name: Premium Caribbean Moonshine Bottling Tour
places.address: 8200 Vineland Ave, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: You stand bottle-side while a small batch is finished, hear how this run differed from the last, and taste with that detail still on your tongue. This premium bottling tour and tasting at Caribbean Moonshine, $70, is the deeper version of the standard tour, closer to the bottling work itself. For craft spirits fans, the extra detail is the upgrade. If you pick one distillery experience, make it this one. Tourist Trail: Worth it for spirits fans — casual drinkers should take the standard tour.

places.name: Hard Rock Cafe Orlando
places.address: 6050 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A guitar hangs over your table, a stage glows next door at Hard Rock Live, and your server points out a jacket worn on an actual tour. Hard Rock Cafe Orlando at Universal CityWalk is the world's largest Hard Rock Cafe; this product covers a set meal with gratuity included. For music fans, lunch doubles as a memorabilia walk. Plan it for a CityWalk day. Tourist Trail: Do it like a local — go for the collection, before or after a show next door.

places.name: Orlando Magic Pregame Warmups & Dining Experience
places.address: 400 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: You hear sneakers squeak and balls bounce in an almost empty arena, close enough to see shooting routines instead of just warmup highlights. This Orlando Magic pregame experience at Kia Center, $265, combines courtside warmups access with dining before tip-off. For real basketball fans, that time on the floor is the part money normally cannot buy. Book it for a home game you already planned to attend. Tourist Trail: Worth it for Magic fans — skip it if you only care about the game itself.
